On a wooden board, on bones, on stones, on palm fronds, as was the case at the beginning. But paper is more durable, softer, and easier.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: these deniers will not believe even if every sign came to them, because among the greatest signs is that the scripture descends, they see it on paper and touch it, and then they deny. This is explained by the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has come into effect will not believe, even if every sign should come to them﴾ [Yunus 96-97], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And signs and warnings do not avail a people who do not believe﴾ [Yunus 101], and the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And there had certainly come to them of the news that which contains a deterrent, far-reaching wisdom, but warnings do not avail, so turn away from them﴾ [Al-Qamar 4-6].

And here be attentive: pause at ﴿so turn away from them﴾ and do not connect, for if you connect the meaning is spoiled; the meaning becomes ﴿so turn away from them﴾ when? ﴿The day the caller calls to a terrible thing﴾. This is one.

In the verse after it: ﴿So they denied Our servant and said, "Mad!"﴾ [Al-Qamar 9], pause, do not connect; for if you connect: ﴿and they said, "Mad!" and was driven away,﴾ the phrase ﴿and was driven away﴾ would become part of their saying, which is not the case. Rather ﴿and was driven away﴾ is conjoined to ﴿they said﴾, meaning: they said, "Mad," and they drove him away.

Such matters, brothers, one must indeed be attentive to, because the noble Qur'an is not like the speech that we write or say. We try to make our speech follow one pattern, but in the Qur'an, glory be to Allah, and this is part of its inimitability, you sometimes see a word with no connection to the next, in order that the addressee or reader may attend, reflect, and ponder. This is a point that many people do not sense; you find him reading in a mere flowing manner without attending to the pauses.

We learned this from our shaykh 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Nasir al-Sa'di, may Allah have mercy on him. He used to lead us in taraweeh and qiyam in Ramadan, and he would stop at the proper pauses, so we would marvel how this was! Previously we would recite the Qur'an in a flowing manner and not heed the meaning. Even His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So woe to those who pray, who are heedless of their prayer﴾ [Al-Ma'un 4-5]: do you pause at ﴿so woe to those who pray﴾? You pause, because Allah made it a place of pause. If you say, glory be to Allah, "So woe to those who pray," how?! The atheist poet said:

"Your Lord did not say, 'Woe to the drunken ones,' but your Lord said, 'Woe to those who pray.'"

We say: yes, he said it, but he is an atheist; he did not read the next verse. Pausing at ﴿so woe to those who pray﴾ has a benefit that may not appear to some people, because when the listener hears the reader say ﴿so woe to those who pray﴾ and pause, you find him confused: "How, ﴿so woe to those who pray﴾?" Then the next words come: ﴿who are heedless of their prayer﴾, and it is as if rain has fallen on dry land. This is the secret of why it is better to follow the verses when possible: pause at every verse even if what follows is connected to it.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: it is appropriate to use the noun in place of the pronoun when the need arises, due to His saying ﴿those who disbelieve would have said﴾. This occurs frequently in the Qur'an in several verses, like the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿Whoever is an enemy to Allah and His angels and His messengers and Jibril and Mika'il – then indeed Allah is an enemy to the disbelievers﴾ [Al-Baqarah 98]. He did not say "an enemy to Him," although the verse ﴿indeed Allah is an enemy to the disbelievers﴾ has a third consideration, which is observing the verse endings. So observe how the noun was placed in the position of the pronoun.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the obstinacy of those polytheists who deny the Prophet (ﷺ) by turning the truth into falsehood. The truth is that it is the Qur'an from Allah, and they turn it into magic. Is this magic in the eloquence of the Qur'an, its fluency, and its clarity, or in that it came as a scripture sent down from heaven, which deceived their sight? Apparently it includes both: they say, "This is not the reality, O Muhammad; our magicians bewitched us," or they say that because of its clarity and eloquence it bewitched them. Whichever it is, the denier, and Allah forbid, clings to everything.

* A student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Yes, pause: ﴿And they said, "We hear and we obey"﴾ [Al-Baqarah 285], pause; it differs if you say: ﴿And they said, "We hear and we obey, Your forgiveness"﴾ [Al-Baqarah 285], then you become one who hears and obeys Allah's forgiveness, which is not the case.

* A student: During recitation, whether reciting a hizb very quickly or during listening recitation, should a person observe these pauses?

* The Shaykh: Yes, one should observe this and pause, even if it is hurried.

* A student: May Allah reward you well. In the Mushaf's orthography, you find that in some cases they write at the beginning of verses rather than at the end of the verse, though the place is a pause...

* The Shaykh: No, this is from the copyists; it is not transmitted.

* A student: May Allah bless you. A man who is bewitched was approached by a man who does not know whether he is a sorcerer or not, who said to him: "I will tell you the location of the magic." Should he deal with him? If he deals with him, does he enter into...

* The Shaykh: This is called among the scholars "undoing magic with magic." Shaykh al-Islam Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Wahhab, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned in his book Kitab al-Tawhid, relating from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib that there is no harm in it, and he said: "They only intend reform. As for what is beneficial, he did not forbid it." Perhaps he took it from the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿And they learned what harms them and does not benefit them﴾ [Al-Baqarah 102], and from His saying: ﴿And they could not harm anyone thereby except by permission of Allah﴾ [Al-Baqarah 102]. But this should not be issued to people as a general fatwa in this way, because one fears first: the deception of sorcerers; second: their multiplication, betrayal, and deceit, so one says to another: "Bewitch so-and-so and I will (...)," and they consume people's wealth falsely; third: that a sorcerer does not undo magic except by learning magic. Therefore it is not appropriate to open the door for people on this great matter, and they would be at the door of (...).

* * *
* A student: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan the accursed: ﴿And they said, "Why was an angel not sent down to him?" And if We had sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided, and they would not be reprieved. And if We had made him an angel, We would have made him a man and obscured for them what they obscure. And mockery has been made of messengers before you, but those who mocked them were encompassed by what they used to mock﴾ [Al-An'am 8-10].

* The Shaykh: Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿And even if We had sent down to you a written scripture on paper, and they had touched it with their hands, those who disbelieve would have said, "This is not but obvious magic."﴾

* From its benefits: Allah's knowledge of what would be if it were, since He knew what these people would say if a scripture were sent down to them on paper.

* And among them: the confirmation of the known through the perceptible, or, if you wish, the intellectual through the perceptible, by His saying ﴿on paper﴾ and His saying ﴿touched it﴾, since this is an affirmation of something perceptible that is seen to be on paper and touched by the hand.

* Among the benefits of this verse: that these are disbelievers, by His saying ﴿those who disbelieve would have said, "This is not but obvious magic."﴾ The context required that He say "they would have said," but He used the noun in place of the pronoun, and this has benefits: first, passing a ruling on the referent of the pronoun by what the apparent description requires. What is the apparent description here? ﴿Those who disbelieve﴾. The referent, if it were a pronoun, would be "those deniers."

The second benefit: analogy, meaning that everyone who says their saying is a disbeliever, since if He had said "they would have said," we would not have learned from the text that whoever says a saying like theirs is a disbeliever. When this description is apparent, we extend by analogy to everything similar to it, or everything characterized by this description.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that magic has an effect. Does the effect occur by reversing realities, or by imagining things to the senses? The answer: the second, since it does not reverse realities. The staffs and ropes that Pharaoh's magicians threw did not turn into snakes, but it was imagined to the onlookers that they were snakes, while in reality they remained staffs and ropes.

By this we reconcile the saying of one who says it has no effect and the saying of one who says it has effect: as for its effect by reversing realities, this is impossible, since none is able to do that except Allah, mighty and majestic. As for its effect by imagination, this is possible, since imagination in reality is a disorder of perception, and disorder results from magic, since sorcerers also sometimes bewitch a person so that he becomes ill, or his mind is disturbed, or the like.

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And they say, "Why was an angel not sent down to him?"﴾ ﴿They say﴾, meaning: those who denied the Prophet (ﷺ).

﴿Why was an angel not sent down to him?﴾ That is: why was an angel not sent down to him, so that it would confirm him? This demand is one of obstinacy, for the Prophet (ﷺ) had already brought clear signs. And there is no greater sign than when they asked for a sign and he showed them the splitting of the moon, and the moon was split into two halves[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3636) and Muslim (2800 / 43), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud.]], and they witnessed it. This is a change in the celestial spheres, so it is among the greatest of signs. But their statement here is from the category of obstinacy, challenge and disbelief in the miracle.

﴿Why was an angel not sent down to him?﴾ An angel (malak) is one of the angels.

﴿And if We had sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided, and then they would not be reprieved.﴾ That is: if We had sent down an angel, the affair would have ended with the descent of punishment upon them. For when previous nations demanded a specific sign, and were given the specific sign they requested, and then did not believe, they were seized with punishment without delay. Quraysh were not seized by the sign of the splitting of the moon, because they did not request that specific sign; rather they said: "O Muhammad, show us a sign," and he showed them the splitting of the moon. So said the scholars. However, when the deniers of the messengers demand a specific sign, and it comes and they do not believe, punishment descends upon them.

And His words ﴿the matter would have been decided﴾ mean: the affair of these people would have been settled, namely by their destruction.

﴿Then they would not be reprieved﴾ means: they would not be given respite, but would be hastened to punishment, and we seek refuge in Allah.

﴿And if We had made him an angel﴾ means: if We had made the Messenger an angel, ﴿We would have made him a man﴾. Even if it were supposed that We had made him an angel, We would necessarily have made him a human being, because an angel does not suit mankind. This is why Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said in Surat al-Isra': ﴿Say: "If there had been in the earth angels walking securely, We would have sent down to them from the heaven an angel as a messenger."﴾ [al-Isra' 95]. But there are only humans on earth, and it is not possible for Us to send angels to them, because that would not be fitting.

﴿If We had made him an angel, We would have made him a man﴾, and then the confusion would remain. This is why He said: ﴿And We would have confused them as they now confuse themselves﴾, that is: We would have mixed up the matter for them just as they mixed it up for themselves.

We benefit from this verse in several ways. Among them: the obstinacy of those who deny the messengers, and their demand for signs, even though the signs were already present, but they are obstinate.

Among them: they believe in angels, I mean those who deny the Prophet (ﷺ); as shown by His words: ﴿Why was an angel not sent down to him?﴾

Among them: they know that the angels are in the heavens, that being their abode and dwelling place. The evidence: ﴿Why was an angel not sent down to him?﴾

Among them, that is, among the benefits of this verse: that an angel is one of the signs of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, when it descends in support of mankind, since they themselves acknowledged that it is a sign indicating the truthfulness of the Prophet (ﷺ).

Among them: that Allah, Glorified and Exalted, responds to the obstinate with the same thing they were obstinate about, and warns them against demanding signs; as shown by His words: ﴿And if We had sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided﴾.

Among them: what we have pointed out, that when the deniers of the messengers demand a specific sign and do not believe, punishment is hastened upon them.

Among the benefits of the second verse: that if Allah wished to send down an angel, He would not send it down in its angelic form, but would make it—what?—a man. Why? For the sake of suitability, the fitness between the messengers and those to whom they are sent.

Among them: the wisdom of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, in sending messengers from among humans, so that people may rely on them and accept them. Moreover, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, makes the messengers come from the middle and noble, the distinguished and excellent of their peoples, so that they may be protected by them. This is not harmful: that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, should give the messengers someone to protect them from their peoples. The statement of the people of Shu'ayb to him supports this: ﴿And were it not for your clan, we would have stoned you﴾ [Hud 91], which indicates that when a person is of the people, he gains great standing and dignity. The opposite is shown by the statement of Lut, peace be upon him: ﴿If only I had strength against you, or could take refuge in a strong pillar﴾ [Hud 80], that is, in a people who would be a support for me.

Why? Because of the lack of suitability between the Messenger and those to whom he is sent. So if he were a man, the confusion and the demand they made would return; as shown by His words: ﴿And We would have confused them as they now confuse themselves﴾.

﴿Why was an angel not sent down to him?﴾ That is: why was an angel not sent down to him, so that it would confirm him? Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Karim) on surah 6, verse 10:

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And messengers before you were certainly mocked﴾. The *lam* (ل) here is the introductory *lam* (*lam al-muwatta'a*, the particle that introduces an oath) and it reinforces the oath. The *qad* (قد) is for emphasis (*tahqiq*). This occurs frequently in the Qur'an. On this basis, the sentence is emphasized by three emphatics: an implied oath, the second being the *lam*, and the third being *qad*.

﴿Was mocked﴾ means: was ridiculed (*suhira*). The evidence is His saying: ﴿So there befell those who mocked them what they used to mock﴾, they mocked them and said: "This is a man, ﴿who speaks of your gods?﴾ [al-Anbiya 36]. ﴿Every time a company of his people passed by him, they mocked him. He said: If you mock us, indeed we mock you as you mock﴾ [Hud 38].

His saying: ﴿messengers﴾ is an indefinite noun (*nakirah*) in an affirmative context, and it does not indicate generality; that is, it does not indicate that all the messengers were mocked, but rather some messengers.

Know that an indefinite noun in an affirmative context does not indicate generality unless there is evidence for it, in which case it does indicate generality, such as the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿A soul will know what it has put forward and what it has left behind﴾ [al-Infitar 5], and ﴿A soul will know what it has brought﴾ [al-Takwir 14]. Here ﴿soul﴾ is an indefinite noun in an affirmative context, yet it is general, since the meaning of the verse is: every soul will know.

﴿Messengers before you﴾ means: in time.

﴿So there befell those who mocked them﴾ means: there descended upon them.

﴿What they used to mock﴾ means: the punishment of what they used to mock, or the recompense for what they used to mock. Allah expressed the recompense with the same verb to point to its cause in one respect, and to make known that the recompense is according to the deed in another respect. The punishment's cause is the deed by which the doer deserved to be punished, so the same deed that is the cause is applied to the punishment itself.

Second: If a person is recompensed for his deed, the same deed, this means that the recompense or punishment is proportionate to the deed: ﴿what they used to mock﴾.

* The noble verse contains benefits, among them: the emphasis of the sentence with various emphatics.

If someone says: Is not the report of Allah true, whether or not it is accompanied by an oath and emphatic particles?

The answer: Yes, but the noble Qur'an came in the Arabic tongue, and in the Arabic tongue emphasis is fitting when the situation calls for it. Otherwise, it is well known that when Allah reports a matter, even without emphasis, it is true and genuine, just as we observe the sun. But the Qur'an is in a clear Arabic tongue. This is one point.

Second: Allah's emphasizing it with an oath indicates its importance, and that it is among the matters that a person must accept and believe. Is that clear?

Third: It may be intended to repel the denial of one who denies the meaning of the report, like Allah, Mighty and Majestic, emphasizing the establishment of the Hour with many emphatics to refute the denial of the deniers.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: it is not strange that the polytheists mock the Prophet (ﷺ), because this has preceded from earlier nations, the mocking of the deniers of the messengers. In what ways? By many things: ﴿Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a great man from the two cities?﴾ [al-Zukhruf 31]. It is as if they say: Muhammad does not deserve this. As in their saying: ﴿Is this the one who speaks of your gods?﴾ [al-Anbiya 36], and the interrogative here is for belittlement, meaning: Who is this man who speaks ill of your gods! He is nothing, and has no value. And among them is their describing him as a madman and a babbler, and the like.

* Among the benefits of this verse: Allah, Blessed and Exalted, cares for His Prophet (ﷺ), since He sends down upon him from the Qur'an what consoles him. Its direction: that mentioning this, namely the mocking of earlier nations toward their messengers, is a consolation for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), because his knowing that earlier nations denied their messengers makes the matter easier for him. Is that not so? This is clear, for a person is consoled by calamities when they befall others, and his own calamity becomes lighter. Allah pointed to this in His saying: ﴿And it will not benefit you today, since you have wronged, that you are sharing in the punishment﴾ [al-Zukhruf 39]. Even though, had they been in this world and people shared in the punishment, it would have been easier for them and would have benefited them and moved them to patience. But on the Day of Resurrection it does not benefit.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the warning to those who deny the Prophet (ﷺ). From where is it taken? ﴿So there befell those who mocked them what they used to mock﴾. That is: beware, O deniers of Muhammad (ﷺ) who mock him.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: an indication that there is no messenger after Muhammad. Pay attention: can this be derived from the verse or not?

* Student: It is not clear.

* Shaykh: In reality, it is not clear, because ﴿messengers before you﴾ is the consolation of a person with what has passed, and it does not prevent that there might be other messengers after the Messenger (ﷺ), if that were possible. So there is no evidence in it for this.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that mocking and ridiculing the messengers necessitates punishment, because of His saying: ﴿So there befell those who mocked them what they used to mock﴾. Then, is this punishment for disbelief or for transgression? The answer: the first, it is for disbelief. Everyone who mocks the messengers or ridicules them is a disbeliever; there is no difficulty in this.

But is his repentance accepted?

The answer: Yes, his repentance is accepted, due to the generality of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, saying: ﴿Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ [al-Zumar 53].

And there is a rational evidence: that reviling the Prophet is disbelief only because of his prophethood, not because of his person. Prophethood and acting upon the law he brought are rights of Allah in reality, and the repentance of rights of Allah is accepted by consensus. So the correct view is that whoever mocks the Prophet or ridicules him, if he repents to Allah with sincere repentance (*tawba nasuha*), the status of apostasy (*ridda*) is lifted from him, he becomes a Muslim, and execution is lifted from him.

But if he reviles the Messenger, if he repents and we accept his repentance, is execution lifted from him or not? There is a difference of opinion. Among the scholars is one who says: his repentance is accepted, because reviling the Messenger is not a personal insult; rather, the insult is directed at what, the prophethood and the messengership, and prophethood and messengership are rights of Allah. So it is accepted, and he is not to be killed, so long as we have accepted his repentance.

Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah have mercy on him, chose that his repentance is accepted, but he is to be killed as a prescribed punishment (*hadd*). He gave as reason that reviling the Prophet, peace be upon him, is without doubt an assault on his person and on his message. As for his message, we say: his repentance is accepted. But as for his person, we must avenge our Prophet (ﷺ), take revenge and kill him. Thus the killing of one who reviles the Messenger, peace be upon him and his family, is obligatory, even if we accept the repentance of the reviler.

So what is the benefit if we say: his repentance is accepted and he is killed? The benefit: he is killed as a Muslim, he is washed, shrouded, and prayed over, his Muslim relatives inherit from him, and he remains under the rulings of Islam. This is unlike the case where we say he is an apostate, in which this ruling is not established for him.

If someone says: Has there not been one who reviled the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, during his lifetime, repented, and the Prophet accepted his repentance?

The answer: Yes, because the right is his. If he pardons him, then the right is his. This is one aspect. Another aspect: as an encouragement to him to repent, he lifted execution from him.

Third: If he repents, he will be among the companions of the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family. The Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, said when he was asked permission to kill the hypocrites: «People should not say that Muhammad kills his companions»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4905) and Muslim (2584/63), from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah.]]. But after his death all these reasons are absent, so it is obligatory upon his community to kill whoever reviles him, peace be upon him.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that sins are a cause of punishment, because of His saying: ﴿what they used to mock﴾; and that the punishment is proportionate to the deed, and for this reason it was expressed by it. This is from the justice of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: that punishment is proportionate to the deed. As for reward, a good deed is multiplied tenfold, up to seven hundredfold, and to many multiples.

Almighty Allah, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿Say: Travel through the earth﴾. ﴿Say﴾ is addressed to the Prophet (ﷺ).

﴿Travel through the earth﴾. ﴿Fi﴾ (in) here carries the meaning of ﴿ʿalā﴾ (upon). The particle ﴿fī﴾ is used in the sense of ʿalā only to indicate that the travelling should be thorough, as if they were moving within the depths of the earth. ﴿Travel through the earth﴾. Is this travel meant figuratively, through the hearts, or literally, on foot?

The answer: It may be either. Travel through the hearts means that a person reflects upon what happened to the earlier nations, based on what is authentically established of their history. The most authentic history of the earlier nations is what came in the Qur'an, or what is confirmed by the Sunnah. Travel on foot means: travel through the earth on your feet, so that you may look at the traces of the deniers who were destroyed, as in the words of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, you pass by them in the morning, and at night. Will you not then use reason?﴾ [al-Saffat 137–138]. Thus travel here includes both travel of the heart and travel on foot for the sake of taking lessons (iʿtibar).

﴿Then look how was the end of the deniers﴾. ﴿Look﴾: with your eyes or with your insight? That is, do you mean with your sights or with your insight? If we say the travel is of the heart, then the meaning of "look" is with insight; if we say it is on foot, then the meaning is with sight. This follows from what was said earlier.

﴿How was the end of the deniers﴾ [al-Anʿam 11]. ﴿How﴾ here is the predicate of ﴿kāna﴾ (was), placed before it. It must be placed first because it is an interrogative, and an interrogative must come at the beginning of the sentence, since it is the very purpose of the sentence. When the purpose of the sentence is this, its proper place is to be put first. For this reason, when you say, "Where is Zayd?", ﴿where﴾ (ayna) must be the fronted predicate, and you may not say, "Zayd where?"

So ﴿kayfa﴾ is in the accusative position as the fronted predicate of ﴿kāna﴾, and ﴿ʿāqibatu﴾ is its delayed subject, with reference to the fronting of the predicate; otherwise it is in its own place.

﴿How was the end of the deniers﴾. So what was it? It was the worst end—we seek refuge in Allah—Allah destroyed them, the Mighty and Majestic, and made them an example for those who came later, so that they might take lessons from them.

* This noble verse contains benefits, among them: the command to travel through the earth for the sake of taking lessons, whether with insight or with sight; because of His words: ﴿Travel through the earth﴾.

* Following from this benefit: we should read the history of the earlier nations from which source? From the Qur'an and authentic Sunnah. This restriction is necessary, because among the weak or fabricated reports about the earlier nations there is that which none but Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, can count. What matters is the authentic, and there are many reports containing accounts of the earlier nations.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the excellence of taking lessons, and that it is a desired matter, because of His words: ﴿Look﴾. Whether the lesson is drawn from those whom Allah punished or from those whom He rewarded: if from those Allah punished, the person is warned; if from those He rewarded, the person is encouraged. And in this verse, which of the two lessons is meant? From those whom Allah punished.

* Among the benefits of this verse: traces indicate the one who made them. This is known by sense and reality. A Bedouin was asked: "By what did you know your Lord?" He said: "Traces indicate the traveller; dung indicates the camel. So a sky with constellations, an earth with pathways, and seas with waves—do they not indicate the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing?" The answer: Yes, by Allah, they indicate the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing. Thus traces indicate the one who made them.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the punishment of the denier. Denial is one of the two components by which disbelief occurs, since disbelief takes place through one of two things: either denial, or arrogance. Yet denial is a branch of arrogance, because a person denies only because he sees himself as above the messenger.

If someone says: "Your statement that travel includes travel on foot in order to look with the eyes is problematic, since the Prophet (ﷺ) forbade entering the dwellings of the deniers or the destroyed"?

The answer: He (ﷺ) did not forbid it absolutely. Rather, he forbade us to enter them exultant, insolent, self-admiring at the traces, and similar things. As for entering them as one who takes lessons, weeping and fearful, there is no prohibition. For this reason he said: "Do not enter upon these who were punished unless you are weeping"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (433), and Muslim (2980/38), from the hadith of ʿAbdullah ibn ʿUmar.]].

So there is a difference between a person who enters these dwellings to take lessons, fear and weep, and another who enters them for exultation, arrogance, recreation and self-admiration. The first is praiseworthy, the second is blameworthy, and with this the problem is resolved.

Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Say: "To whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth?"﴾ [al-An'am 12]. Ask these deniers, who reject tawhid al-uluhiyyah (affirming that Allah alone is the one worthy of worship): ﴿To whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth?﴾ Is it to Zayd, or to 'Amr, or to so-and-so or so-and-so?

Then He, blessed and exalted, commanded His Prophet ﷺ to answer this question himself, so He said: ﴿Say: "To Allah."﴾ Here we ask: is the answer from Allah or from the Messenger? The answer is: from the Messenger, by the command of Allah. Therefore the answer is the answer of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, because Allah commanded the Messenger to say this: ﴿Say: "To Allah."﴾

﴿He has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾ [al-An'am 12]. ﴿Prescribed﴾ means "made obligatory," because kitabah (prescribing) means ijab (making obligatory). Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿O you who have believed, fasting has been prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you﴾ [al-Baqarah 183]. ﴿Prescribed﴾ means what? It means "obligated and made mandatory." Allah, the Exalted, also said: ﴿Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times﴾ [an-Nisa' 103], meaning an obligation with set times.

﴿He has prescribed for Himself﴾: ﴿for Himself﴾ means "for His essence," and the nafs (self) of Allah is His essence, not an attribute. Rather, it is the essence itself. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And Allah warns you of Himself﴾ [Aal 'Imran 28]. The meaning is not "He warns you of an attribute that is His self"; rather the meaning is "Allah warns you of Himself," that is, the essence of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. So it is not an attribute but the essence. The meaning of "He warns you of Himself" is that Allah warns you of His punishment, because He, the Majestic and Exalted, commanded us to know an important matter when He said: ﴿Know that Allah is severe in punishment and that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Ma'idah 98]. So He commanded us to know this important knowledge, which contains both encouragement (targhib) and warning (tarhib). Where is the warning in it?

* Student: ﴿Know that Allah is severe in punishment,﴾ this is the warning.
* Shaykh: This is the warning. ﴿And that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ is the encouragement. So He, glory be to Him and exalted, commanded us to know about His actions and attributes, as warning and as encouragement. Here He said: ﴿And Allah warns you of Himself,﴾ because the context is one of threat and punishment, addressing the polytheists who deny.

His words ﴿mercy﴾ mean that He shows mercy to His servants, the Mighty and Majestic. He prescribed this upon Himself. For this reason the authentic hadith qudsi (a sacred hadith, whose meaning is from Allah while its wording is from the Prophet ﷺ) says: "Indeed My mercy precedes My wrath."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (7422) and Muslim (2751/14), from Abu Hurayrah.]] Allah's mercy toward the servants is what He prescribed upon Himself. It is not that we prescribed it upon Him; rather He prescribed it upon Himself.

If someone says: "We see people who are struck by misery and affliction, who lose wealth and children, and who are in extreme hardship. Where is the mercy?"

The answer: whatever befalls a person of affliction while he is a believer is, what? It is mercy. Because if he is patient, he is rewarded with the reward of the patient, and if he seeks reward (ihtisab) he is rewarded with the reward of the thankful. So it is good for him. How many people, if they were given health, wealth and children, would become arrogant, and wealth would corrupt them? And how many people are the opposite.

Everything that afflicts the believer, praise be to Allah, is mercy and expiation. Even if a person is startled by something that confronts him, he is recorded as having a reward for that. "O Allah, to You belongs praise." Until the hadith came: if a man loses something from his pocket, for example, and then panics, fearing it has been lost, he has a reward.[[Narrated by at-Tirmidhi (2991), from 'A'ishah, and its wording: "Until he places it in the sleeve of his shirt, then loses it and is alarmed for it, until the servant comes out of his sins as red gold comes out of the furnace."]] To this extent! So this is mercy. How excellent is the saying of Rabi'ah al-'Adawiyyah: "The sweetness of its reward has made me forget the bitterness of its patience."

All pains, misery, fatigue, worry and grief in this world pass away. Either they pass away into their opposite, or they lead their owner to destruction, but they must pass away. The reward, however, remains.

If someone says: "And the disbeliever?"

The answer: the disbeliever is the one who forfeited mercy for himself, even though Allah has mercy upon him by facilitating for him food, drink, marriage, shelter, and what is similar to these.

Then He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿He will surely gather you for the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt﴾. Allah has spoken the truth. ﴿He will surely gather you﴾ is also a sentence emphasized with three emphatics: the implied oath, the lam that falls in the answer of the oath, and the nun of emphasis. The implied meaning is: "By Allah, He will surely gather you." The address is to the creation. ﴿He will surely gather you﴾, O people, all of you, as He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Say: "Indeed, the former and the latter will all be gathered to the appointed time of a known Day"﴾ [al-Waqi'ah 49-50]. Allahu akbar! We will be gathered with our fathers, our grandfathers, and the grandfathers of our grandfathers, back to Adam. All will be gathered. Likewise, our descendants, the first and the last, will all be gathered together until the Day of Resurrection. When the deniers compared resurrection by saying: ﴿Bring us our fathers, if you are truthful﴾ [al-Jathiyah 25], it was said to them: ﴿Say: "Allah gives you life, then causes you to die, then will gather you to the Day of Resurrection"﴾ [al-Jathiyah 26]. You were not told that you are being resurrected now so that you could argue and say: "Bring our fathers." Rather you were told: you are gathered for what? For the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt.

His words ﴿He will surely gather you to the Day of Resurrection﴾: the Day of Resurrection is the Last Day, and it was named so for three matters. This is what we know, and Allah knows best whether there is something beyond it. The three matters are:

First: the standing of people from their graves before the Lord of the worlds. This standing is a great standing, O our brothers. The entire world, with one cry, all come to present themselves, and none is left behind. This is a very, very great standing. Even the one eaten by predators, burned by fire, or drowned by water, must come out.

It is also named qiyamah (standing) because justice is established on it. Retribution will be taken even for the hornless sheep from the horned sheep.[[Narrated by Muslim (2582/60), from Abu Hurayrah.]] These are two.

Third: the witnesses stand on it, who testify. This nation testifies against the previous nations, and the Messenger ﷺ will be a witness over this nation. For these three matters the Day was named the Day of Resurrection.

If it is said: "What is the evidence?"

We say: as for the first, its evidence is the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿The Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 6].

As for the second, the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And We will set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection﴾ [al-Anbiya' 47], meaning for the day on which justice is established.

As for the third, the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believed in the worldly life and on the Day when the witnesses stand﴾ [Ghafir 51].

Then He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿about which there is no doubt﴾. This is a negation intended to emphasize the affirmation that came before it. What is the affirmation? ﴿He will surely gather you﴾, meaning a gathering that is emphasized and about which there is no doubt. The negation here is not a pure negation; rather it clarifies the completeness of the affirmation, that it is a matter about which there is no doubt. On this explanation, the negation is on its own basis.

It has been said that the negation here means a prohibition, meaning "do not doubt it." But the first is more eloquent, because when it is said "there is no doubt in it," if a person doubts, that is due to a defect in his mind, since what has been absolutely negated of doubt cannot be doubted by a sane person. So keeping the negation on its own basis is more eloquent and more appropriate.

Then He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Those who have lost themselves, they will not believe﴾. ﴿Those who have lost themselves﴾ is a subject (mubtada'), and the predicate may be omitted. The estimated meaning is: "Those who have lost themselves are the losers," as He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Say: "Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection"﴾ [az-Zumar 15]. So the meaning is: those who lost themselves are truly the losers.

﴿They will not believe﴾ is an emphasis or an explanation of the cause by which the loss occurred. It is also possible that the sentence ﴿they will not believe﴾ is the predicate of the subject, and it is joined with the fa' because alladhina (those who) is a relative pronoun, which conveys generality, and the relative pronoun resembles the conditional in its generality, so the fa' is attached to its predicate.

* In this noble verse there are benefits. Among them: all who are in the heavens and the earth belong to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. The evidence is: ﴿Say: "To whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth?" Say: "To Allah."﴾

If someone says: "How did you take the generality when man (man) is for rational beings and what (ma) is for non-rational beings?"

The answer: these two words are interchangeable, meaning that one of them may stand in place of the other. The evidence is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens glorifies Allah﴾ [al-Jumu'ah 1], and in another verse: ﴿Whoever is in the heavens﴾ [an-Nur 41]. This indicates that man and ma are interchangeable, although the more common usage is that ma is for non-rational beings and man is for rational beings. Accordingly, we say: man here includes both rational and non-rational beings. Or we say: man is for rational beings, but it is used for them as a general expression, because if Allah, the Exalted, owns the rational being, who is willing and choosing, then what is other than him is all the more so.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: affirming the heavens and the earth. This is repeated often for us, and you know that the heavens are seven and the earths are seven.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: when we believe in this, and that whoever is in the heavens and the earth belongs to Allah, we will not turn to anyone but Allah, and we will not fear anyone but Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, because He is the owner of whoever is in the heavens and the earth. Would that we truly put our trust in Allah. If we put our trust in Allah as He deserves, the matter would be as the Prophet ﷺ said: "He would provide for you as He provides for the birds, which go out in the morning hungry and return in the evening full-bellied."[[Narrated by at-Tirmidhi (2344) and Ibn Majah (4164), from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab.]] "They go out in the morning hungry" means they fly at the beginning of the day while they are hungry, and return at the end of the day with full bellies. Glory be to Allah!

This is something observed. You find birds in the early morning flying in the air, and Allah the Exalted has given them keen sight, as a mercy from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. They see the grain while they are in the sky and descend upon it. They see the tiny seed that a person can only perceive with difficulty, and they see it easily. You find them taking a very small seed from the middle of a spread carpet, from among its nap, but Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, gave them sight so that they may live.

The point is: when you know that whoever is in the heavens and the earth belongs to Allah, on whom will you rely? Whom will you fear? Whom will you hope in? Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the answer of the questioner himself when the matter is clear, based on His saying: ﴿Say: "To Allah."﴾ Although He commanded him to ask, then commanded him to answer. So if the matter is clear and not disputed, then you answer, because the one being asked may be prevented from answering by arrogance and pride. So you answer yourself when the matter is clear and not disputed.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: Allah, the Exalted, may prescribe upon Himself whatever He wills. The evidence is His saying: ﴿He has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾.

If someone says: "How can something be binding upon Allah?"

The answer: Allah bound Himself to it, and He may do whatever He wills. We do not bind Allah to anything, but Allah may bind Himself to something. The prescribing of mercy by Allah upon Himself does not contradict His perfection; rather it is from His perfection, the Mighty and Majestic, that He prescribes mercy upon Himself. But we have no right over Allah except what He made obligatory upon Himself. Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his Nuniyyah:

"There is no obligatory right for the servants upon Him;
He made obligatory the great reward."

"He made obligatory" — not "we." 

"If they are punished, it is by His justice..."
".............."

Because the sin is their sin.

"...... or if they are blessed, it is by His grace, and grace belongs to the Bestower."
Glory be to Him and exalted.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: Allah is referred to by the word nafs (self); the evidence is His saying: ﴿He has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾, and it has parallels. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And Allah warns you of Himself﴾ [Aal 'Imran 28], and 'Isa, peace be upon him, said: ﴿You know what is within myself, and I do not know what is within Yourself﴾ [al-Ma'idah 116].

The self (nafs) of Allah is not like the self of a human being. A human uses the word nafs for himself and has a nafs, as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death﴾ [az-Zumar 42], and He said: ﴿Every soul will taste death﴾ [Aal 'Imran 185].

Here, ﴿takes the souls﴾ means the spirit within the body, not the body, because at death the body is not seized. The body is in the earth and is hidden. What is taken is the spirit. So a human has a nafs, which is the spirit, and he refers to his essence by the word nafs, so he says: "I spoke to you myself," and you say: "The man himself came." But as for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, He does not have a nafs in the sense of a separate thing; rather He is His nafs, meaning He is His essence, the Mighty and Majestic.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: affirming resurrection, based on His saying: ﴿He will surely gather you to the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt.﴾

* Among its benefits: emphasizing a matter with an oath and other emphatics when the need calls for it. When does the need call for it? The need calls for it in certain situations. Among them: when the one addressed is a denier, in which case, according to rhetoric, the speech must be emphasized. Among them: when the matter is distant and strange, in which case it is emphasized, but not like the first. The first is emphasized obligatorily, and this is emphasized..? 

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: No, it is not permissible (jawazan); we say it is recommended (istihbaban). That is, emphasizing it is better than not doing so, and we say it is good (istihsanan). Whenever the need calls for emphasizing the speech, emphasize it, and this is not considered verbosity or a flaw in eloquence.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the wisdom of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in gathering the first and the last, so that this day becomes a witnessed day, as He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿That is a Day to which all mankind will be gathered, and that is a Day witnessed﴾ [Hud 103]. The first and the last will witness it. We witness Habil and Qabil, and we witness the last person of this nation. The whole world is witnessed; indeed everything is witnessed: the jinn, the beasts, the wild animals, everything. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And there is no creature on the earth, nor bird that flies with its wings, but they are communities like you. We have not neglected in the Book anything. Then to their Lord they will be gathered﴾ [al-An'am 38]. Everything. If a person were to picture this day, he would see a great scene that he cannot grasp now. But we understand its meaning and do not grasp its reality. Its reality is more eloquent than what we imagine. O Allah, make it easy for us.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: naming the Day of Resurrection the Day of Resurrection, for the reasons you have heard in the tafsir.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that there is no doubt about this day, by the Sharia and by reason. By the Sharia, because Allah informed us of it, emphasized it, and set forth examples for it.

By reason: it is not reasonable that Allah, the Exalted, would create this creation, command and forbid it, send messengers to it, and then souls, wealth and offspring are violated in fighting in the way of Allah, and the outcome is that the earth simply swallows them. This contradicts wisdom. So reason requires that there be a resurrection, even if there were no explicit text. How much more so when the texts are numerous, very numerous.

And from the mercy of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and to Him belong praise, favor and grace, that He repeats the affirmation of the Day of Resurrection and sets forth examples for it, because belief in the Last Day is what truly moves a person to faith. For if the believer did not believe that he will be resurrected and recompensed, whether for good, then good, or for evil, then evil, he would never act, and the nation would become a place of plunder, looting, seizure and aggression.

Among the benefits of this verse: these deniers have ruined themselves, as if they had never existed on the earth, because they did not profit from their lives. Therefore, since they did not profit from the life of this world, they did not profit from the life of the Hereafter, and so they will abide forever in the Fire of Hell, and we seek refuge in Allah.

Another benefit of the verse: it is an element of eloquence (fasahah) to mention the cause after the effect (al-musabbab), if we take the clause ﴿فَهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ ("so they do not believe") as a predicate. The reason for this is that the cause of their loss is non-belief, so the cause is placed last and the effect is placed first. This holds when we take ﴿فَهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ as the predicate of ﴿الَّذِينَ خَسِرُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ﴾ ("those who have ruined themselves"). If, however, we take it as an independent clause, this benefit does not arise, since the order is then sequential.

Then He, Exalted and Majestic, said: ﴿And His is whatever dwells in the night and the day﴾ [al-An'am 13]. The pronoun in ﴿His﴾ refers to God, Exalted and Majestic.

As for ﴿dwells﴾ (sakana), it may be from *al-suknā* (dwelling, residence), or it may be from *al-sukūn*, which is the opposite of motion. If it is from *al-sukūn*, the question arises: where is the moving thing? Since things are either still or moving, how can He say ﴿His is whatever dwells﴾?

The answer to this difficulty is that it belongs to the type of speech that mentions one of two opposites and dispenses with the other. Its parallel is God's saying: ﴿And He made for you garments that protect you from the heat, and garments that protect you from your violence﴾ [al-Nahl 81]. The garments protect against heat and cold, but He mentioned only heat and violence, because the two garments are alike: one is worn in the heat of the weather, and the other in the heat of battle. So He said ﴿garments that protect you from the heat﴾ and ﴿garments that protect you from your violence﴾. The point is that He dispensed with mentioning cold by mentioning heat.

If, however, we take it as *al-suknā*, then ﴿His is whatever dwells﴾ means that everything belongs to Him, because all created beings dwell in their places of settlement.

If a verse is suitable for both meanings, or if the wording is suitable for both, may we use it for both meanings? Yes, on the condition that the two meanings do not contradict each other. If they do contradict each other, then one takes the meaning that the evidence favours.

In ﴿His is whatever dwells in the night and the day﴾, consider His saying ﴿in the night and the day﴾. You will find that it is general with respect to time. The verse before it, ﴿Say: To whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth?﴾, is general with respect to place. So God, blessed and exalted, mentioned the generality of place and the generality of time: the generality of place in ﴿Say: To whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth? Say: To God﴾, and the generality of time in ﴿His is whatever dwells in the night and the day﴾.

﴿And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾: He mentioned hearing, which encompasses every sound, and knowledge, which encompasses every state.

There is no harm in restating the divisions of hearing with which God described Himself. Hearing is first of two kinds: the hearing of response and the hearing of sound. The hearing of response is found in God's saying, blessed and exalted: ﴿Indeed, my Lord is the Hearer of supplication﴾ [Ibrahim 39]. This includes both the hearing of response and the hearing of sound, and it includes the worshipper's saying: "God hears those who praise Him."

The hearing of sound has divisions or types. (If you wish, say "types", since you called the first "divisions", so mention the second as "types".) The first type is intended to express support and victory. The second is intended to express threat. The third is intended to express encompassing.

An example of the first, intended as support, is God's saying, blessed and exalted, to Moses and Aaron: ﴿Do not fear. Indeed, I am with you both, hearing and seeing﴾ [Ta-Ha 46].

An example of the second, intended as threat, is His saying: ﴿Or do they think that We do not hear their secrets and their private conversations? Yes, [We do]﴾ [al-Zukhruf 80].

An example of the third is God's saying: ﴿God has already heard the speech of the woman who argues with you concerning her husband and complains to God, and God hears your exchange. Indeed, God is All-Hearing, All-Seeing﴾ [al-Mujadila 1].

God, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿And His is whatever dwells in the night and the day, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾. Regarding ﴿dwells﴾ there are two meanings:

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: Yes. And the second?

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: Yes, from *al-sukūn*. Do the two meanings contradict each other?

* Student: They do not contradict each other.

* Shaykh: Then the verse indicates both meanings.

Regarding His saying ﴿And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾: is the hearing meant here the hearing of response rather than the hearing of sound?

* Student: The hearing of sound is included.

* Shaykh: Then both meanings are intended together. What do you say about God's saying ﴿Indeed, my Lord is the Hearer of supplication﴾? Which of the two types is it?

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: Yes, the hearing of sound and of response, because He hears them and then responds to them.

Do you have evidence from the Qur'an that hearing comes to mean response or acceptance?

* Student: ﴿Indeed, my Lord is the Hearer of supplication﴾.

* Shaykh: [There is] God's saying: ﴿And do not be like those who said, "We hear," while they do not hear﴾ [al-Anfal 21]. This is a clear text. ﴿We hear﴾ means perceiving by sound, that particular sound. ﴿While they do not hear﴾ means they do not respond; otherwise they do hear with their ears.

* From the benefits of this noble and great verse, ﴿His is whatever dwells in the night﴾: God, blessed and exalted, is singled out as the owner of everything. What is the basis of this exclusivity? It is the placing of the predicate first, ﴿His﴾, although its proper place is later. Placing what should be delayed before its place conveys restriction (*ḥaṣr*). This is why we say that His saying ﴿You alone do we worship﴾ [al-Fatiha 5] is pure monotheism, meaning: we worship none but You. We say the same of ﴿You alone do we ask for help﴾ [al-Fatiha 5].

* From the benefits of this verse: stillness and motion are in God's hand, exalted is He. Since He is the owner of whatever is still and whatever moves, He is the owner of both motion and stillness. This is evidence that the actions of servants are created by God, Exalted, and this is the position of the early generation (*al-salaf*) and the People of the Sunnah (*Ahl al-Sunnah*). It is a middle position between the views of the Jabriyyah (who hold that humans have no real agency) and the Qadariyyah (who hold that humans create their own actions independently).

* From the benefits of this verse: the affirmation of these two names, the All-Hearing (*al-Samī'*) and the All-Knowing (*al-'Alīm*), and the affirmation of the attributes they contain: the attribute of hearing in ﴿the All-Hearing﴾, and the attribute of knowledge in ﴿the All-Knowing﴾.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 6, verse 14:

﴿Say, "Shall I take as a protector other than Allah?"﴾ [al-An'am: 14]. ﴿Atakhidh﴾ here takes two objects: the first object, (ghayr) (other than), is placed first, and the second is ﴿waliyyan﴾ (a protector). If we wished to arrange them according to their grammatical function, the verse would read: "Qul atakhidh ghayr Allah waliyyan." The point is that Allah commanded His Prophet ﷺ to declare openly: ﴿Shall I take as a protector other than Allah?﴾ One who seeks help from Him, who has Him manage my affairs, and whom I follow in His law? The interrogative here is for negation.

﴿Fatir al-samawati wa'l-ard﴾ means: their Creator, without any previous pattern.

﴿Al-samawati wa'l-ard﴾ has been discussed many times before.

﴿Wa huwa yut'imu wa la yut'am﴾: He is Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. ﴿Yut'imu﴾: there is no one who feeds another except that Allah is the One who fed him. "Fed him" means He facilitated food for him, and were it not for that, food would not have reached him.

Allah the Mighty and Majestic said, explaining this: ﴿Have you considered what you sow? Is it you who make it grow, or are We the growers?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 63-64]. The answer: Rather, You, our Lord. ﴿If We willed, We could make it into debris, and you would remain astonished, [saying], "Indeed, we are burdened with debt. Rather, we are deprived."﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 65-67]. Had Allah made it debris, we would not have eaten it.

Then: ﴿Have you considered the water which you drink? Is it you who sent it down from the clouds, or are We the sender?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 68-69]. The answer: Rather, You, our Lord. This food and this drink: the crops are food, and the water is drink.

Then what makes food and drink wholesome, which is cooking and preparing by means of fire: ﴿Have you considered the fire which you kindle? Is it you who produced its tree, or are We the producer?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 71-72].

So the One who feeds is Allah the Mighty and Majestic. Then, if Allah the Exalted willed, we would not be fed even if food were available; if Allah willed, He would not have created for us mouths, intestines, or stomachs, and we would not eat.

So ﴿yut'imu﴾ means: He brings into existence food, both what is eaten and what is drunk, and what makes food and drink wholesome; likewise He brings into existence in the children of Adam the faculties that accept food and benefit from it.

Some scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, mentioned that food will not reach you until more than three hundred people have worked on it, because you begin with ploughing, irrigation, channelling water, and other things, then buying, grinding, and kneading; you will find many things that the food does not reach you until it has passed through all of these.

﴿Wa la yut'am﴾: or "wa la yat'am"? What we have is ﴿wa la yut'am﴾. So others are in need of Him, while He needs no one. He is ﴿not fed﴾ because He is free of need of anyone. Moreover, He, may He be exalted, does not eat, because He is the One, the Self-Sufficient (al-Samad); had He eaten, He would be in need of food, and this is impossible for Allah the Mighty and Majestic.

﴿Wa huwa yut'imu wa la yut'am. Qul﴾: another declaration. ﴿Indeed I have been commanded to be the first of those who submit﴾. So the first command is to realise Tawhid al-Rububiyyah (the Oneness of Lordship), and the second is to realise Tawhid al-'Ibadah (the Oneness of Worship).

﴿Qul﴾ means: say to the people, openly. ﴿Indeed I have been commanded to be the first of those who submit﴾: ﴿the first of those who submit﴾ from this nation, not from all nations. The meaning of ﴿aslama﴾ here is: he submits to Allah outwardly and inwardly, because Islam is applied to this meaning, and when Islam has this meaning, faith is included within it.

﴿Wa la takunanna min al-mushrikin﴾: the phrase ﴿wa la takunanna﴾ is conjoined to ﴿qul﴾, meaning: say this, and ﴿do not be among the polytheists﴾, but rather devote worship and submission sincerely to Allah the Mighty and Majestic.

* In this noble verse: the Prophet ﷺ was commanded to declare that he would not take a protector other than Allah. Is this obligatory upon him or not? Yes, it is obligatory upon him to declare it, because he is a messenger, an imam who is followed, so he must declare the realisation of Lordship.

* Among its benefits: that the servant should seek refuge only in Allah the Exalted, because Allah is the Protector, and the protection of Allah the Mighty and Majestic is founded on praise, as He the Exalted said: ﴿And He is the Protector, the Praiseworthy﴾ [al-Shura: 28].

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that Allah alone is the Creator of the heavens and the earth without any pattern; meaning that He, the Exalted, did not create heavens and earths before and then recreate them again, but they are as they are.

* Among the benefits of the verse: the perfection of the power of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, in that He originated the heavens and the earth, and the heavens and the earth remained according to what Allah, Blessed and Exalted, willed: ﴿The sun runs to a stationary place for it﴾ [Ya-Sin: 38], ﴿And the moon, We have determined for it phases﴾ [Ya-Sin: 39]; they did not differ.

* Among the benefits of this verse: that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is the Feeder, and there is no feeder other than Him.

* Built upon this benefit: we should not ask for food except from Allah, Blessed and Exalted. If we—and we seek Allah's forgiveness and turn to Him in repentance—had held fast to this, along with reliance upon Allah and seeking His help, our provision would be guaranteed, due to the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out, and will provide for him from where he does not expect﴾ [al-Talaq: 2-3]. But material and sensory matters have overcome us, so that man—regrettably—relies on causes more than on the One who causes, the Mighty and Majestic.

And in a hadith from the Prophet ﷺ: "If you truly relied upon Allah with the reliance due to Him, He would provide for you as He provides for the birds: they go out in the morning hungry and return in the evening full." ("Taghdu khimaṣan," meaning: they go out at the beginning of the day hungry; "wa tarūhu biṭānan," meaning: they return at the end of the day.) [Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (2344) and Ibn Majah (4164) from the hadith of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab.]

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that Allah the Exalted is not fed by anyone, due to His not needing food and not needing anything else. He is ﴿not fed﴾ because He does not need food, and ﴿nor is He fed﴾ also, meaning: He does not need anything else; He is free of need of all that is other than Him, and all that is other than Him is in need of Him.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the obligation for the Prophet ﷺ to declare about himself that he is the first to submit, because of His saying: ﴿Say, "Indeed I have been commanded to be the first of those who submit"﴾ [al-An'am: 14], meaning from this nation; and this is what has come to pass.

* Among the benefits of the verse: that the Prophet ﷺ is in need of Islam, and has no share in Lordship, as he himself stated, peace be upon him, when he called his closest kinsmen, calling each by name: "O so-and-so, son of so-and-so," until he reached his daughter Fatimah, and said: "O Fatimah, daughter of Muhammad, ask me from my wealth whatever you wish; I cannot avail you anything against Allah." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2753) and Muslim (206/351) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the validity of forbidding what cannot possibly occur, because of His saying: ﴿And do not be among the polytheists﴾. The Prophet's ﷺ committing shirk is legally impossible, yet he was forbidden from it.

If someone says: what is the wisdom when it cannot occur?

We say: the wisdom, as far as we know, is two-fold:

The first: calling him to steadfastness in sincerity, so that he does not commit shirk in the future.

The second: reassuring his community that when they are forbidden from shirk, this is not objectionable and there is no harm in it, since their leader, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him, was commanded not to be among the polytheists.

Can it be inferred from this that we say to a person, "You are a polytheist," if he does what constitutes shirk? This may be said, depending on the situation: if we think that, were we to say, "You are a polytheist," he would be seized by jahiliyyah zeal, grow arrogant and reject it, then we do not address him in this manner. But if we know that he is one who fears Allah, and that if we say, "This is shirk; if you do it, you are a polytheist, and if you say it, you are a polytheist," he would be seized by fear of Allah the Mighty and Majestic and would keep far away from it entirely, then there is no harm in our saying, "You are a polytheist," according to what the situation requires.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 6, verse 15:

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Say: Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day.﴾ [al-An'am 15] Again, I declare: if you disobey Allah, you will be punished.

﴿Say: Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day.﴾ What is ﴿the punishment﴾ the object of? Is it the object of ﴿I fear﴾, or of ﴿I disobey﴾? It is the object of ﴿I fear﴾. The meaning is: I fear the punishment of a tremendous day if I disobey my Lord. And what is the tremendous Day? The tremendous Day is the Day of Resurrection, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing.﴾ [al-Hajj 1]

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: it is obligatory upon the Prophet (ﷺ) to declare the recompense of the Day of Resurrection, and that he fears it if he disobeys his Lord.

* And among its benefits: disobedience is a cause of punishment, but acts of disobedience are of two kinds: sins that Allah will not forgive, which is shirk (associating partners with Allah); and sins that fall under the will of Allah, which are the major sins (kaba'ir); and there are other sins that righteous deeds expiate, which are the minor sins (saghair). This concerns what is between you and Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

As for the rights of the children of Adam, it is necessary to give them their rights: either by seeking their pardon in this world, or by good deeds taken from the deeds of this wrongdoer. We have previously discussed whether, when a person repents from a sin that involves wrong done to another, the right of the other person is dropped or not. We mentioned that the apparent texts indicate that it is dropped if it is not a matter of property, like one who commits fornication with a woman by force and then repents: Allah accepts his repentance and pleases the woman who was forced into fornication. He said: ﴿Whoever is turned away from it that Day, Allah has had mercy upon him﴾ [al-An'am 16].

Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿Say: Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day.﴾ [al-An'am 15] ﴿Say﴾ means: to these people and others, declaring this important statement.

In His saying ﴿innī﴾ there are two readings: ﴿innīya﴾ and ﴿innī﴾, and both are canonical (sab'iyyah).

His saying ﴿the punishment of a tremendous Day﴾ is the object of ﴿I fear﴾, meaning: I fear the punishment of this tremendous Day. I think we have explained this and its benefits.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 6, verse 16:

﴿Whoever is spared punishment that Day, Allah will have shown him mercy.﴾ In ﴿whoever is spared﴾ there are also two readings: ﴿مَنْ يَصْرِفْ﴾ (man yaṣrif, "whoever spares") and ﴿مَنْ يُصْرَفْ﴾ (man yuṣraf, "whoever is spared").

﴿عَنْهُ﴾ ("from it") means: from it, the punishment.

﴿فَقَدْ رَحِمَهُ﴾ ("then He has had mercy on him") means: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has had mercy on him. Someone may ask: how do we know that the pronoun in His saying ﴿رَحِمَهُ﴾ refers back to Allah, Mighty and Majestic?

It is answered: because He was mentioned earlier: ﴿Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day.﴾ ﴿Whoever is spared from it﴾ means: my Lord spares this punishment, ﴿then He has had mercy on him﴾; or ﴿whoever is spared from it﴾, meaning this punishment, ﴿then He has had mercy on him﴾, i.e., my Lord.

﴿And that is the clear triumph﴾: the one referred to by ﴿that﴾ is the sparing understood from His saying ﴿whoever is spared﴾.

His saying ﴿الْفَوْزُ﴾ (al-fawz, "the triumph") is the predicate of the subject, and ﴿الْمُبِينُ﴾ (al-mubin, "the clear") is an attribute of "the triumph."

* In this verse there is evidence that true triumph is that which is attained by Allah's sparing a person the punishment on the Day of Resurrection. That is, the triumph which is genuinely manifest, which is the greatest triumph, because any other triumph is fleeting; even one who is granted success in this world, his triumph is incomplete, unless his triumph in this world is a means to righteous deeds through which he triumphs in the Hereafter.

﴿That is the clear triumph﴾: ﴿الْمُبِينُ﴾ means "the clear" (al-bayyin). It is an active participle from (abāna), and (abāna) may be intransitive or transitive. When you say, "The teacher abāna (made clear) to the student the meaning of the book," this is transitive. When you say, "The dawn abāna," meaning it became clear, this is intransitive. So ﴿الْمُبِينُ﴾ here means "bayyin" (clear, manifest).

* In the verse there are benefits, among them: the triumph of the one from whom the punishment is spared on the Day of Resurrection.

* Among them: the affirmation of mercy for Allah, expressed in a verb form, by His saying ﴿فَقَدْ رَحِمَهُ﴾. The mercy of Allah, blessed and exalted, is among the essential attributes that are also active (al-ṣifāt al-dhātiyya al-fi'liyya); in terms of its meaning it is active, and in terms of being a settled attribute of Allah it is among the essential attributes.

If someone says: is the mercy of Allah real, or is it an expression for reward, or for the will to reward? The answer: it is real, but it is not like the mercy of the created being, which carries a kind of weakness; rather, it is the mercy of the Creator who is above His servants, Mighty and Majestic.

Some people have denied mercy and said: Allah is not described with real mercy, because it indicates tenderness and softness, and this does not befit Allah, Mighty and Majestic. When we say to them, "Explain it to us," they say: mercy here is an expression for the effects of mercy, which are either the will, or the reward and bounty that result from Allah's mercy.

When it is asked of them: what has led you to divert the speech from its apparent meaning? They say: because mercy, in the manner we have mentioned, indicates weakness. This is the extent of their argument.

We say to them: the answer to this fruit of your argument is, for us, very easy: we say that this mercy which you claim indicates weakness is only the mercy of the created being; as for the mercy of the Creator, it does not indicate this in any way, but rather indicates the perfection of His grace and generosity, Mighty and Majestic.

Furthermore, we may dispute your claim that tenderness and softness indicate weakness. How many a powerful ruler is merciful, while he is possessed of strong authority and could oppress his subjects as he wishes, yet he is merciful to those who deserve mercy. So we first deny the claim; then, even if we grant for the sake of argument that mercy indicates tenderness and softness, this is the mercy of the created being.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the true, manifest, clear triumph is the triumph of being spared the punishment on the Day of Resurrection. We ask Allah to grant us and you that.

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said, consoling His Messenger (ﷺ), strengthening him and fortifying his resolve: ﴿If Allah touches you with harm, there is none who can remove it except Him﴾ [al-An'am 17]. The word "harm" (ḍurr) here includes harm to the body, to the mind, to wealth, and everything through which a person may be harmed.

The word ﴿ḍurr﴾, as you see, is indefinite in a conditional context, and an indefinite noun in a conditional context conveys generality: whatever harm Allah may touch you with, meaning, may afflict you with. ﴿There is none who can remove it﴾ means: there is no one who can remove it except Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

﴿And if He touches you with good, then He is Able to do all things﴾. The "good" here is the opposite of harm: health, sound mind, wealth, family, security, the opening of the breast (to faith), and other things.

﴿Then He is Able to do all things﴾: He is capable of turning the harm that has befallen you into good.

In another verse: ﴿And if Allah touches you with harm, there is none who can remove it except Him, and if He wills good for you, there is none who can repel His bounty﴾ [Yunus 107], Mighty and Majestic is He.

* From this noble verse it is derived that a person should hang his hope upon Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for when he knows the content of this verse he will rely upon Allah in all his affairs.

In another verse: ﴿And if Allah touches you with harm, there is none who can remove it except Him, and if He wills good for you, there is none who can repel His bounty﴾ [Yunus 107], Mighty and Majestic is He.

* It is derived from this noble verse that a person should hang his hope upon Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for when he knows the content of this verse he will rely upon Allah in all his affairs.

* Among its lessons: strengthening the Prophet (ﷺ) in calling to Allah, and that however much these people try to harm you, they cannot do so unless Allah wills it.

* Among them: encouragement to patience, for when you know that the one who afflicts you with harm is Allah, you must be patient, since you are His servant and He does with you as He wills, so be patient over the harm that befalls you.

* Among them: the strength of a servant's hope in Allah, Mighty and Majestic, when harm befalls him, that the harm will be removed from him. The proof of this is His saying: ﴿Then He is Able to do all things﴾. How many harms have befallen people to the point of despair and hopelessness, which Allah removed! How many a person has been struck by illness until he reached the edge of the grave, and then Allah healed him; how many a person has been struck by poverty until he could not find his daily sustenance for the day and night, and Allah made him rich; how many a person was alone and Allah provided for him; and so on, because Allah is Able to do all things.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the complete sovereignty of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and that He, glorified and exalted, is the one who disposes of His servants as He wills; by His saying: ﴿If He touches you﴾ with such-and-such, ﴿and if He touches you﴾ with such-and-such.

* Among them: the generality of Allah's power; by His saying: ﴿Then He is Able to do all things﴾. Power (qudra) is opposed by incapacity (ʿajz). Here are two attributes that are similar or close: strength (quwwa) and power (qudra). The difference between them is known through definition. Qudra: the ability to act without incapacity; quwwa: the ability to act without weakness. The evidence for qudra is the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿And Allah is never to be frustrated by anything in the heavens or on earth; indeed, He is ever Knowing and Competent﴾ [Fatir 44]. The evidence for quwwa is the saying of Allah, Exalted: ﴿Allah is the One who created you from weakness, then made after weakness strength, then made after strength weakness and white hair﴾ [al-Rum 54]. Which is more complete, or which is more general?

We say: quwwa is more general, because it applies to one who has consciousness and to other than one who has consciousness, meaning to one who has will and to one who does not. You say: "So-and-so is strong," and you say: "Iron is strong." Qudra, however, applies only to one who has will, for it is not correct to say: "The door is capable," since it has no will. Which is more complete?

Strength is more complete, because the existence of qudra necessarily implies quwwa, but not the reverse. We illustrate this with a man who was told: "Carry this stone," and he carried it, but with difficulty. How do we describe this man? As capable but not strong. Another person, whom we told: "Carry this stone," tried to carry it but failed; we say: this one is incapable, not capable. A third man, whom we told: "Carry this stone," took it up as if it were a feather. This one is strong; is he also capable? Yes, and all the more so.

﴿And if He touches you with good, then He is Able to do all things﴾. "All things": Allah is capable of them. Even if something seems far-fetched in your mind, Allah is capable of it. For this reason Allah, Blessed and Exalted, reminded Zakariyya when he said: ﴿My Lord, how can I have a son when my wife is barren and I have reached extreme old age?﴾ [Maryam 8]. Allah said to him: ﴿So it will be; your Lord says: It is easy for Me, and I created you before, when you were nothing﴾ [Maryam 9]. He said: No, I created you before when you were nothing, and He is capable of creating a son for you, is it not so?

This is a clear argument from the greater to the lesser, or at least a clear argument of equivalence: the One Able to bring to non-existence is Able to bring into existence, and the One Able to bring into existence is Able to bring to non-existence.

So, my brother, do not consider it too much to ask Allah, Blessed and Exalted, for anything that does not involve transgression in supplication, even if it seems distant in your view, for Allah is Able to do all things.

And He is the Subduer over His servants, and He is the All-Wise, All-Aware.

﴿Huwa﴾ (He) refers to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and its antecedent is what precedes in the verse.

﴿Al-Qahir fawqa 'ibadihi﴾ (the Subduer over His servants): al-qahr is dominance together with authority (al-sultah), meaning power; for the one who is merely overpowering may have no authority, whereas the subjugation (qahr) of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is dominance together with complete authority.

As for His saying ﴿fawqa 'ibadihi﴾ (over His servants): is the intended meaning elevation of rank, elevation of place, or both? Yes, both: elevation of place and elevation of rank. Accordingly, the meaning is: the Subduer over His servants; in terms of meaning, no power can overcome Him, and in terms of place, He is above everything.

As for His saying ﴿'ibadihi﴾ (His servants): it is the plural of ʿabd, and what is intended here is the general servitude (al-ʿubudiyyah al-ʿammah) which includes both the believer and the disbeliever. Servitude has three categories: general, particular, and most particular (akhass). The general is the servitude of all created beings being humbled before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, so they are all worshipful. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿There is none in the heavens and the earth but that he comes to the Most Merciful as a servant﴾ [Maryam 93]. The particular is the servitude of the believers, as in the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth in humility﴾ [al-Furqan 63]. The most particular servitude is that of the messengers, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And certainly has Our word preceded for Our servants, the messengers. Indeed, they would be the ones given victory. And indeed, Our soldiers – they will be the predominant﴾ [as-Saffat 171–173]. So here there are three categories. Brother, may Allah bless you, explain them to us: is ﴿al-Qahir fawqa 'ibadihi﴾ here the general or the particular?

* Student: General.

* The Shaykh: General. Know that the particular is included within the general; that is, they are servants of Allah in both the servitude of decree (al-ʿubudiyyah al-qadariyyah) and the servitude of law (al-ʿubudiyyah al-shariyyah).

So ﴿al-Qahir fawqa 'ibadihi﴾ means the servitude of decree; everyone is subject to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Even if one is among the harshest of Allah's servants, he is a servant of Allah.
