* Shaykh: What is meant by it?
* Student: (...) they have no doubt (...).
* Shaykh: That they have no doubt that this is the truth, so the proof has been established against them.
﴿Those who have lost themselves, they do not believe﴾. Is not the absence of faith before the loss? How is the loss mentioned before the consequent ruling?
* Student: The result is upon him.
* Shaykh: That is, those whom Allah has decreed to be losers will not believe, so they do not believe.

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie against Allah or denies His signs?﴾
That is: no one is more unjust than one who invents a lie against Allah or denies His signs. These are two categories: the first lies against Allah, and the second denies the signs of Allah. No one is more unjust than them, and whoever combines both is worse.
﴿One who invents a lie against Allah﴾ by saying: "Allah has a son" — this is inventing a lie against Allah; or saying: "Allah has a partner" — this is inventing a lie against Allah; or saying: "This universe was not created by Allah," inventing a lie against Allah, if he says: "Nature created it" and the like.
﴿Or denies His signs﴾: i.e., denies the signs that indicate that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is true. Cosmic or legislative? Both: he denies the cosmic signs or the legislative signs.
Denial of the cosmic signs is to deny that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created them, or to deny that Allah, Exalted, alone created them. Denial of the legislative signs is to deny the sending of the messengers with the revelation they brought.

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed﴾ — ﴿indeed He﴾ is a judgment upon whoever invents a lie against Allah or denies His signs. But He did not say "they," rather He used the apparent noun in place of the pronoun to generalize, so that it includes them and others.
Success (falah) is salvation and attainment of what is sought, so the wrongdoer will not be saved and will not succeed.

* In this noble verse there are benefits. Among them: injustice varies; some of it is more severe than others. Why? Because sins vary; some are greater than others. There are major sins and minor sins, and major sins themselves vary, some being the greatest of major sins and what is below them. Minor sins also vary. So from where do we know that forbidden deeds vary in injustice? Because every forbidden act or abandonment of an obligation is an injustice, and if it varies, it follows that the deeds vary.
* Among the benefits of the verse: a warning against a person inventing lies against Allah, since it shows that it is in the highest rank of injustice. Among this—that is, inventing lies against Allah—is that a person lies against his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, regarding the meaning of His signs, saying: "Allah intended such-and-such," and this is a lie against Allah. Among it is that he invents a lie against Allah regarding His rulings, saying: "This is lawful and this is unlawful," as Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿And do not say, concerning what your tongues describe falsely, "This is lawful and this is unlawful," to invent lies against Allah﴾ [al-Nahl 116]. Accordingly, whoever says that the meaning of ﴿He rose over the Throne﴾ [al-A'raf 54] is "He seized the Throne" — does he enter the verse or not? He undoubtedly enters the verse, because he has invented a lie against Allah.
Whoever says: "This thing is forbidden," when it is lawful, has invented a lie against Allah.
Whoever says: "This is lawful," when it is forbidden, has invented a lie against Allah.
So the principle regarding inventing lies against Allah is that one distorts His signs to meanings He did not intend, or speaks of rulings Allah has not decreed.
Among this is takfir: if one says: "This is disbelief" when it is not disbelief, he has invented a lie against Allah, because takfir is a legal ruling. By what is it established? By the Book and the Sunnah. Takfir is not left to people: whoever wills declares takfir and whoever wills does not. Rather, takfir is referred to Allah and His Messenger. Whoever Allah and His Messenger declare to be a disbeliever, we must declare him a disbeliever, and whoever Allah and His Messenger negate disbelief from, we must negate disbelief from him.
If someone says: "There are general expressions in some rulings that are called disbelief; how do we know whether it is major or minor disbelief?" We know that by the general principles of the Sharia, and the ruling of disbelief is applied to these principles, and thereby it becomes clear whether it is major or minor. Since declaring rulers to be disbelievers is among the gravest matters, the Prophet (ﷺ) forbade rebellion against them unless we see clear, manifest disbelief for which we have a proof from Allah.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the magnitude of the injustice of one who denies the signs of Allah, since he has entered the highest class of injustice: ﴿And who is more unjust﴾.
* And among them: he is not judged as unjust, or as being in the highest rank, unless the signs have been made clear to him. He denied the signs of Allah, and Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿And Allah would not mislead a people after He has guided them until He has made clear to them what they should avoid﴾ [al-Tawbah 115]. So when He has made clear to them what they should avoid, He judges them to be astray, Glorified and Exalted is He; otherwise they have an excuse.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the obligation to affirm all of Allah's signs, cosmic and legislative. The reason is that "signs" (ayat) is in construct form, and a plural in construct form indicates generality.
* A branch of this benefit: whoever believes in some and disbelieves in others has disbelieved in all, and is not considered a believer. Some people believe and affirm what their reason sees as true and deny what they see as untrue, or believe what they find suitable and reject its opposite. Allah has stated their ruling: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers, and want to differentiate between Allah and His messengers, and say, "We believe in some and disbelieve in others," and want to adopt a way between that — those are the disbelievers in truth. And We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment﴾ [al-Nisa' 150-151].
And Allah, Exalted, rebuking the Children of Israel, said: ﴿Do you believe in part of the Book and disbelieve in part?﴾ [al-Baqarah 85]. And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made clear that whoever disbelieves in one messenger has disbelieved in all, saying: ﴿The people of Noah denied the messengers﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 105], though the people of Noah were the first to whom messengers were sent. So be attentive to this. It is not possible for a person to divide the Sharia, believing in part and disbelieving in part, because we know that such a person follows only his own desires.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the negation of success from the wrongdoer, i.e., what he seeks cannot be achieved for him; rather, the opposite occurs.

If someone asks: what is the reconciliation between this noble verse and other texts that indicate that some act is the most unjust of things, such as His saying: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who prevents the mosques of Allah from having His name mentioned in them﴾ [al-Baqarah 114], and here He says: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie against Allah﴾, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said, relating from his Lord in a hadith qudsi: «Who is more unjust than one who goes to create like My creation» [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (7559) and Muslim (2111/101), from Abu Hurayrah] regarding image-makers. How do we reconcile these texts?

The answer is from one of two angles. Either we say: these things share the highest rank of injustice, so all of them are in the status of "most unjust." Or it is said: the "most unjust" is relative. For example, here ﴿who is more unjust than one who invents a lie against Allah﴾ is said relative to those who invent lies against others.
The last angle is that we say: this is a relative superlative. The meaning is: among those who invent lies against others, who is more unjust than one who invents a lie against Allah? No one. That is: he invents a lie against, for example, Zayd, or so-and-so, and this is undoubtedly forbidden, but the most unjust thing is to invent a lie against Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
﴿And who is more unjust than one who prevents the mosques of Allah from having His name mentioned in them﴾ [al-Baqarah 114] is a relative superlative. That is: any person who prevents people from a right they have—who is more unjust than one who prevents their right to the mosques? For example, you may prevent this man from entering the school; is this worse, or preventing him from entering the mosque? The second. You may prevent him from entering the market; this is injustice, but which is more unjust, this or one who prevents the mosques of Allah? The second.
In the matter of image-making: "Who is more unjust than one who goes to create like My creation" — i.e., those who imitate others in making images when done in a manner of injustice. So who is more unjust than one who goes to create like the creation of Allah? No one. This is one angle.
The first angle you have also known, or have you not known it? That they all share in being "most unjust," i.e., in the highest rank of injustice.

Another difficulty: ﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed﴾. We mentioned that the wrongdoer does not succeed, and this benefit includes good news for the oppressed: that the wrongdoer will not succeed. So the fighters are given glad tidings of victory, and the end of those who oppose them is failure. And whoever is wronged by having his wealth taken or denied, and the like, is given glad tidings that this wrongdoer will not succeed.
But if someone says: what is the reconciliation between this verse and reality, since we see that the wrongdoer may succeed?
The reconciliation with reality is to say: success is of two kinds. Absolute success: this is never possible for the wrongdoer. The proof is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): «Indeed Allah gives respite to the wrongdoer until when He seizes him, He does not let him go», and he recited His saying: ﴿And thus is the seizing of your Lord when He seizes the cities while they are committing wrong. Indeed, His seizure is painful and severe﴾ [Hud 102] [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4686) and Muslim (2583/61), from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari]. So the wrongdoer must stumble; he must lose, whether the worldly life is long or short. This is absolute success. Success in a particular time, place, or matter is what may occur without contradicting the verse, because Allah, Exalted, may give the wrongdoer a success so that he is deceived by it and persists in his transgression, and then Allah breaks his back.
Allah, Exalted, indicated this in Surah Al 'Imran: ﴿And that Allah may purify those who believe and destroy the disbelievers﴾ [Al 'Imran 141]. He purifies them through expiation of sins for what befell them of defeat, and purifies them so they do not return to disobedience a second time. ﴿And destroy the disbelievers﴾: how does He destroy the disbelievers when they are victorious?
Because when the disbeliever is victorious, he becomes audacious, boastful, and proud. So the wrongdoer may succeed, but with a restricted success, for a wisdom or wisdoms that we do not know, but Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knows.
What is our position if the wrongdoer is given power over us? Our position is to be patient, not to despair, and to await relief from the Creator of the earth and the heavens, for patience is the key to relief, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: «Know that victory comes with patience, relief comes with distress, and with hardship comes ease» [narrated by Ahmad (2803), from Ibn 'Abbas].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: warning against injustice, and that its consequence is loss and ruin, by His saying: ﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed﴾. May Allah protect us and you from injustice, and make us among the successful, the pious, and the doers of good.

* Student: Shaykh, may Allah bless you. Sometimes some people, especially those who are not students of knowledge but who are committed and want to show their zeal for Islam, begin speaking about the rulers, and show that they are enraged and wish for their removal and the like, from things which, as we have studied, contradict the evidences and also contradict the requirements of reason. What is the correct position for students of knowledge, since they also speak about students of knowledge, and some of them endorse it, or even encourage it? What is the obligation of a student of knowledge in such a situation?
* Shaykh: The obligation upon a student of knowledge is to clarify what the evidence requires of hearing and obeying the rulers, unless they are commanded to disobey, and what the evidences require of the obligation to refrain from their faults. And whoever wishes to give advice, the path to it is open.
* Student: Some argue: "If I forbid them, I accustom them to cowardice and humiliation." May Allah reward him with good, he has shown his love for Islam and the religion; in whatever form he does it, he says: "Leave him."
* Shaykh: Yes, we say: there is no harm; dignity of the self is obligatory. But dignity of the self must be according to the requirements of the Sharia, so that it is balanced; otherwise each would want his own dignity, and this one wants his own dignity, and that one wants his own dignity, and there would be chaos. There is evidence for this, and perhaps you and others have also fallen into such a situation, where he confronted people in this state. So the obligation is to give advice, and to cite as examples the trials that have occurred, the shedding of blood, and the plundering of wealth.

Otherwise, this one would want "ʿizzat al-nafs" (self-dignity), and that one would want "ʿizzat al-nafs," and this one would want "ʿizzat al-nafs," and there would be chaos. There is evidence for this. Perhaps you and others have also fallen into something similar: he confronted people in this state. So the obligation is to give advice, and to cite as examples for these people what has resulted from the calamity, the shedding of blood, and the plundering of wealth among those who have taken this path, from the time of the Kharijites against ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, and Muʿawiyah, until our present day.

* Student: May Allah pardon you, O Shaykh. Sins do have an effect, and they have a quality (...) of punishment, because a person is punished by the sins that cause him a punishment from Allah, the Exalted, and it becomes good for him. Like the sick person, O Shaykh; were it not for some people, but not all people, the illness (...) the sick person remembered Allah and returned to his Lord. When Allah grants him health, he forgets what he was in before. Among them, O Shaykh, is what happened to the Companions at the Battle of Uhud and the Battle of Hunayn, O Shaykh. Some of them disobeyed the Messenger (ﷺ), and Allah, the Exalted, punished them with defeat, and He punished them when they became conceited by their large numbers at Hunayn.

* The Shaykh: Yes indeed, that is correct. This is from the wisdom of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: this army, which is the noblest army on the face of the earth since Adam was created, suffered defeat because of a single act of disobedience. So what about the sins that have filled the atmosphere?

Second: they suffered defeat because of their pride in their number and multitude, and they were the noblest army on the face of the earth from the creation of Adam until the Hour is established. This is an admonition for us: if we want to be victorious over our enemies, it is absolutely not permissible for us to immerse ourselves in sins. Some of us are immersed in atheism and disbelief, and Allah forbid, in allegiance to the disbelievers and supporting them. How can victory come? So in reality, these are two great examples through which lessons are drawn, from the wisdom of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and so on with these matters.

* Student: Shaykh, may Allah preserve you, there are some oppressors whom we see do not receive any punishment even at the end of their lives. So is punishment here necessarily something that reaches them in this world, or...?

* The Shaykh: If he is an oppressor for a principle among the principles, then that principle must be humiliated even after his death. If it is a personal matter, then even if it does not happen in this world as far as we see, he will face it in the Hereafter. Perhaps there are things in the heart of the oppressor that we do not know about, with which he is tested: such as constriction of the chest, aversion to the truth, and similar things.

* Student: May Allah reward you well. We said: among lying about Allah is lying about the implications of the evidences. And if a person errs in the implication of a verse, there is no (...) its root.

* The Shaykh: This, may Allah bless you, if he speaks about the interpretation of the verse, we examine: is it based on a legal rule? Does this match what the language requires or what the Shariah requires? If he errs, he is forgiven after exerting effort. But if he is obstinate and says, "The intended meaning is such-and-such," then he has no excuse.

* The Student: He wants to explain to people while he is not qualified for it.

* The Shaykh: No, it is not permissible, especially the Qur'an. If you report the meaning of a verse, you have testified that Allah intended this. This is a serious matter.

* Student: What is the criterion for supporting the disbelievers such that it becomes one of the nullifiers of Islam?

* The Shaykh: Supporting them is that he supports them in their disbelief. That is the support.

* Student: Like congratulating the disbelievers?

* The Shaykh: Yes indeed.

* Student: Such as that they have settled in the lands of the Muslims and established themselves there, so some of them congratulate one another?

* The Shaykh: No, this is haram; it is not permissible.

* Student: Is this considered a nullifier?

* The Shaykh: This is haram. The matter of nullifiers, we do not discuss it, because it requires clarification. But there is no doubt that one who congratulates the disbelievers on occupying the lands of the Muslims is in grave danger. We ask Allah for well-being.

Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And the day We gather them all together﴾ [al-An'am 22]. ﴿Yawm (the day)﴾ is an adverbial complement (zarf), and it is well known that a zarf and a prepositional phrase (jar wa majrur) must have something they depend on (muta'allaq), as the author of al-Jumal said:

"There must be, for the prepositional phrase, a dependent element,
either a verb or its equivalent in meaning, such as 'murtaqi' (climbing)."
"Except every extra particle, which has no governing effect,
such as the ba', min, the kaf, and also la'alla."

So where is the dependent element of ﴿yawm﴾? It is omitted. The estimated meaning is: "Remember the day We gather them." Is it: "Remember [this] to yourself," or "Remember it to them"?

The answer is the second, though it is also permissible to say: "Remember it to yourself, so that you may be consoled by this reminder and their affair becomes easy for you."

﴿Nahshuruhum﴾ means: We gather them.

﴿Jami'an (all together)﴾: not one of them will escape.

﴿Then We will say to those who associated partners [with Allah]: "Where are your partners whom you used to claim?"﴾ [al-An'am 22]. ﴿Naqulu lil-ladhina ashraku (We will say to those who associated)﴾ means: with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in the world.

﴿Ayna shuraka'ukum (Where are your partners?)﴾: the interrogative here is for rebuke and reproach, since it is known that they will not come; rather it is to rebuke and reproach them, and to make them regret that they will not benefit from them.

﴿Shuraka'ukum (your partners)﴾ means: those you associated with Allah, Mighty and Majestic. We know that the polytheists were of various kinds and categories: among them were those who associated with Allah a stone, or a tree, or the moon, or a star. The point is that they varied.

So it is said: ﴿Where are your partners whom you used to claim?﴾ meaning: you claimed that they were gods, and a god benefits whoever worships him. So where are they?

The answer: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, explained it. ﴿Then﴾ means: after this question, ﴿their trial (fitnatuhum) was only that they said: "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists."﴾ [al-An'am 23]. ((Al-fitna)) here means ((the proof/argument)).

﴿Then their fitna was not﴾ means: their argument.

﴿Only that they said: "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists"﴾: they swore by Allah that they had not been polytheists. Were they truthful in this oath?

No. For this reason He said: ﴿See how they lied against themselves﴾ [al-An'am 24]. Look, O addressee, at how they lied against themselves. Here there is a difficulty: ﴿how they lied against themselves﴾ and we were commanded to look, and the intended looking here is the looking of contemplation (i'tibar). But how can He say ﴿they lied against themselves﴾ when the matter has not yet come, since this will be on the Day of Resurrection?

The answer: this is the narration of a present state (hikayat al-hal). Allah, Mighty and Majestic, always relates future things so that a person imagines them as though they had already happened, because a certain future event is as if it were entirely present. For this reason Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿The command of Allah has come, so do not seek to hasten it﴾ [al-Nahl 1], although it had not yet come, as is shown by His saying: ﴿so do not seek to hasten it﴾. So the past tense is used for narrating a present state, so that a person imagines the thing as though it were before his eyes.

﴿They lied against themselves﴾ by their saying: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists.﴾

Then He said: ﴿See how they lied against themselves, and what they used to fabricate has gone astray from them﴾. ((Dalla)) means: it was lost and they did not find it, like a man whose wealth is lost and he does not find it. These people lost their gods and did not find them.

And His saying: ﴿what they used to fabricate﴾ means: what they used to fabricate of their claim that these were gods besides Allah, for this is among the greatest fabrication, as was mentioned in the verse two verses before.

Returning to the readings of this verse. He says: ﴿Then their fitna was not (lam takun)...﴾. I have the readings: ﴿lam yakun fitnatuhum illa an qalu﴾, and the reading in the Mushaf is ﴿lam takun fitnatuhum illa an qalu﴾. The difference lies in the verb, in the subject of (kana), and in the predicate of (kana). The verb instead of ﴿takun﴾ is ﴿yakun﴾, why? Because the subject of kana in this reading is masculine, namely His saying ﴿illa an qalu﴾, since the meaning is: their fitna was not except their saying.

The second: ﴿wallahi rabbana﴾ is a reading meaning: "By Allah, O our Lord, we were not polytheists." This variation in the readings, O my brothers, does no harm, because in the earlier first generation they did not vocalize the letters nor add dots to them, meaning they did not put a single dot or two dots, above or below, so that the two readings are identical in the written script and differ only in pronunciation, and in the pointing and inflection that came later after the Qur'an was pointed and given its inflection.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: consolation to the Prophet (ﷺ), since the outcome of those who denied him is mentioned to him.

* Among its benefits: a warning against shirk, since the polytheist will be rebuked on a day when he cannot escape.

* Among its benefits: the affirmation of the Day of Resurrection, the Day of Gathering.

* Among its benefits: that the gathering is general and comprehensive, with no one exempt from it, neither believer nor disbeliever, neither righteous nor wicked, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, emphasized it by His saying ﴿all together﴾.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of speech for Allah, from His saying ﴿Then We will say to those who associated: "Where are your partners?"﴾. A disputant may argue and say that the speaker is the angels, and Allah attributed their speech to Himself because they are His messengers speaking by His command, as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿So when We recite it, follow its recitation﴾ [al-Qiyama 18], although the reciter is Jibril.

We say: this is certainly possible, that the one who says this to these polytheists may be angels, and Allah attributed it to Himself because they speak by His command. But what is the apparent meaning of the Qur'an? That the speaker is Allah, Mighty and Majestic. And if this is the apparent meaning of the Qur'an, we have no alternative to it, because Allah will call us to account on the Day of Resurrection: He says the words, then we say, so how can it be diverted to mean the angels without evidence? It is obligatory to take the apparent meaning of the Qur'an unless evidence is found; if evidence is found that moves the speech from its apparent meaning, then it is accepted with all respect. The main point here is the affirmation that Allah speaks.

If one asks: Does He speak with audible, intelligible letters, or with other letters?

The answer: the first, without doubt.

If one asks: Does His voice resemble the voices of created beings?

The answer: No, because Allah says: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾ [al-Shura 11]; and because when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, speaks by revelation, the heavens are seized with a tremor and the angels swoon. Such a thing never occurs in the speech of the children of Adam, nor in the speech of created beings in general; it is impossible.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the rebuke of those polytheists, since they are addressed in this great assembly with: ﴿Where are your partners?﴾

* Among its benefits: this verse shows that the idols do not benefit their worshippers, because they do not help them in this situation. Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Indeed you and what you worship besides Allah are fuel for Hell﴾ — you will be cast into its midst — ﴿you will be going into it. Had these been gods, they would not have gone into it﴾ [al-Anbiya 98–99]. Look at this verse: the polytheists rejoiced at it and seized the opportunity, saying: "This Muhammad says that the things worshipped are in the Fire, and Jesus is worshipped, so Jesus must be in the Fire." Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the good has preceded from Us, they will be kept far from it﴾ [al-Anbiya 101].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that those who worship these idols have no proof or evidence, but only a mere claim, taken from His saying ﴿you claimed (tazAAmun)﴾, and "zaʿm" in most cases is a statement for which there is no evidence.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse that follows: ﴿Then their fitna was not except that they said﴾ to the end. Among its benefits: those people were tested by this answer, found it pleasing, and considered it beneficial, namely: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists.﴾

* Following from this benefit: a person may be tested by something, so that he sees truth as falsehood and falsehood as truth. So protect yourself from this trial, hold yourself accountable for it, and seek refuge in Allah from being among its people.

* Among its benefits: the acknowledgment by these polytheists of Allah's divinity and lordship: their divinity in their saying ﴿By Allah (wallahi)﴾, and their lordship in their saying ﴿our Lord (rabbana)﴾. But does this benefit them? At that time it does not benefit them; indeed it would not benefit them even had they affirmed Allah's oneness when death descended upon them, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And repentance is not for those who do evil deeds until, when death comes to one of them, he says, "Indeed I have now repented"﴾ [al-Nisa 18].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that what they fabricated as partners of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will go astray from them despite their intense search for it, just as a lost animal strays from its owner; by His saying ﴿and what they used to fabricate has gone astray from them﴾.

If one asks: How can we reconcile this noble verse, where they say ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists,﴾ with His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿On that Day those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth were leveled over them, and they will not conceal from Allah any statement﴾ [al-Nisa 42]? As for the Qur'an, there is no contradiction in it, and it is impossible for it to contradict. Scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, have composed works on this great question, among them the work of Shaykh Muhammad al-Shanqiti, may Allah have mercy on him, the well-known exegete and jurist of usul: Daf' Iham al-Idtirab fi Ayat al-Kitab (Removing the Appearance of Disorder in the Verses of the Book). Contradiction is absolutely impossible; if you see a contradiction, the flaw is from you: either from deficiency of understanding, or negligence in seeking, or bad intention, wishing to search for things whose apparent meaning is conflict in order to discredit the Qur'an, or from deficiency of knowledge. Otherwise there is no contradiction. Here we say: the Day of Resurrection is fifty thousand years long, and people have various states in it. In one state they deny that they were polytheists, and in another state they acknowledge it. When they see that the people of monotheism have been saved, they say: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists.﴾ But when their mouths are sealed and their hands and feet testify to what they used to earn, then they acknowledge, because it is impossible for them to deny in the presence of witnesses from themselves.

Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And the day We gather them all together﴾ [al-An'am 22]. ﴿Yawm (the day)﴾ is an adverbial complement (zarf), and it is well known that a zarf and a prepositional phrase (jar wa majrur) must have something they depend on (muta'allaq), as the author of al-Jumal said:

"There must be, for the prepositional phrase, a dependent element,
either a verb or its equivalent in meaning, such as 'murtaqi' (climbing)."
"Except every extra particle, which has no governing effect,
such as the ba', min, the kaf, and also la'alla."

So where is the dependent element of ﴿yawm﴾? It is omitted. The estimated meaning is: "Remember the day We gather them." Is it: "Remember [this] to yourself," or "Remember it to them"?

The answer is the second, though it is also permissible to say: "Remember it to yourself, so that you may be consoled by this reminder and their affair becomes easy for you."

﴿Nahshuruhum﴾ means: We gather them.

﴿Jami'an (all together)﴾: not one of them will escape.

﴿Then We will say to those who associated partners [with Allah]: "Where are your partners whom you used to claim?"﴾ [al-An'am 22]. ﴿Naqulu lil-ladhina ashraku (We will say to those who associated)﴾ means: with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in the world.

﴿Ayna shuraka'ukum (Where are your partners?)﴾: the interrogative here is for rebuke and reproach, since it is known that they will not come; rather it is to rebuke and reproach them, and to make them regret that they will not benefit from them.

﴿Shuraka'ukum (your partners)﴾ means: those you associated with Allah, Mighty and Majestic. We know that the polytheists were of various kinds and categories: among them were those who associated with Allah a stone, or a tree, or the moon, or a star. The point is that they varied.

So it is said: ﴿Where are your partners whom you used to claim?﴾ meaning: you claimed that they were gods, and a god benefits whoever worships him. So where are they?

The answer: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, explained it. ﴿Then﴾ means: after this question, ﴿their trial (fitnatuhum) was only that they said: "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists."﴾ [al-An'am 23]. ((Al-fitna)) here means ((the proof/argument)).

﴿Then their fitna was not﴾ means: their argument.

﴿Only that they said: "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists"﴾: they swore by Allah that they had not been polytheists. Were they truthful in this oath?

No. For this reason He said: ﴿See how they lied against themselves﴾ [al-An'am 24]. Look, O addressee, at how they lied against themselves. Here there is a difficulty: ﴿how they lied against themselves﴾ and we were commanded to look, and the intended looking here is the looking of contemplation (i'tibar). But how can He say ﴿they lied against themselves﴾ when the matter has not yet come, since this will be on the Day of Resurrection?

The answer: this is the narration of a present state (hikayat al-hal). Allah, Mighty and Majestic, always relates future things so that a person imagines them as though they had already happened, because a certain future event is as if it were entirely present. For this reason Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿The command of Allah has come, so do not seek to hasten it﴾ [al-Nahl 1], although it had not yet come, as is shown by His saying: ﴿so do not seek to hasten it﴾. So the past tense is used for narrating a present state, so that a person imagines the thing as though it were before his eyes.

﴿They lied against themselves﴾ by their saying: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists.﴾

Then He said: ﴿See how they lied against themselves, and what they used to fabricate has gone astray from them﴾. ((Dalla)) means: it was lost and they did not find it, like a man whose wealth is lost and he does not find it. These people lost their gods and did not find them.

And His saying: ﴿what they used to fabricate﴾ means: what they used to fabricate of their claim that these were gods besides Allah, for this is among the greatest fabrication, as was mentioned in the verse two verses before.

Returning to the readings of this verse. He says: ﴿Then their fitna was not (lam takun)...﴾. I have the readings: ﴿lam yakun fitnatuhum illa an qalu﴾, and the reading in the Mushaf is ﴿lam takun fitnatuhum illa an qalu﴾. The difference lies in the verb, in the subject of (kana), and in the predicate of (kana). The verb instead of ﴿takun﴾ is ﴿yakun﴾, why? Because the subject of kana in this reading is masculine, namely His saying ﴿illa an qalu﴾, since the meaning is: their fitna was not except their saying.

The second: ﴿wallahi rabbana﴾ is a reading meaning: "By Allah, O our Lord, we were not polytheists." This variation in the readings, O my brothers, does no harm, because in the earlier first generation they did not vocalize the letters nor add dots to them, meaning they did not put a single dot or two dots, above or below, so that the two readings are identical in the written script and differ only in pronunciation, and in the pointing and inflection that came later after the Qur'an was pointed and given its inflection.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: consolation to the Prophet (ﷺ), since the outcome of those who denied him is mentioned to him.

* Among its benefits: a warning against shirk, since the polytheist will be rebuked on a day when he cannot escape.

* Among its benefits: the affirmation of the Day of Resurrection, the Day of Gathering.

* Among its benefits: that the gathering is general and comprehensive, with no one exempt from it, neither believer nor disbeliever, neither righteous nor wicked, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, emphasized it by His saying ﴿all together﴾.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of speech for Allah, from His saying ﴿Then We will say to those who associated: "Where are your partners?"﴾. A disputant may argue and say that the speaker is the angels, and Allah attributed their speech to Himself because they are His messengers speaking by His command, as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿So when We recite it, follow its recitation﴾ [al-Qiyama 18], although the reciter is Jibril.

We say: this is certainly possible, that the one who says this to these polytheists may be angels, and Allah attributed it to Himself because they speak by His command. But what is the apparent meaning of the Qur'an? That the speaker is Allah, Mighty and Majestic. And if this is the apparent meaning of the Qur'an, we have no alternative to it, because Allah will call us to account on the Day of Resurrection: He says the words, then we say, so how can it be diverted to mean the angels without evidence? It is obligatory to take the apparent meaning of the Qur'an unless evidence is found; if evidence is found that moves the speech from its apparent meaning, then it is accepted with all respect. The main point here is the affirmation that Allah speaks.

If one asks: Does He speak with audible, intelligible letters, or with other letters?

The answer: the first, without doubt.

If one asks: Does His voice resemble the voices of created beings?

The answer: No, because Allah says: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾ [al-Shura 11]; and because when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, speaks by revelation, the heavens are seized with a tremor and the angels swoon. Such a thing never occurs in the speech of the children of Adam, nor in the speech of created beings in general; it is impossible.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the rebuke of those polytheists, since they are addressed in this great assembly with: ﴿Where are your partners?﴾

* Among its benefits: this verse shows that the idols do not benefit their worshippers, because they do not help them in this situation. Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Indeed you and what you worship besides Allah are fuel for Hell﴾ — you will be cast into its midst — ﴿you will be going into it. Had these been gods, they would not have gone into it﴾ [al-Anbiya 98–99]. Look at this verse: the polytheists rejoiced at it and seized the opportunity, saying: "This Muhammad says that the things worshipped are in the Fire, and Jesus is worshipped, so Jesus must be in the Fire." Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the good has preceded from Us, they will be kept far from it﴾ [al-Anbiya 101].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that those who worship these idols have no proof or evidence, but only a mere claim, taken from His saying ﴿you claimed (tazAAmun)﴾, and "zaʿm" in most cases is a statement for which there is no evidence.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse that follows: ﴿Then their fitna was not except that they said﴾ to the end. Among its benefits: those people were tested by this answer, found it pleasing, and considered it beneficial, namely: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists.﴾

* Following from this benefit: a person may be tested by something, so that he sees truth as falsehood and falsehood as truth. So protect yourself from this trial, hold yourself accountable for it, and seek refuge in Allah from being among its people.

* Among its benefits: the acknowledgment by these polytheists of Allah's divinity and lordship: their divinity in their saying ﴿By Allah (wallahi)﴾, and their lordship in their saying ﴿our Lord (rabbana)﴾. But does this benefit them? At that time it does not benefit them; indeed it would not benefit them even had they affirmed Allah's oneness when death descended upon them, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And repentance is not for those who do evil deeds until, when death comes to one of them, he says, "Indeed I have now repented"﴾ [al-Nisa 18].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that what they fabricated as partners of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will go astray from them despite their intense search for it, just as a lost animal strays from its owner; by His saying ﴿and what they used to fabricate has gone astray from them﴾.

If one asks: How can we reconcile this noble verse, where they say ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists,﴾ with His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿On that Day those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth were leveled over them, and they will not conceal from Allah any statement﴾ [al-Nisa 42]? This verse declares that they will not conceal from Allah any statement, yet here they concealed it? They said: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists.﴾

The answer: First, we must know, believe, and be certain that there is no contradiction in the Qur'an at all. Contradiction lies in a person's understanding due to his deficiency. As for the Qur'an, there is no contradiction in it, and it is impossible for it to contradict. Scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, have composed works on this great question, among them the work of Shaykh Muhammad al-Shanqiti, may Allah have mercy on him, the well-known exegete and jurist of usul: Daf' Iham al-Idtirab fi Ayat al-Kitab (Removing the Appearance of Disorder in the Verses of the Book). Contradiction is absolutely impossible; if you see a contradiction, the flaw is from you: either from deficiency of understanding, or negligence in seeking, or bad intention, wishing to search for things whose apparent meaning is conflict in order to discredit the Qur'an, or from deficiency of knowledge. Otherwise there is no contradiction. Here we say: the Day of Resurrection is fifty thousand years long, and people have various states in it. In one state they deny that they were polytheists, and in another state they acknowledge it. When they see that the people of monotheism have been saved, they say: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists.﴾ But when their mouths are sealed and their hands and feet testify to what they used to earn, then they acknowledge, because it is impossible for them to deny in the presence of witnesses from themselves.

Then He said: ﴿And among them are some who listen to you﴾, to the end of the verse [al-An'am 25]. ﴿Min﴾ (among) here is partitive (tab'idiyyah), and its sign is that some (ba'd) can take its place; that is, "some of them who listen to you."

﴿Yastami'u﴾ (listens) here is in the singular form, observing the wording of ﴿man﴾ (who). This is because the relative pronoun ﴿man﴾ may be treated either according to its meaning or according to its wording. When its meaning is observed, the pronoun referring back to it follows what is intended by the meaning; when its wording is observed, it is singular.

﴿Man yastami'u ilayk﴾ means: who attends and listens to your recitation, but they do not benefit. Therefore He said: ﴿And We have placed over their hearts coverings, lest they understand it﴾. ﴿Ja'alna﴾ (We have placed) means: We have made.

﴿Over their hearts coverings﴾: ﴿akinnah﴾ (coverings) is the plural of ﴿kinan﴾, like ﴿zimam﴾ and ﴿azimmah﴾ (reins), and it is that which covers a thing and conceals it.

As for His words ﴿lest they understand it﴾: it means the desire that they understand it, so it is by way of an omitted noun; that is, We do not desire that they understand it. If you wish, say: "out of aversion that they understand it." Some have said that it is with the implied ﴿la﴾ (not), meaning "that they not understand it." The meaning is one, but our interpreting it as "aversion" is preferable to interpreting it as "not," because when we interpret it as "not," we explain an affirmative by a negative, and this is far-fetched. When we interpret it as "aversion," this is consistent, like His saying: ﴿Allah makes clear to you, lest you go astray﴾ [an-Nisa 176], i.e., out of aversion that you go astray.

As for His words ﴿yafqahuhu﴾ (understand it): fiqh in the language means understanding, as He said: ﴿And there is not a thing but that it glorifies Him in praise, but you do not understand their glorification﴾ [al-Isra 44], i.e., you do not understand it. The meaning is that Allah placed over their hearts a protective covering against their understanding of it, so its meaning does not reach their hearts.

﴿And in their ears a deafness﴾: i.e., and We placed in their ears. ﴿Waqr﴾ (deafness) means a load and deafness, such that they gain no benefit from what they hear. Whoever gains no benefit from hearing is like one who did not hear. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, negated understanding from them, whose seat is the heart, and hearing, whose seat is the ear.

﴿And in their ears a deafness﴾: this is like His saying, blessed and exalted: ﴿When Our verses are recited to him, he says: "Tales of the ancients"﴾ [al-Qalam 15], meaning he did not understand them and did not comprehend them, and he only considers them fables, i.e., idle talk that has no meaning that reforms creation.

﴿And if they see every sign, they will not believe in it﴾: whether they see with their eyes or see with their hearts every sign, they will not: ﴿believe in it﴾. The sign (ayah) is the indicator that proves the truth of the Prophet ﷺ, as the Mighty and Majestic said in Surah al-Qamar: ﴿And if they see a sign, they turn away and say: "Continuous magic"﴾ [al-Qamar 2].

We ask Allah for guidance. A person whose heart is sealed (we seek refuge in Allah) does not believe in any sign; signs come to him like the sun, yet he does not believe, because his heart is covered and guidance does not reach it.

﴿And if they see every sign, they will not believe in it﴾: here Allah negated from them understanding, whose seat is the heart, and hearing, whose seat is the ear, and belief in the signs, whose seat is the heart, along with the sight of the eye.

﴿And if they see every sign, they will not believe in it, until when they come to you, they dispute with you﴾. ﴿Hatta﴾ (until) here indicates the limit (lil-ghayah), and it may also be inceptive (lil-ibtida'). The difference between them is that if we take it as indicating a limit, what precedes it is bounded by it, meaning that they do not benefit from the signs, until, when they come to you, they dispute with you. It may also be inceptive, and the inceptive is like the resumptive waw (wa al-isti'nafiyyah).

﴿Until when they come to you, they dispute with you, those who disbelieve say﴾, to the end. ﴿Yujadiluna﴾ (they dispute): mujadalah is contention, and it is called mujadalah because each of the two disputants twists the proof so that it stands against the other; it is taken from jadl al-habl (twisting of a rope), which is twisting it until it becomes firm and strong. They dispute with the Prophet ﷺ with the doubts they raise against him, but Allah the Most High answers them.

As for His words ﴿yujadiluna﴾, the clause is in a position of accusative as a circumstantial clause (hal) from the waw in His words ﴿jaa'uka﴾, meaning: while they are disputing with you.

﴿Those who disbelieve say﴾: this is the answer to ﴿idha﴾ (when). ﴿Yaqulu﴾ is not jussive, because the conditional ﴿idha﴾ is not a jussive particle. You say: "When Zayd comes, 'Amr comes," without jussive. As for the poet's saying:

........................... ∗∗∗ wa-idha tusibka musibatun fatahammal
this is considered an anomaly (shadh) and is not used as evidence.

﴿Those who disbelieve say: this is not but tales of the ancients﴾: this is the end.

﴿In hadha﴾ means "this is not," and that ﴿in﴾ here is negative is shown by the fact that ﴿illa﴾ (except) follows it, and when ﴿illa﴾ follows it, it is negative.

It may also come as negative without ﴿illa﴾. The word ﴿in﴾ has several meanings: it comes as conditional, as negative, as superfluous (za'idah), and as the lightened form of the heavy (mukhaffafah min al-thaqilah): four meanings.

It comes as conditional, and this is common, for example: ﴿If a good thing befalls you, it troubles them﴾ [at-Tawbah 50]. It comes as negative; example?

﴿This is not but the word of a human﴾ [al-Muddaththir 25], i.e., this is not but the word of a human. And it comes as the lightened form of the heavy?

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: No, "in," we mean "in."

* Student: ﴿And indeed, those who disbelieve almost...﴾

* The Shaykh: ﴿And indeed, those who disbelieve almost slip you with their eyes﴾ [al-Qalam 51]. The fourth, the superfluous?

* Student: "Ma in ra'aytu al-haqq hatta taba'tuhu" (I did not see the truth until I followed it).

* The Shaykh: "Ma in ra'aytu al-haqq hatta taba'tuhu," meaning I did not see the truth until I followed it; meaning I did not see it until I avoided it? Does the sentence hold?

* Student: The poet's saying:

Banu Ghudanah, you are not gold ∗∗∗ nor refined silver, but you are clay pottery.
* The Shaykh: The poet's saying:

Banu Ghudanah, you are not gold ∗∗∗ nor refined silver, but you are clay pottery.
In this noble verse: ﴿in hadha illa asatir al-awwalin﴾, ﴿in﴾ is negative.

﴿Illa asatir﴾: ﴿asatir﴾ is the plural of ﴿usturah﴾ (fable). An usturah is what people talk about in gatherings to pass the time; it has no meaning. Among the common people it is called what? Idle talk with no meaning; yet a person wants to remove boredom, laziness and to pass time.

﴿Al-awwalin﴾ means: the earlier ones.

* In this noble verse there are benefits. Among them: not every listener benefits, by His saying: ﴿And among them are some who listen to you﴾, the verse. Consider His saying, the Most High: ﴿And among them are some who listen to you, until when they leave your presence, they say to those given knowledge: "What did he just say?"﴾ [Muhammad 16]. They do not know what he said.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: a warning against listening without benefiting, that this is the practice of the disbelievers. It follows from this that when a person listens, he should reflect and ponder what he has heard, especially if it is the Book and the Sunnah, so that he understands its meaning.

* Among the benefits of this verse: that understanding has its seat in the heart, by His saying: ﴿And We have placed over their hearts coverings, lest they understand it﴾.

If someone asks: what is the cause of these coverings that veil the truth from the heart?

The answer: their cause is sins, as Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿When Our verses are recited to him, he says: "Tales of the ancients." Nay! Rather, what they used to earn has covered their hearts﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 13-14]. Sins come between a person and understanding of the religion of Allah. For this reason some scholars said: whoever is asked for a fatwa should seek Allah's forgiveness before answering, so that istighfar may erase the rust that is on the heart, and they cited the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you. And do not be an advocate for the treacherous. And seek forgiveness of Allah; indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [an-Nisa 105-106]. This is a good deduction, especially when a matter is unclear to you and you are prevented from knowing the correct ruling. Then you should seek forgiveness and supplicate, and not be hasty, because you are speaking on behalf of the Sharia of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that failing to benefit from hearing is exactly like deafness, by His saying: ﴿and in their ears is a deafness﴾ [Fussilat 44]. Indeed, the deaf person is excused, whereas one who does not benefit from what he hears is not excused, because the deaf person's lack of hearing is an affliction that befell him.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that these disbelievers neither benefit from what they hear nor from what they witness, by His saying: ﴿And if they see every sign, they will not believe in it﴾. Signs are of two kinds: cosmic signs (ayat qadariyyah) and legislative signs (ayat shar'iyyah). Among the cosmic signs are what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, brings about in the universe, such as the splitting of the moon, the winds that Allah sent upon the confederates, likewise the descent of rain and the withholding of rain, and countless other things; then the sun, the moon, the stars, the mountains, the trees and the animals are all among Allah's signs. Are they cosmic or legislative?

* Students: Cosmic.

* The Shaykh: Cosmic. As for Allah's legislative signs, they are the revelation; if you reflect upon revelation, and its most noble part is the Qur'an, you will know the great signs it contains in reports and rulings. The believer benefits, and the non-believer does not benefit, until Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And if they see a piece of the sky falling, they say: "Layered clouds"﴾ [at-Tur 44]; they do not believe it is a punishment. Among this is what happens in our time: storms, catastrophes, floods and earthquakes, which for some people are natural matters that do not indicate threat and warning. That is from the rust on the hearts (we ask Allah for well-being), and from resembling the disbelievers in that they: ﴿if they see every sign, they will not believe in it﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sends signs in support of the messengers and as a warning to their opponents, as the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿They say: "Why was no sign sent down upon him from his Lord?" Say: "Signs are only with Allah, and I am only a clear warner." Is it not sufficient for them that We have sent down to you the Book being recited to them?﴾ [al-Ankabut 50-51]. And the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And We did not send the signs except as a warning﴾ [al-Isra 59]. So the signs Allah sends are support for the messengers and a warning to their opponents; but, as we said, these opponents, we ask Allah for well-being, do not benefit from the signs, and so they do not believe in them.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the disbelievers dispute with the Muslims, dispute with the Prophet ﷺ, and dispute with those who follow the Prophet, but with what?

With falsehood, in order to refute the truth. But the owner of the truth, who is worthy of it, should be given good news that victory is his, by the saying of Allah the Most High: ﴿Rather, We hurl the truth against falsehood, and it crushes it, and behold, it vanishes. And woe to you for what you describe﴾ [al-Anbiya 18]. But this requires two things: a sincere intention and knowledge with which to repel the arguer's doubt. It is not permissible for a person to enter into a dispute with a man of falsehood while he has no knowledge, for if he did, the defeat would fall on whom? On the truth. So do not enter into a dispute with a person unless you know how to hit him while being sincere in intention. As for entering a dispute with a person of eloquent speech and strong doubts, do not do so, for if you do, you will be defeated, and your defeat will be a defeat of the truth you are defending.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that a person should learn the methods of disputation, by His saying: ﴿until when they come to you, they dispute with you﴾. So learn, brother, the methods of disputation in order to dispute with them in support of the truth. It may be said that from this follows the claim spread by some people that there is no need to revisit the disputation of the speculative theologians (mutakallimun) such as the Ash'aris, the Mu'tazilis and their likes, since their time has passed; this is a clear delusion.

Firstly: their time has not ended; they still exist: Mu'tazilis, Jahmis, Ash'aris, Khawarij, Shi'is, all still exist.

Secondly: the methods of disputation with these groups benefit a person in disputing with others, because they open for a person the doors of argument, and he learns how to overcome his opponent with what he argues. Furthermore, as for our country here in Saudi Arabia, we did not know much of these sects; but since we have mixed with people, going to them and they coming to us, this thing has appeared, and some innovations have appeared; otherwise people would not know anything of this except those who read books. Therefore we say: reading about disputation with the speculative theologians has benefit without doubt, but it is better that you read it while you are weak in knowledge? No; for if you did, what would happen? You would be led astray. You must have a protection with which you shield yourself.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the one who disputes with falsehood resorts to obstinacy or to threats if he has power. The obstinacy in this verse: ﴿those who disbelieve say: this is not what?﴾ ﴿but tales of the ancients﴾. This is obstinacy, because their claim that it is tales of the ancients is obstinacy beyond doubt, and everyone knows that the noble Qur'an is not the word of a human, let alone tales of the ancients. As for resorting to force, look at the disputation between Pharaoh and Moses, where Pharaoh said to him: ﴿If you take a god other than me, I will surely make you among the imprisoned﴾ [ash-Shu'ara 29]; so he resorted to force and intimidation. And consider His saying: ﴿I will surely make you among the imprisoned﴾ and not "I will imprison you," indicating that he wished to appear in the guise of power that imprisons people, and having prisoners, so he threatened Moses that he would be among them.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that whoever disputes with falsehood to refute the truth is a disbeliever, by His saying: ﴿Those who disbelieve say﴾. Here the explicit noun is used in place of the pronoun, whereas the context required: "until when they come to you disputing with you, they say: this is nothing but tales of the ancients." But He said ﴿those who disbelieve say﴾. Among the benefits of using the explicit form in place of the pronoun is that when this explicit description is a meaning, it encompasses and includes everything that applies to it. So whoever disputes with falsehood to refute the truth is a disbeliever; then he is either a lesser disbeliever (kufr asghar) or a greater disbeliever (kufr akbar).

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 6, verse 26:

Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And they forbid others from it and keep away from it themselves﴾ [al-An'am 26].

Whom does the pronoun in ﴿they﴾ refer to? It refers to the disbelievers who argue (against the Prophet).

﴿They forbid others from it﴾ means: from what you have brought of revelation.

﴿And keep away from it﴾ means: they distance themselves from it. The "forbidding" (nahy) is mentioned before the "keeping away" (na'y), although the expected order would have been to begin with "keeping away", which is their own action rather than their action toward others. This indicates the intensity of their hatred for what the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, brought, to the point that they begin by forbidding people before they themselves keep away from it.

﴿And they destroy none but themselves﴾. Here ﴿in﴾ (in) means (ma) (not), i.e., they destroy none but themselves, as in another verse: ﴿And they will not harm you at all﴾ [an-Nisa' 113]. Their disputing and their forbidding of people does not harm the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, in any way; rather, it is the destruction of themselves. Is the intended destruction here physical or spiritual?

The answer: spiritual, because this disputing disbeliever does not die by his disputing; he remains alive, but in reality he has been destroyed in the spiritual sense.

﴿But they do not perceive it﴾ means: these people do not realize that by this forbidding of what the Messenger brought and by their keeping away from it, they have destroyed themselves. That is why you find them boasting of their disbelief. Abu Sufyan said on the day of Uhud: "Exalted is Hubal!" He boasts of what? Of the idol he worships, claiming that it has prevailed over Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him and his family. The Prophet ﷺ said to them: "Answer him." They said: "What shall we answer him with?" He said: "Say: Allah is most high and most majestic."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (3039) from the hadith of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib.]]

So the point is that these disputing disbelievers do not perceive that they are in error, may Allah grant us well-being, and this is the utmost of trials: that a person sees himself as upon the truth while he is upon falsehood. Among the supplications of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, was: "O Allah, show us the truth as truth and grant us the ability to follow it, and show us falsehood as falsehood and grant us the ability to avoid it, and do not make it confused for us, lest we go astray."[[Al-'Iraqi said in his takhrij of the hadiths of Ihya' (3/1418): I have not found a source for its beginning. Al-Mustaghfiri narrated in ad-Da'awat from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet ﷺ used to supplicate: "O Allah, You have asked us of ourselves what we cannot possess except through You, so give us from it what pleases You with us." In its chain is Wahlan ibn Khubayr, whom al-Azdi declared weak. Muslim also has, from the hadith of 'A'ishah, what he would open his night prayer with: "Guide me to what has been disputed concerning the truth..." to the end of the hadith. Ibn Shahin said in Madhahib Ahl as-Sunnah (38): among the supplications of earlier generations: "O Allah, show us the truth as truth and inspire us to follow it, and show us falsehood as falsehood and inspire us to avoid it."]]

* Student: Which books are recommended for reading the speech of the theologians, the one containing refutations that convince a person? Sometimes some books and works...

* Shaykh: Yes. By Allah, I have not seen anything better than the books of Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, and Ibn al-Qayyim. But the words of Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, are easier and closer to understanding. As for the rest of the theologians, most of their writing is disputation: the Ash'aris against the Mu'tazilah. This is sufficient. If you want sound creed, then take the books of Shaykh al-Islam and Ibn al-Qayyim. This is the best I have seen.

* Student: May Allah pardon you, O Shaykh. Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, O Shaykh, is deeper in evidence, and Ibn al-Qayyim, may they both have mercy on them, is easier in arranging speech and in the coherence of its parts.

* Shaykh: Correct, that is the reality. Therefore the books of Ibn al-Qayyim are considered a ladder to the books of Shaykh al-Islam, may Allah have mercy on him.

* Student: How can one reconcile excusing by ignorance, meaning the excuse of those followers who are followers of misguidance, with the fact that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, increases people in misguidance; since the establishment of proof is not by a single word that is repeated to them constantly?

* Shaykh: These did not remain ignorant, because the Messenger came to them with clear signs, but they say: ﴿Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion﴾ [az-Zukhruf 22].

* Student: Does this apply to followers of misguidance, meaning any individual...

* Shaykh: Followers of what?

* Student: Followers of misguidance, the followers who say...

* Shaykh: The ruling differs. If these followers were never told about the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him at all, nor that a messenger had come to mankind, and their leaders concealed this from them, then they are excused. But if they have come to know, then it must be made known. It should also be known that there is a difference between the Jews, the Christians, and others. Others must have the proof conveyed to them and understood. As for the Jews and Christians, the proof is established upon them merely by hearing—hearing of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, no one from this nation hears of me, be he Jew or Christian, then dies without believing in what I have brought, except that he will be among the companions of the Fire."[[Narrated by Muslim (153/240) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]] The reason is that the books of the Jews and Christians explicitly describe the attributes of the Messenger ﷺ, so nothing remains for them except what? Except that they hear of his emergence. When they hear of his emergence, the proof is established upon them.

* Student: The hadith of the Prophet ﷺ: "I am a guarantor of a house at the edge of Paradise for one who abandons disputation even if he is in the right" [[Narrated by Abu Dawud (4800) from the hadith of Abu Umamah.]]. Is it absolute, even concerning the people of innovation?

* Shaykh: No, disputation is prohibited when it is not for the truth. As for disputation aimed at establishing the truth and nullifying falsehood, it is obligatory. But, for example, our arguing over some worldly matter, while I know that I am correct, yet when I see my companion wishing to dispute, I leave it.

I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan. The saying of Allah, the Most High: ﴿And they forbid others from it and keep away from it themselves﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the enemies of Islam forbid others from Islam, and their forbidding of it necessarily entails that they pursue every path that distances people from it, because their forbidding of it is a real forbidding that comes from the heart. This necessitates that they pursue every path that distances people from the Shariah of Allah. The methods for this vary: it may be by raising doubts, or by corrupt ideas, or by corrupt morals, or by sowing discord among people, or what is similar to that. The main point is that the methods are many.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: these people combined misguidance with misleading others. Where is misleading others in His saying?

* Student: ﴿They forbid others﴾.

* Shaykh: And misguidance?

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: Well done. And this is the utmost of transgression, which is injustice.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: whoever tries to nullify the truth and distance people from it has only harmed himself.

His saying: ﴿And they destroy none but themselves﴾. Even if the world dazzles him and an apparent victory appears to him, he is in reality destroyed. Have you understood this? For example, Abu Sufyan said in the battle of Uhud: "Exalted is Hubal!" And he said: "We have al-'Uzza, and you have no al-'Uzza."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (3039) from the hadith of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib.]] So he boasted and lifted up his nose. But will this state remain, or will the outcome be against them? The second is what is certain, whether in this world or in the Hereafter.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: a warning against a person's following paths of destruction while he does not perceive it. Allah the Most High has explained this in His saying: ﴿Is one whose evil deed has been made attractive to him, so he sees it as good [equal to one guided]? For indeed, Allah leaves astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills﴾ [Fatir 8].

Beware. But if someone says: what indicates to a person whether he is upon correctness or not?

The answer: he should return to the Book and the Sunnah, and to the guidance of the righteous predecessors and their methodology, and so he will know whether he is upon correctness or upon error.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 6, verse 27:

Then Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿And if you could see when they will be made to stand over the Fire and they will say, "Oh, would that we could be returned and not deny the signs of our Lord and be among the believers."﴾ [al-An'am 27].

First: ﴿law﴾ (if) is a conditional particle. Is it a particle of existence for existence, or of non-existence for non-existence?

Consider ﴿law tara﴾ (if you could see). The answer (jawab) is omitted, its estimated form being: "If you could see when they were made to stand over the Fire, you would see a dreadful, great and terrible matter." So the answer is omitted. When you say, "law jaa Zayd lajaa 'Amr" (if Zayd had come, 'Amr would have come), here it is a particle of non-existence for non-existence. If you say, "lamma jaa Zayd jaa 'Amr" (when Zayd came, 'Amr came), this is a particle of existence for existence. And if you say, "lawla Zayd lajaa 'Amr" (were it not for Zayd, 'Amr would have come), it is non-existence for existence. Thus these three share existence and non-existence between them.

And His saying: ﴿And if you could see when they were made to stand over the Fire﴾ — the address is to the Prophet ﷺ, or to everyone who can be addressed; that is, "If you could see, O one who sees, when they were made to stand over the Fire." They were made to stand over it; that is, the angels made them stand, because they themselves do not desire the Fire, but they are made to stand over it by compulsion, the angels causing them to stand, as the Exalted said: ﴿On the Day they will be pushed into the Fire of Hell with a violent pushing﴾ [al-Tur 13], and the Exalted said: ﴿Every time a company is thrown into it, its keepers will ask them﴾ [al-Mulk 8]. ﴿When they were made to stand over the Fire﴾; and the Fire is the abode which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has prepared for the disbelievers, as the Exalted said: ﴿And fear the Fire which has been prepared for the disbelievers﴾ [Al 'Imran 131].

Then they said: ﴿Oh, would that we could be returned and not deny the signs of our Lord﴾ [al-An'am 27]. Did they say it with their tongues or with their hearts? The original meaning is that the saying is with the tongue, with sound and letters.

And their saying: ﴿Yaa laytana﴾ (Oh, would that we...). This ﴿yaa﴾ is for alerting (tanbih), not a vocative particle (harf nida'). We say this because "layt" (would that) is a particle that cannot be addressed as a vocative. This is the easiest and closest view.

It has been said that ﴿yaa﴾ is a vocative particle and that the one addressed is omitted, estimated according to what the context requires; here it would be estimated as, "O our Lord, would that we were returned." But what we said first is more correct, because it is easier and does not require an estimate. When a statement is in doubt between containing something estimated or not, we take the second, because it is the original.

﴿Layatana nuradd﴾ ("would that we were returned"): ﴿layt﴾ is for wishing (tamanni), and wishing occurs with the impossible and with the difficult. An example of the impossible is the poet's saying:

Alā layta al-shabāba ya'ūdu yawman *** fa-ukhbirahu bimā fa'alal-mashību
This is impossible. An example of the difficult is:

Alā layta mā hādhā al-ḥamāma lanā *** ilā ḥamāmatinā wa niṣfahu fa-qad
This is difficult.
And like the poor man's saying: "Would that I had wealth so I could give charity from it." This is not impossible, but it is difficult.

Here: ﴿Yaa laytana nuradd﴾ — is the wish impossible or difficult? It is impossible, because it is not possible for them to be returned to the world, and even if they were returned, the matter would be contrary to what they said.

﴿Yaa laytana nuradd wa la nukadhdhiba bi-ayati rabbina﴾ — these are included within the wish. ﴿Wa nakūna min al-mu'minīn﴾ — likewise. They wished for three things:

First: being returned to the world.

Second: not denying the signs of Allah.

Third: being among the believers. This is why ﴿la nukadhdhiba﴾ came in the accusative (naṣb), because the ﴿wāw﴾ here is the wāw of accompaniment (wāw al-ma'iyya), so the second is with the first. Likewise ﴿nakūna﴾ came in the accusative, because the ﴿wāw﴾ is what? (wāw al-ma'iyya), so the third is with the first. They wished for all these three things, but they were lying in what they said. Therefore Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿But it has appeared to them what they used to conceal before. And even if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars﴾ [al-An'am 28].

* Student: It was revealed about Abu Talib: the meaning of ﴿yanhawna 'nhu﴾ (they forbid from it) is that he defends the Prophet ﷺ, and ﴿yan'awna 'anhu﴾ (they keep away from it) means that he does not believe.

* Shaykh: No, this is a great error, because the verse is in the context of censure for forbidding from it and keeping away from it, and it is known that defending the Prophet ﷺ is not blameworthy but praiseworthy. No, this is an error, but he saw that the picture resembles the condition of Abu Talib and thought it to be so, and this is from distorting the Quran; the blame is directed at both matters.

* * *
* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan: ﴿And if you could see when they were made to stand over the Fire, and they said, "Oh, would that we could be returned and not deny the signs of our Lord and be among the believers" (27). But it has appeared to them what they used to conceal before. And even if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars﴾ [al-An'am 27, 28].
* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿And if you could see when they were made to stand over the Fire﴾, and what came before it we have already taken its benefits.

﴿And if you could see﴾ — the address is either to the Prophet ﷺ, or to everyone to whom this address reaches. They said: ﴿Oh, would that we could be returned and not deny the signs of our Lord﴾.

We said: in His saying ﴿wa la nukadhdhiba bi-ayati rabbina﴾ there are two readings: a reading with raf' (nominative) and a reading with naṣb (accusative). On the reading with naṣb, the ﴿wāw﴾ is the wāw of accompaniment; meaning, they wished that they would be returned and not deny the signs of Allah. On the reading with raf', it is included in His saying ﴿Yaa laytana nuradd﴾, i.e., the content of the saying: they say, "Oh, would that we were returned and did not deny the signs of our Lord," so the ﴿wāw﴾ is conjoining the preceding clause, so they said: "We do not deny the signs of our Lord." The first is more eloquent, and it is the reading with naṣb. ﴿wa nakūna min al-mu'minīn﴾ is conjoined to it.

* In this verse there are benefits; among them: the intensity of the regret of the disbelievers when they are made to stand over the Fire of Hell, because they wish for something that cannot be.

* And among them: the affirmation of the Fire, which is the abode Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has prepared for the disbelievers; and the Book and the Sunnah have mentioned the kinds of punishment in it that are known to many people.

* And among them: the affirmation of speech by people after resurrection, and that a person after resurrection speaks and acts as he speaks and acts in the world.

* And among them: these people's acknowledgment of the signs of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; by their saying: ﴿and not deny the signs of our Lord﴾.

* And also among them: their acknowledgment that they are not believers, because they wished to be believers, but this will not benefit them, since everything has ended.

* And among them: the permissibility of omitting what is known; and the meaning is that it is permissible linguistically. On this Ibn Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

"And omitting what is known is permissible, as you say, 'Zayd is with whom is with you two'"
("And omitting what is known is permissible") is not only in the subject and predicate, but in the subject and predicate, the verb and the agent, and in every speech. So what is the estimated element? What?
* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: No, "lara'ayta amran 'adheeman" (you would have seen a great matter) — that is the answer.

Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Nay, there has become apparent to them what they used to conceal before﴾ [al-An'am 28]. ﴿Nay﴾ (bal) is a turning away from and nullification of what preceded it in their statement: ﴿Oh, would that we were returned, and would not deny the signs of our Lord, and would be among the believers﴾. That is: nay, they would not believe even if they were returned.

﴿There has become apparent to them﴾, meaning: it became clear to them.

﴿What they used to conceal before﴾. So what is it that they used to conceal before? Is it their affirmation of the messengers and what they brought, but they would deny it (jahd)? Or is it what they used to conceal before of disbelief that they were hiding?

On the first view, the context concerns the disbelievers; on the second, the context concerns the hypocrites (munafiqun).

﴿Nay, there has become apparent to them what they used to conceal before﴾. What did they conceal? Their affirmation of the messengers, but they denied it, and jahd (denial) is the rejection of what was known; or ﴿what they used to conceal before﴾ of disbelief, since they show faith and conceal disbelief. So on the first view the verse is about whom? About the disbelievers. On the second, about the hypocrites. Can we say that the verse includes both meanings?

The answer: Yes, because there is no contradiction. But what makes it problematic to apply it to the hypocrites is that the surah is Meccan, since Surat al-An'am is Meccan and was revealed at Mecca all at once. How then can it contain an allusion to the hypocrites? The answer to this difficulty: there is no difficulty, because Allah, glorified and exalted, informs about what will happen on the Day of Resurrection, and on the Day of Resurrection hypocrisy will have occurred, isn't that so?

Also, Allah mentions the hypocrites in the Meccan surahs in anticipation of what will happen and in preparation for them. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said in Surat al-Ankabut: ﴿And Allah will surely make evident those who believed, and He will surely make evident the hypocrites﴾ [al-Ankabut 11], and it is Meccan. Accordingly there is no difficulty, and the verse includes both meanings. The Noble Qur'an is great: its verses, phrases and words may bear several meanings, and the Qur'an, in its greatness, accommodates all these meanings so long as some of them do not contradict others. If some of them contradict one another, then preference (tarjih) is required.

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Nay, there has become apparent to them﴾, meaning: became clear to them: ﴿what they used to conceal before﴾.

﴿And if they were returned﴾, meaning to the world, ﴿they would certainly return to what they were forbidden﴾. So is their statement true or false? Therefore He said: ﴿And indeed they are liars﴾. ﴿And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden﴾, that is: to the denial of the messengers and to hypocrisy, ﴿and indeed they are liars﴾ in their statement: ﴿Oh, would that we were returned, and would not deny the signs of our Lord﴾.

* In the noble verse: the realities will become manifest and clear on the Day of Resurrection. Consider Allah's words at the end of Surat Ya-Sin, where, when mentioning the blowing of the Trumpet, He says: ﴿O woe to us! Who has raised us from our resting place?﴾ Then they will say: ﴿This is what the Most Merciful promised, and the messengers spoke the truth﴾, or it will be said to them: ﴿This is what the Most Merciful promised, and the messengers spoke the truth﴾ [Ya-Sin 52]. The matter will then be clear at that time, but it will not benefit one who did not believe in it during his life.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the connection of Allah's knowledge to the impossible, as in His words: ﴿And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden﴾.

If someone says: this is not impossible, because Allah is able to return them to the world.

It is said: it is impossible according to Allah's promise, for Allah has decreed that people will not return to the world.
