This is why, when the martyrs who were killed in the way of Allah wish, they wish to return to the world and be killed a second time, as did ʿAbd Allah ibn Haram, when Allah said to him: "Ask (what you wish)." He said: "I wish to return to the world and be killed in Your cause again." He said: "I have decreed that they will not return to it." [Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (3010) and Ibn Majah (190) from Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah.] This is a universal, divine decree. Is it then impossible according to Allah's power or according to Allah's promise?

* Students: According to Allah's promise.

* The Shaykh: According to Allah's promise. Likewise, injustice with respect to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is impossible according to His promise, yet He is able to do injustice. There is something impossible in itself and something impossible by other than itself. So His words: ﴿And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden﴾ contain evidence that Allah's knowledge is connected to the impossible.

If someone says: Can a thing be impossible in itself and yet be known by Allah, Mighty and Majestic?

The answer: Yes. Listen to Allah's words: ﴿Had there been in them gods other than Allah, they would both have been corrupted﴾ [al-Anbya' 22]. This is rationally impossible and cannot occur, yet Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knew that if there were gods in the heavens and earth other than Allah, they would be corrupted. Thus Allah's knowledge is connected to the impossible, and to the possible, as in: ﴿Allah knows that you used to deceive yourselves﴾ [al-Baqarah 187], and to the necessary, such as Allah, Blessed and Exalted, knowing His own perfect attributes. This is why we say: the most comprehensive of Allah's attributes is knowledge.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the disbelievers are not free from lying even in the Hereafter, and likewise the hypocrites, since Allah has called them liars and said: ﴿And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: emphasizing a matter when the need calls for it, either because of its importance, or because the addressee is doubtful about it, or for other reasons. The point is that it is part of eloquence and rhetoric to emphasize a statement when the need for emphasis arises. Where is the emphasis in the verse? In which clause? ﴿And indeed they are liars﴾. Here it is emphasized with (inna) and (the lam).

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 6, verse 29:**

﴿And they say, "There is nothing but our life of this world, and we will not be resurrected."﴾ [al-An'am: 29] ﴿They say﴾: i.e., those who deny the resurrection (al-ba'th).

﴿There is nothing﴾: i.e., it is not.

﴿but our life of this world﴾: meaning there is no other life; there is nothing but the life of this world. Then they emphasized this statement by their saying: ﴿and we will not be resurrected﴾. This is an explicit denial of the resurrection, even though the resurrection is indicated by the Book, the Sunnah, reason and the consensus (ijma') of the scholars, and this will come in the benefits (al-fawa'id).

As for his saying: ﴿our life of this world﴾: ﴿al-dunya﴾ (the world), is it from al-dana'a (nearness) in rank and status, or from nearness in time and duration, or from both?

It is from both. It is "dunya" in relation to the Hereafter because it comes before the Hereafter, and it is also "dunya" in rank, lower than the Hereafter, as the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿But the Hereafter is better and more enduring﴾ [al-A'la: 17]. For this reason you will never find in this world lasting joy at all, meaning joy for the body and joy for the heart. You will not find this; that is, a blessing for the body and the heart that is not possible to last forever. Either there is bodily pleasure, which is the comfort that people now call for (many people call for comfort and luxury, and the most important thing to them is entertainment and luxury). This is a bodily pleasure, but it generates in the heart great regret and constriction of the chest. Or there is pleasure in the heart, and this belongs to the believers, as the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer – We will surely cause him to live a good life﴾ [al-Nahl: 97]. Yet a person must still have both what gladdens him and what displeases him, so it is not possible to find in this world anything complete from every aspect. For this reason the description applies to it perfectly. We ask Allah to grant us and you asceticism in it (al-zuhd) and desire for the Hereafter.

As for his saying: ﴿and we will not be resurrected﴾: i.e., we will not be brought out of the graves. They have no proof for this denial except mere desires and obstinacy. Otherwise, what is the obstacle? Allah has established rational, sensory and legal proofs for the necessity of the resurrection, or for its possibility, and that it is not impossible. But they, may Allah protect us, denied it, and because of their denial they did not work for the Hereafter; all their work was for this world. We ask Allah for safety.

* In these noble verses: the disbelievers deny the resurrection; because his saying ﴿and they say﴾ is coordinated with what precedes it, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, stated this explicitly in His saying: ﴿Those who disbelieve claim that they will never be resurrected. Say: "Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected"﴾ [al-Taghabun: 7].

* Among the benefits of this verse: the indication of the nearness of the life of this world, and that it is not that life which a person should preserve and forget the Hereafter; because of His saying: ﴿al-dunya﴾.

It has come in a hadith: "If the world were equal to the wing of a mosquito, Allah would not have given a disbeliever a drink of water from it"[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (2320) and Ibn Majah (4110) from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd.]]. On this Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

If the world were equal to the wing of a mosquito, the Lord would not give the ingrate any of it.
But by Allah, it is more worthless in His sight than that wing, incapable of flight.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the denial of these people is a denial of obstinacy. We derive this from the fact that if what they said were true, the creation of creatures would become pointless, without benefit: nations that live, die, fight and clash, and then there is no resurrection in which the good-doer is recompensed for his goodness and the wrongdoer for his wrongdoing. This is not possible.

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And if you could see when they are made to stand before their Lord﴾ [al-An'am 30]. This is another standing (mawqif), and the address in His words ﴿you could see﴾ is either to the Prophet (ﷺ) or to everyone to whom the address is directed.

﴿When they are made to stand﴾ means: when they are made to stand before their Lord. In the verse that precedes this, someone may ask: how is the future expressed with the past, ﴿when they were made to stand﴾, and not "when they will stand"?

It is said: a thing that is certain is expressed in the past tense because its occurrence is established, and from this is the Most High's saying: ﴿The command of Allah has come, so do not seek to hasten it﴾ [an-Nahl 1]. Thus this is a depiction of a future state as though it were a present, already-past thing.

﴿They are made to stand before their Lord﴾, who is Allah, Mighty and Majestic. He attributed lordship (rububiyyah) to them, although they are among the lowest of Allah's servants, as a pointer that He, Mighty and Majestic, is the Creator, the Owner, and the Manager of them, so it was incumbent upon them to worship Him. Thus attributing lordship to them points to the fact that authority over them belongs to Him, Mighty and Majestic, and despite that they did not believe in Him or in His messengers, nor did they act for this Day.

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿When they are made to stand before their Lord. He says, "Is this not the truth?"﴾. ﴿He says﴾ is a resumptive clause (jumlah isti'nafiyyah) explaining what took place at the standing.

﴿Is this not the truth?﴾ The thing referred to is the resurrection (al-ba'th) which they used to deny. In this sentence there is a superfluous preposition: the "bi" (ب) in His words ﴿bil-haqq (with the truth)﴾. The scholars of rhetoric (balaghah) say that the addition of particles indicates emphasis, so this sentence is, in terms of i'rab, emphasized by the superfluous "bi". ﴿Is this not the truth?﴾ means: with the established truthfulness about which there is no doubt.

﴿They say, "Yes, by our Lord!"﴾ So they answered with the answer accompanied by an oath, and at first they used to say: "We will not be resurrected," but here they swore that this resurrection is true. However, if someone asks me whether this oath benefits them, the answer is: it does not benefit them, because the Hereafter is a place of recompense, not a place of action.

﴿They say, "Yes, by our Lord!"﴾ (Say) good. ﴿By our Lord!﴾ The (waw) here is a particle of oath (harf qasam), and the oath, as we have often seen, is the affirmation of a matter by mentioning a great object with a particular particle, which is the (waw), the (ba') and the (ta').

He says: ﴿So taste the punishment because you used to disbelieve﴾. That is, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: when they acknowledged that this is the truth, it became clear that their earlier denial was disbelief, by their own admission.

As for His words ﴿Taste the punishment﴾, the command here is for humiliation, not honor, because no one is honored with punishment; it is for humiliation. The word "taste" is applied to punishment to indicate that its occurrence is certain, for a person's tasting of a thing means that he has become completely certain of it. For example, if I say to you: "I have an apple for you in my pocket," you believe me; when you see it, your certainty increases; when you eat it, it increases even more. The first is called "knowledge of certainty" (ʿilm al-yaqin), the second "eye of certainty" (ʿayn al-yaqin), and the third "truth of certainty" (haqq al-yaqin).

As for His words ﴿because you used to disbelieve﴾, the (ba') is causal (lil-sababiyyah), and the (ma) is a verbal-noun particle (masdariyyah), so what follows it is taken as a verbal noun, and the meaning is: "because of your disbelieving", that is, disbelieving in the Last Day, in the one who informed you of the Last Day, namely the messengers, peace be upon them, and in the one who sent them.

Where is the response (jawab) of (law)? It is omitted; its estimate is: "you would see a tremendous matter." Omitting it is permissible, but is omitting it equally permissible, or is omission more eloquent?

The answer: the second, so that the mind may go in every direction, because if the response were mentioned it would be restricted to what was mentioned; but when it is omitted, a person imagines that omitted thing to be greater than any description, so omitting such a thing is part of eloquence while still being appropriate to the situation.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of Allah's lordship over these disbelievers, from His saying ﴿their Lord﴾.

* Among its benefits: that Allah has angels who bring people to Him, Mighty and Majestic, as evidence from His saying ﴿when they were made to stand﴾, and not "when they stood"; so they are brought and made to stand.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of speech to Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿He says, "Is this not the truth?"﴾.

* Among them: that Allah's speech is with letters and with sound. With letters, because ﴿Is this not the truth?﴾ consists of letters; with sound, because they heard and answered, saying: ﴿Yes, by our Lord!﴾.

* Among them: that this oath of theirs shows intense regret for their earlier denial; it is as though they gave the lie to themselves with an oath attached, and it is clear that such a thing comes only from a heart full of anguish, but the time has passed.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of causes, from His saying ﴿because you used to disbelieve﴾. Affirming causes is what corresponds to reality. Know that people have divided into three categories regarding the affirmation of causes; people of this Ummah, the Ummah of Muhammad (ﷺ), have divided into three categories:

The first: those who denied causes altogether, and said that things come about merely by chance, and merely because Allah created them.

Among them: those who affirmed causes as having effect in themselves, and these are the materialists who believe that the universe interacts by itself, even if they claim affiliation to the Ummah, like some philosophers or pseudo-philosophers.

The third: those who affirmed causes, but as having the power that Allah placed in them, not by themselves. This view is the middle path that is required. For this reason we find that the effects of things change by the decree of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. The fire that was kindled for Ibrahim, what was it? It was coolness and safety, although if we returned to the cause itself it would have burned; but it does not burn except by the will of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. We also find that Allah, Blessed and Most High, brings about things whose causes we do not know, which indicates that the cause is not the agent; rather the agent is Allah. Yet in His wisdom He made a cause for everything.

* Among this too, among the benefits of the verse: omission of what is already known, as in the verse before it.

* Student: Swearing by other than Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is lesser shirk if there is no exaltation in it. If a person swears only while exalting the one sworn by, but his exaltation is less than his exaltation of Allah, would it be major disbelief?

* The Shaykh: He asks, saying: if a person swears by other than Allah, Mighty and Majestic, believing in its exaltation, does he become a disbeliever?

The answer: he does not become a disbeliever, unless he believes that it has exaltation equal to or greater than the exaltation of Allah. Many ignorant people may believe that their leaders have more exaltation than Allah; this is major shirk. But anything below that is not major.

* Student: (...) Why is it not said: "There will appear to them the consequence of their denial and disbelief," since it is the Day of Resurrection? Why is this not said?

* The Shaykh: That is it. What is it that they conceal? They conceal either disbelief, if they are hypocrites, or they conceal belief in the prophets, if they are disbelievers.

* The student: "And there will appear to them on the Day of Resurrection their consequence."

* The Shaykh: "There will appear to them" this; and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, expresses the punishment by the act that is its cause.

* Student: The earth, O Shaykh: the plants of the earth all die completely and then all grow again except (...). Does this, O Shaykh, indicate the resurrection on the Day of Resurrection?

* The Shaykh: Yes indeed. Allah has given this as an example, saying, Most High: ﴿And among His signs is that you see the earth barren, but when We send down water upon it, it stirs and swells. Indeed, He who revived it is the Reviver of the dead. Indeed, He is Competent over all things﴾ [Fussilat 39].

* Student: Shaykh, may Allah reward you well, some people, when they swear by Allah, Glorified and Exalted, verbally, do not mean it; but when they swear by the Qur'an (mushaf), they mean it. Shaykh, may Allah reward you well, what is said about these people?

* The Shaykh: We have never heard of this except tonight!

* The student: This is common among us; when they swear by the mushaf they are sincere, but when you tell them, "Say: by Allah," they say it and are not sincere.

* The Shaykh: This is from their ignorance, because exalting an oath by the mushaf is part of exalting Allah, Mighty and Majestic, since the mushaf is the speech of Allah, Most High. But this is ignorance, just as some of them swear by Allah carelessly. However, if you say to them, "Swear by the Prophet," they would not swear except while being truthful.

* Student: Some Muslims, when they are warned of the punishment of the grave and of punishment in general, say: "Have you seen the grave? Have you seen its punishment?" Do such people fall under this verse, O Shaykh?

* The Shaykh: Yes, they fall under the verse as deniers, because one who believes only in what he can sense has not believed in the unseen, and he is a disbeliever. But denying the punishment of the grave is of two kinds: one may deny the punishment of the grave upon the body; this does not make one a disbeliever, because some scholars of the community have held this view, that it is upon the body, meaning. And one may deny it altogether, saying: not upon the body nor upon the soul; this is disbelief, why? Because he denies what has been transmitted by mass narration (mutawatir) from the Prophet (ﷺ) and received by the whole Ummah with acceptance. Every person who prays says: "I seek refuge in Allah from the punishment of Hell and from the punishment of the grave"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1377), and Muslim (588/128), from the hadith of Abu Hurairah.]], and the Noble Qur'an has pointed to this in several verses.

* Student: May Allah reward you well, O Shaykh. Some sinners, when you advise them and warn them of Allah, say that Allah has decreed this for them to be this way. How should such a person be answered?

* The Shaykh: This is an argument from predestination (qadar), and the sinner has no proof in predestination, because we say to this man with ease: Do you know that Allah decreed this for you, unless you do it? Will he say...?

* The student: He will say: No.

* The Shaykh: He will say: No. Then why do you act? Why did you not decree that Allah decreed good for you and act with good?

This answer is very easy, apart from what we say now: if you heard about two towns, one with trade, security and tranquility, and another the opposite, to which would you go? He would say: I go to the first. So we say: this is like the works of this world, and like the works of the Hereafter.

* Student: May Allah protect you, O Shaykh. Without resurrection, the importance of life would be void, correct?

* The Shaykh: Yes.

* The student: Is it possible to comment on this statement?

* The Shaykh: Without?

* The student: Without, meaning resurrection, that we will be resurrected, the importance of life would be void?

* The Shaykh: What?

* The student: Void?

* The Shaykh: Cut off?

* The student: Voided.

* The Shaykh: Voided, yes, correct: without resurrection the importance of life would be voided, because life in reality is not complete life; it has no importance that a person lives as he lives, then perishes into nothing. What benefit is there? In truth, one who denies resurrection thereby denies that there is any benefit in this world. Suppose a man did everything, had products and inventions, and what does he benefit? He benefits nothing unless there is no afterlife in which he is recompensed. If he says: wealth cannot be gained, we say to him: and what is the end of wealth? Its end is the latrine.

Now, the most general benefit is eating and drinking; where does it go? In the belly, and it comes out to where? To filthy places. This is the end of wealth. So what is the benefit of this world? Therefore, denying resurrection, apart from being disbelief and misguidance, is considered foolishness.

**Student:** I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. ﴿Those who denied the meeting with Allah have certainly lost, until, when the Hour comes upon them suddenly, they say, "Oh, our regret over what we neglected concerning it!" while they carry their burdens on their backs. Unquestionably, evil is what they carry.﴾ (31) ﴿And the worldly life is not but amusement and diversion. And the home of the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah. Then will you not reason?﴾ (32) ﴿We know that what they say certainly grieves you, but it is not you that they deny; rather, the wrongdoers are rejecting the signs of Allah.﴾ (33) ﴿And messengers were denied before you, and they were patient over what they were denied and harmed until Our victory came to them. And there is no changer of the words of Allah. And there has certainly come to you some information about the messengers.﴾ (34) ﴿And if their turning away has been difficult for you, then if you are able to seek a tunnel into the earth or a stairway into the sky to bring them a sign, [you may do so]. But if Allah had willed, He would have gathered them upon guidance, so do not be among the ignorant.﴾ [al-An'am 31–35].

**Shaykh:** We seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Those who denied the meeting with Allah have certainly lost.﴾ This sentence is emphasized by ﴿qad﴾, and emphasizing particles (ḥurūf al-tawkīd) are many; some come before and some come after. For example, the lam in your saying "inna Zaydan la-qā'im" (indeed Zayd is standing) is an emphasizing particle, but it comes later. The scholars of balaghah (eloquence) mentioned these when they discussed the statement (khabar) and its types, that it is initial (ibtida'i), responsive (talabi), or denial-responsive (inkari), and they discussed the emphasizing particles. Whoever wants to cover them completely should refer to those works.

This verse is emphasized by one emphasizer, which is ﴿qad﴾.

﴿Those who denied the meeting with Allah have lost.﴾ Lost what? Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, left the loss unrestricted. He did not say "they lost themselves," or "their families," or anything else, so this is an absolute loss. Allah spoke the truth. How great is the loss of those who denied the meeting with Allah! These people will not work for the meeting with Allah, and their existence in this world becomes a loss with no benefit from it, rather with harm. Because a person's existence in this world, along with his disbelief in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is worse than his not having existed at all, and worse than the existence of beasts. Beasts exist in this world, then perish, then are resurrected on the Day of Resurrection with no reckoning for them, but this person will have a reckoning. For this reason some of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, including 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, wished that they were a tree that is cut down, meaning cut off. He said: "I wish I could leave it" (meaning this world) "with neither loss nor gain."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (7218) and Muslim (1823/11).]] This was said by 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, so what about those who came after him? Everyone who does not fill his time with obedience to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and I ask Allah to make me and you among them, has suffered a loss and missed the profit.

As for His saying ﴿denied the meeting with Allah﴾, it means the meeting with Him. Allah, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿O mankind, indeed you are laboring toward your Lord with labor and will meet Him﴾ — what? ﴿fa-mulāqīhi﴾ [al-Inshiqaq 6]. It is necessary that the One who commanded you and forbade you, and sent the messengers to you, and gave you intellect, you will meet Him, and He will hold you to account. The meaning is that they denied the resurrection in which there is a meeting with Allah.

﴿Until, when the Hour comes upon them suddenly.﴾ ﴿Until when there came upon them﴾ — ﴿ḥattā﴾ here is initial (ibtidā'iyyah), indicating the separation of what follows from what precedes.

﴿When the Hour comes upon them﴾, which is the Hour of Resurrection, ﴿suddenly, they say: "Oh, our regret over what we neglected concerning it!"﴾. The Hour may also refer to the hour of their departure from the world, because whoever dies, his resurrection has occurred; he has moved from the house of works to the house of recompense.

His saying ﴿suddenly﴾ means without expectation. The Great Hour will come suddenly, arriving upon people when a man has prepared the water trough for his camels to drink, yet he cannot; when he has lifted a morsel to his mouth, yet he cannot; and when two men have spread a garment between them so that one may sell it to the other, yet he cannot complete the contract.[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (7121) and Muslim (2954/140), from Abu Hurayrah.]] It comes suddenly.

﴿They said﴾ is the response to ﴿idhā﴾ (when). ﴿They said: "Oh, our regret over what we neglected concerning it!"﴾ Here we cannot take ﴿yā﴾ as a vocative particle. Why? Because regret is not called upon. Regret (ḥasrah) is remorse and sorrow over something that has passed. Accordingly, ﴿yā﴾ is for alerting (tanbīh), as if they said: "How great is our regret!" It was also said that ﴿yā﴾ is a vocative particle, and that "regret" is imagined as a rational thing to which the call is directed. According to this view the meaning is: "O regret, be present, for this is your time." The meaning does not differ between the two views; the only difference is whether the verb is estimated or not. Regret (ḥasrah) is remorse and sorrow over something lost.

﴿Over what we neglected concerning it.﴾ Tafrīṭ (neglect) means shortcoming.

The pronoun in ﴿fīhā﴾ (concerning it) refers to the Hour, meaning: we neglected preparing for it, because they wasted their lives on what has no benefit, and sometimes on what is harmful.

He said: ﴿while they carry their burdens on their backs﴾, meaning on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿They carry their burdens on their backs﴾ — ﴿awzār﴾ means the recompense of their deeds, ﴿on their backs﴾. Allah, the Exalted, always expresses recompense by the term "deeds." Do you know why? For two benefits.

The first benefit: that a person may correct his deeds.

The second benefit: that it may be known that the recompense is of the same kind as the deed, because recompense for deeds revolves around two matters with no third: the first is grace (faḍl), and the second is justice ('adl), with no injustice. If the deeds are good deeds, it is by grace; if they are bad deeds, it is by justice. Sometimes it may be by grace, where Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, pardons him.

﴿They carry their burdens on their backs﴾, meaning the recompense of deeds ﴿on their backs﴾, carried literally. This is what is obligatory: that we take the verses according to their apparent meaning.

No one should say: How can the recompense be carried on the back?

We say: The Day of Resurrection is not measured by the days of this world, because the conditions differ enormously. It is permissible and possible that Allah, the Exalted, creates these recompenses as bodies that are carried on the backs. What prevents it? Allah, the Exalted, has said: ﴿And they will surely carry their burdens and burdens along with their burdens﴾ [al-'Ankabut 13]. It is absolutely impermissible to measure the conditions of the Hereafter by the conditions of this world, because when you recite the Qur'an and learn what has come in the Sunnah about the conditions of the Day of Resurrection, you will be certain that there is no equivalence, and one cannot be measured by the other.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Unquestionably, evil is what they carry.﴾ ﴿Sā'a﴾ means "evil" (bi'sa). ﴿Alā﴾ is an opening and alerting particle (adāt istiftāḥ wa tanbīh). In this place we may add another point: a warning against evil deeds.

As for His saying ﴿Unquestionably, evil is what they carry﴾: if you take ﴿mā﴾ as a relative pronoun (ism mawṣūl), it requires a returning pronoun (ā'id); if you take it as a verbal-noun particle (maṣdariyyah), it does not require a returning pronoun. So what is the estimate if we take it as a relative pronoun? The estimate is: "Evil is what they carry," meaning "what they carry it is." But if we take it as maṣdariyyah, it does not need a pronoun, but needs reformulation (sabk), meaning converting the verb into a verbal noun. Accordingly the estimate is: "Evil is their burden." The meaning does not differ: Allah, the Exalted, censured what they carry on their backs of burdens.

* In this verse there are benefits. First: a clarification of the loss of the disbelievers who deny the resurrection, and that however much they think they have gained, they are losers. But when will they know that they are losers? When the term comes. As for now, they are in intoxication and do not know. For this reason, if they succeed economically, militarily, or intellectually, they will think they are winners, but they are losers.

* Among the benefits of the verse: the obligation of believing in the meeting with Allah, by the evidence that loss is established for whoever denies it, and it is well known that it is not permissible for a person to put himself into loss.

Does the meeting with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, include seeing Him?

Some scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, used this verse and His saying ﴿fa-mulāqīhi﴾ [al-Inshiqaq 6] as evidence for seeing Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and they said: meeting cannot be except face to face. Accordingly, the verse is evidence for the establishment of what? The seeing of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. And the establishment of the seeing of Allah is established by the text and by consensus.

Accordingly, the verse is evidence for the establishment of the seeing of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and the establishment of the seeing of Allah is established by the text and by consensus: the Qur'anic text and the Prophetic text. And the consensus (ijma') is from the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, and the imams of guidance after them.

From the evidences for seeing Allah in the Qur'an, what is the point of the evidence?

* Student: ﴿Looking toward their Lord.﴾ [al-Qiyamah 23]

* Shaykh: Yes, indeed, by the estimate: "looking toward the reward of their Lord."

* Student: O Shaykh, looking when joined with "ilā" (toward) indicates..

* Shaykh: (...) he does not contradict and say: "looking" is not intellectual looking, as in His saying: ﴿Look at what is in the heavens and the earth﴾ [Yunus 101]. He says: looking with the eye. But ﴿toward their Lord﴾ means toward the reward of their Lord. He will not obey you; your opponent will not obey you. He says: toward the reward of their Lord. Yes, you look toward Allah's reward, of what is in Paradise of bliss, the dark-eyed maidens, and everything. How will you respond to him?

* Student: O Shaykh, the pronoun "hā" (her) is attached to "Rabb" (Lord), O Shaykh, so we cannot take it to mean the reward.

* Shaykh: The pronoun is attached to Rabb; this is a mistake.

* Student: We say: the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, continued reciting the Qur'an..

* Shaykh: No, this is the establishment of consensus.

* Student: That if Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, wanted them to look at Allah's reward, He would have expressed it explicitly, and would not have used a word that allows other meanings.

* Shaykh: Correct, this answer is the sound one. If Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, had wanted to clarify that they look toward Allah's reward, He would have said it. But that He, the Mighty and Majestic, intends Allah's reward, and then says ﴿toward their Lord﴾ [al-Qiyamah 23], this is obscuring to creation. Is it clarification or obscuring? Obscuring. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Allah intends to make clear to you﴾ [al-Nisa' 26], and says: ﴿Allah makes clear to you that you not go astray﴾ [al-Nisa' 176]. Then what is your evidence for inserting this word into the Qur'an? If you permit this, you permit anyone who wants to express the Qur'an by its meaning to say: "Faces that Day will be radiant, toward the reward of their Lord looking." This is clear distortion. Is it clear?

Alright, what about from the Sunnah?

* Student: In the saying of Allah the Exalted..

* Shaykh: No, (...).

* Student: In the explanation of His saying, the Exalted..

* Shaykh: No.

* Student: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Indeed, you will see your Lord on the Day of Resurrection as you see the moon on the night of the full moon; you will not be harmed in seeing Him."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (554), Muslim (633/211), and al-Tirmidhi (2554), whose wording it is, from Abu Hurayrah.]]

* Shaykh: Yes, "Indeed, you will see your Lord on the Day of Resurrection as you see the moon on the night of the full moon." This comparison is for affirmation (taḥqīq). That is, just as you, in your distant places, see the moon on the night of the full moon without any of you pressing against another, so you will see Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

When Abu Razin al-'Uqayli asked the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, how will Allah call us to account in one day, when we are many and He is one? How is this?" He said: "Shall I not tell you about one of the signs of Allah?" [He said:] "What is it?" He said: "The moon. All of you see it in its place, and it is one, while you are many people." [[Narrated by Abu Dawud (4731) and Ibn Majah (180) from Abu Razin.]]

So this hadith, as our brother said, is evidence for the establishment of seeing Allah with the eye.

Alright, have we remained with consensus?

* Student: The Companions and the Successors agreed on the seeing of Allah, glorified and exalted.

* Shaykh: Who said this statement?

* Student: Trustworthy transmitters, O Shaykh.

* Shaykh: How is the path to establishing this consensus?

* Student: Trustworthy scholars transmitted it.

* Shaykh: No. With what did the scholars argue for their consensus?

* Student: With the Qur'an and the Sunnah.

* Student: When the Companions recited the Qur'an and recited the hadith of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and interpreted it according to its apparent meaning, and did not turn the wording away from its apparent meaning, this is evidence that they agreed, and no one among the Companions is recorded as disagreeing about the interpretation of that.

* Shaykh: I mentioned this to you. I said: if the one who speaks says to you: there is no acceptance of what you say about consensus, where is its path?

I say: The Companions recited the Qur'an and heard the hadiths from the Messenger ﷺ, and nothing came from any of them saying contrary to its apparent meaning. So this is a consensus from them of what? Not my silence, but my approval, a consensus from them that it is according to its apparent meaning. This is a proof with no difficulty. Bring me one of the rightly-guided caliphs, or any other Companion, who says that the seeing refers to the Paradise and the reward Allah has prepared for them, and not to seeing Allah. You will not find it. The imams of guidance after them followed them.

In any case, the verse here about the meeting with Allah has been used by some scholars as evidence for the establishment of the seeing of Allah, glorified and exalted, arguing that meeting must be face to face.

If this inference is valid, well and good; otherwise we are not in need of it. Is it clear? Good. If this inference is not valid, then the meaning of the meeting with Allah is the resurrection after death, because the disbeliever will not see Allah, glorified and exalted, as He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿No! Indeed, they, that Day, will be veiled from their Lord.﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 15].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the Hour comes suddenly, whether it is the Great Hour or the Small Hour.

Does the Small Hour not come suddenly?

Yes. Earthquakes come suddenly; storms and destructive calamities come suddenly. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, warned of this, saying: ﴿Then do the people of the towns feel secure that Our punishment will not come upon them by night while they are asleep?﴾ [al-A'raf 97] — asleep, heedless, not thinking of punishment, so it comes upon them while they are asleep. ﴿Or do the people of the towns feel secure that Our punishment will not come upon them in the morning while they are playing?﴾ [al-A'raf 98] — they are playing, heedless, not thinking that punishment would come, and punishment comes upon them. ﴿Do they feel secure from the plan of Allah?﴾ [al-A'raf 99] — with what He has bestowed on them of security, ease, and prosperity. ﴿None feels secure from the plan of Allah except the losing people.﴾ [al-A'raf 99]. The sudden loss here is the Great Hour and the Small Hour.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the intensity of the regret of those who denied the meeting with Allah, and their admission against themselves that they were negligent. But does this benefit them?

No. The work has ended; it does not benefit them. Something that has passed cannot be returned. For this reason they admitted that they were negligent.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the people of burdens carry their burdens on their backs on the Day of Resurrection, literally or figuratively?

Literally, because this is what is obligatory: that we apply the Qur'anic and Prophetic texts according to their apparent meaning.

If someone says: How will they carry them?

The answer: This is a question out of place, because the conditions of the Hereafter are not measured by the conditions of this world.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that deeds are subject to praise and blame, as in His saying: ﴿Unquestionably, evil is what they carry﴾; this is blame.

Subject to praise, such as His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Is the reward of good anything but good?﴾ [al-Rahman 60]. So deeds are subject to blame and to praise.

If blame or praise of the deed is established, does that necessitate blame or praise of the doer, the agent, or praise of him?

The answer: Yes, this is the principle, especially in worldly matters, because we have only the outward appearance; the matters of the Hereafter are with Allah.

For this reason, if we see a person prostrating to an idol, we say: he is a disbeliever, even though it is possible that he is ignorant. But we say: he is a disbeliever. If he becomes upright and affirms the oneness of Allah, this description is lifted from him; otherwise it remains.

Let it be known that some people have gone to excess regarding the issue of specifying and generalizing, to the point that some doubted whether it is permissible to say of one who prostrates to an idol that he is a disbeliever. May Allah be the One sought for help. How? Say it without hesitation: is it permissible to say of one who abandons the prayer that he is a disbeliever?

We say: "Say [to them], and do not be concerned." If he does not say it, then when is it disbelief, and when is it shirk?

Yes, if there is an impediment to takfir (declaring someone a disbeliever), then each matter takes its own ruling. But the principle is that we judge everyone who does something that constitutes disbelief, or says something that constitutes disbelief, to be a disbeliever in his own person, until we establish the hadd (prescribed punishment) against him. If he claims an impediment, we examine whether this is valid or not, and we rule on each case according to what the circumstances require.

* The student: It is known in some verses.
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* The student: In it, in some verses, there is the expression "sins" (khataya).
* The Shaykh: What?
* The student: In some verses there is the expression "sins," such as the words of the Exalted: ﴿And those who disbelieved said to those who believed, "Follow our way, and we will bear your sins"﴾ [al-'Ankabut 12].
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* The student: (...) Is it clear that what is carried is the sins themselves, and not the recompense for deeds?
* The Shaykh: (...) Now, on the Day of Resurrection, there are no deeds; on the Day of Resurrection there is only recompense.
* A student: May Allah reward you well. The one who says: "Allah is seen, but not from a direction." Does this mean he has affirmed the seeing of Allah?
* The Shaykh: Not at all. It is impossible to see a thing without a direction, and where would you see it? But this is strange.
It appears to me, based on what we know of their intelligence, that they do not mean that He is not seen from a direction, but rather they say: He is seen, but direction is not affirmed. Do you understand?
There is a difference between them. If we say, "He is not seen from a direction," its meaning is denial. But if we say, "He is seen, not from a direction," meaning direction is not affirmed, this is not like the first. Rather, we must say that Allah, exalted is He, is undoubtedly in a direction, which is the direction of height. Did not the Messenger (ﷺ) say to the slave-girl, "Where is Allah?" She said, "In the sky"?[[Recorded by Muslim (537/33) from the hadith of Mu'awiya ibn al-Hakam al-Sulami.]] But a direction that encompasses Him, exalted is He, or a direction unbefitting Him, such as the direction of the lowest part, this is prohibited.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 6, verse 32:

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And the life of this world is but amusement and diversion.﴾

(Ma) is a negation particle, and (al-hayah, "life") is the subject, and what follows (illa, "except") is the predicate. This is one of the forms of restriction (hasr), and it is the strongest form of restriction, namely negation and affirmation.

﴿The life of this world is but amusement and diversion.﴾ "The life of this world" is this life of ours. It is described as "this world" (al-dunya) for two reasons:

The first reason: the nearness of its time.

The second reason: the lowliness of its rank.

As for the first, it is clear, for the world (dunya) comes before the Hereafter. As for the second, it is also clear to anyone who has understanding, for this world is base (dania), it contains no good, and the most that it offers is that the body is made comfortable while the heart is not. The people of this world are therefore deprived of the bliss of the heart, because of the words of Allah, blessed and exalted, ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while being a believer – We will surely cause him to live a good life﴾ [an-Nahl 97]. So the good life belongs to whoever combines these two qualities: righteous deeds and, secondly, faith.

Thus it has been called "dunya" for these two reasons:

The first: the nearness of time.

The second: the nearness of value and rank, for it is near (dania).

Indeed, the Prophet (ﷺ) said, as related by Imam Ahmad from al-Mustawrid ibn Shaddad, who said: "The place of the whip of one of you in Paradise is better than the world and all that is in it"[[Narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad (9651) from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, and by al-Bukhari (2892) from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd.]] — the whole of the world, from its beginning to its end, and all that is in it, is worth less than the place of a whip. So how much more so when a person in Paradise — O Allah, make us among them, O Lord of the worlds — looks at the farthest extent of his dominion just as he looks at its nearest part, a distance of two thousand years.

His saying: ﴿but amusement and diversion⦆ means: amusement for the bodies and diversion for the hearts. All the deeds of this world are amusement, all the deeds of this world are diversion, but it is a diversion from one thing by another: a diversion by the deeds of this world from the deeds of the Hereafter. It is amusement in the sense that its doer gains nothing from it. At the least it may be said that it is neither for him nor against him in this deed, neither for him nor against him; and yet it may in fact be against him. When it is neither for him nor against him, is it serious or play? Answer: it is play, without doubt, when it is neither for him nor against him. And so we say concerning the meaning of His saying: ﴿amusement﴾.

If someone says: how can it be amusement when the people of this world have seriousness, determination and energy in their works?

We say: yet with respect to reward and recompense, it is amusement in which there is no good.

﴿And the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah﴾. The lam here is the lam of emphasis (lam al-ibtida'), which serves to affirm.

The "Hereafter" (al-dar al-akhirah) has two readings: this reading, ﴿wa-la-dar al-akhirah﴾, and the second, ﴿wa-dar al-akhirah﴾ with an idafah (construct).

The Hereafter is the counterpart of this world and its rival, and it is what comes after resurrection. Allah the Exalted named it "the Hereafter" (al-akhirah) because it is the last of the stages, for the children of Adam have four stages:

The first stage: in the wombs of their mothers.

The second stage: in this life.

The third stage: in the barzakh (intermediate state) between death and resurrection.

The fourth stage: in the resurrection after death, when the Hour is established. For this reason it is called "the Hereafter."

﴿better﴾ than what?

It is well known that the context requires: better than this world and its amusement and diversion. The object of comparison has been omitted because it is known. Among the rules of rhetoric: what is known and does not need forced estimation to be supplied is better omitted, for that brings brevity; and sometimes the reverse applies, where rhetoric requires that the matter be expanded upon.

﴿better for those who fear Allah﴾, i.e., who guard themselves against Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

The fear of Allah (taqwa) has been mentioned to us many times; it is summed up as taking a protection from the punishment of Allah by carrying out His commands and avoiding His prohibitions with knowledge and insight.

Some people have elaborated in defining it, such as their saying:

Leave sins, small and great, that is taqwa;
And act like one walking over a field of thorns, wary of what he sees;
Do not belittle any small sin, for mountains are made of pebbles.

Some say: that you act in obedience to Allah, upon a light from Allah, hoping for the reward of Allah; and that you abandon what Allah has forbidden, upon a light from Allah, fearing the punishment of Allah.
But the first is more comprehensive and clearer, because by it the derivation of taqwa is known: taking a protection from the punishment of Allah by carrying out His commands and avoiding His prohibitions with knowledge and insight.

﴿better for those who fear Allah. Will you not then reason?﴾ The interrogative here is for rebuke, and the meaning is: understand this reality, and recognize the worth of this world and the worth of the Hereafter.

By "reason" here is meant the reason of right guidance, not the reason of legal responsibility, for these people do have reason, but it is not the reason of guidance.

* This verse contains benefits:

* Among them: discouraging attachment to this world and encouraging desire for the Hereafter, the basis of which is that it describes this world with what you have heard, and describes the Hereafter with what you have heard.

* Among them: that the whole of this world is amusement and diversion: amusement for the limbs, and diversion for — what? For the hearts.

* Among them: that the world has no state other than that; the evidence of restriction is ﴿The life of this world is but amusement and diversion﴾.

* Among them: that the Hereafter is better for the God-fearing, "for those who fear Allah," better than what? Better than this world.

Accordingly, whatever harm befalls them in this world for the sake of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, or illnesses that afflict them, or the loss of a beloved, or the like, will in the Hereafter be forgotten, as if it had never been, for the Hereafter wipes out everything that came before, as though it had never been.

* Among them: the affirmation of the Hereafter, for affirming its qualities indicates the existence of its root.

* Among them: that the Hereafter is good for those who hold fast to taqwa, while for others it is not good but evil. For this reason the hadith says: "The world is a prison for the believer and a paradise for the disbeliever"[[Narrated by Muslim (2956/1) from the hadith of Abu Hurairah.]].

For the believer it is a prison, because if the whole bliss of this world were compared with the bliss of the Hereafter, it would be nothing. As for the disbeliever, it is his paradise, because in this world he was joyful among his people, but in the Hereafter it is the reverse.

We have already related to you what happened to the hafiz Ibn Hajar, who was chief judge in Egypt. He passed by a Jewish oil-seller exhausted from harm: the harm of the oil, the heat, and other things. Ibn Hajar, may Allah have mercy on him, was being pulled by horses or mules in a carriage, because he was chief judge of Egypt. This Jew stopped him and said: "How can you be in this state while I am in this state, when your hadith says: 'The world is a prison for the believer and a paradise for the disbeliever'?" He answered him on the spot, saying: "What the believer has of bliss in this world, compared with the Hereafter, is only a prison; and what torment you are in, compared with the Hereafter, is only a paradise." The Jew understood the truth and embraced Islam.

Allah the Exalted mentioned three verses concerning the preference of the Hereafter over this world. The first verse is tied to a specific person; the second is tied to a specific group by a description; and the third is unrestricted.

What is the verse restricted to a specific person?

* A student: ﴿By the morning brightness, and by the night when it covers, your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you. And the Hereafter is better for you than the first﴾ [ad-Duha 1-4].

* The Shaykh: His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And the Hereafter is better for you than the first﴾, and that is the Messenger (ﷺ).

The one tied to a description: ﴿And the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah﴾, and His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And the Hereafter is better and more lasting for whoever fears Allah﴾ [an-Nisa' 77]. And what is the unrestricted one?

* A student: At the end of Surah Sabbih (al-A'la).

* The Shaykh: At the end of Surah Sabbih: ﴿But you prefer the worldly life, while the Hereafter is better and more enduring﴾ [al-A'la 16-17]. May Allah bless you.

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿We certainly know that what they say grieves you﴾.

Research first: ﴿قَدْ نَعْلَمُ﴾ (qad) is for affirmation (tahqiq). But the grammarians say that with the past tense it is for affirmation, and with the present tense it is for diminution (taqlil). This is the general rule: with the past tense it is for affirmation, as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿We certainly know what the earth diminishes of them﴾ [Qaf 4].

With the present tense they say it is for diminution, as in the saying: "qad yajud al-bakhil" (the miser may sometimes give). So (qad) here is for diminution. But it has come in the Qur'an joined to the present tense while meaning affirmation, as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿He certainly knows what you are upon﴾ [an-Nur 64], and like this verse, ﴿We certainly know that what they say grieves you﴾, and there are other examples.

So do we say it is for diminution, or do we say it is for affirmation?

The answer: it is for affirmation, without doubt. But it expresses the past with the present, to indicate that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knew and knows what will occur, so it indicates continuity, unlike the knowledge of the past, which indicates something that has passed and ended. But when the matter is continuous, it comes with the present-tense form.

Second: ﴿إِنَّهُ لَيَحْزُنُكَ﴾. Although it follows the verb of knowing, when it follows knowledge the hamza must be opened, as in His saying: ﴿Allah knew that you were deceiving yourselves﴾ [al-Baqarah 187] and ﴿Allah knew that you would remember them﴾ [al-Baqarah 235]. Why is the hamza kasra here? It is kasra because of the presence of the lam, the lam of emphasis (lam at-tawkid). When the lam of emphasis is present, (inna) must be kasra in all cases. Do you understand? When its predicate or subject is joined with the lam, it must be kasra in all cases. Without the lam, the structure of the verse would be: "qad na'lamu annahu yahzunuka", but the lam makes the hamza kasra.

﴿قَدْ نَعْلَمُ إِنَّهُ لَيَحْزُنُكَ﴾ has two readings: ﴿لَيُحْزِنُكَ﴾ and ﴿لَيَحْزُنُكَ﴾. ﴿لَيُحْزِنُكَ﴾ is from the quadriliteral form, from "ahzanahu, yuhzinuhu" (to cause someone grief). ﴿لَيَحْزُنُكَ﴾ is from the triliteral form: "hazanahu, yahzunuhu" (to grieve him). Al-huzn (grief) is the opposite of joy; it is a state residing in the soul that entails dejection and regret.

﴿لَيَحْزُنُكَ الَّذِي يَقُولُونَ﴾: What is it that they say? They say a monstrous and great statement. They say: "The angels are daughters of Allah," they say: "We worship idols so that they bring us closer to Allah, Mighty and Majestic," they say to the Messenger (ﷺ): "He is a sorcerer, he is possessed, he is a soothsayer." So everything they say that contradicts monotheism and the message undoubtedly grieves the Prophet (ﷺ) and his family.

Is this a defense of himself, or grief for Allah, Mighty and Majestic? The second, without doubt.

﴿فَإِنَّهُمْ لَا يُكَذِّبُونَكَ﴾: He says it, the Knower of the secret and what is more hidden, Mighty and Majestic, who knows what is in the hearts. ﴿إِنَّهُمْ لَا يُكَذِّبُونَكَ﴾ means: in their hearts. As for their tongues, they say: "He is a sorcerer, a liar," but in their hearts, no. They know that he is truthful and trustworthy; before the message they called him "al-Amin" (the Trustworthy), they were pleased with him and made him their judge. But when he came with the truth, they—may Allah protect us—turned away from it and denied it.

﴿فَإِنَّهُمْ لَا يُكَذِّبُونَكَ﴾ means: in their hearts, unlike their tongues, for they do deny. ﴿فَإِنَّهُمْ لَا يُكَذِّبُونَكَ وَلَكِنَّ الظَّالِمِينَ بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ يَجْحَدُونَ﴾. ﴿الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ here refers to those who deny the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so it is the wrongdoing of disbelief.

﴿بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ﴾ is connected to ﴿يَجْحَدُونَ﴾ and is placed before it for two purposes: the first, to convey restriction (hasr); the second, to match the rhyme of the verses (ra'us al-ayat). Matching the endings of verses is undoubtedly part of eloquence. For this, consider the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in Surah Ta-Ha: ﴿They said: We believe in the Lord of Harun and Musa﴾ [Ta-Ha 70], where Harun is mentioned first, although Musa is mentioned first in all other places, but for the sake of matching the endings of the verses.

* So there are two benefits: the meaningful (ma'nawi), and the verbal (lafzi).

The meaningful: it conveys restriction, as if the meaning is: "But the wrongdoers deny only the signs of Allah," and they acknowledge many other things, but they do not acknowledge the signs of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

* In these noble verses: the affirmation of Allah's knowledge of everything these deniers say, by His saying: ﴿We certainly know that what they say grieves you﴾.

* And among them: consolation to the Prophet (ﷺ) and strengthening of his spirit; in this verse there is clear consolation and strengthening of his spirit. Likewise, a person should console his brother in what befalls someone like him, so that the matter becomes easier for him, because a person by nature, when he finds a partner in it, what? The matter becomes easier for him. Have you not considered His saying: ﴿And it will not benefit you today, since you did wrong, that you are sharing in the punishment﴾ [az-Zukhruf 39]? In this world, when they share the punishment, it is easier for them, but in the Hereafter it will not benefit them. Consider also the saying of the woman al-Khansa:

Were it not for the abundance of those who weep around me for their brothers, I would have killed myself.
And they do not weep like my brother, but I console myself about him with consolation.

When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, mentions to His Prophet (ﷺ) what consoles him, strengthens his spirit, and removes his grief, this is from the favour of Allah upon him, blessed and exalted is He.

* Among the benefits of the noble verses: the Prophet's (ﷺ) eagerness for the guidance of creation, and that the turning away of people from the religion of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, grieves him.

* And among them: the knowledge of Allah, Exalted is He, of what is in the hearts; by His saying: ﴿So they do not deny you, but the wrongdoers deny the signs of Allah﴾.

A parallel to this verse is His saying, about the people of Pharaoh: ﴿And they denied them, though their souls were convinced of them, out of wrongdoing and arrogance﴾ [an-Naml 14]. Here "ظُلْمًا" is a verbal object of purpose whose governing verb is (jahadu), meaning: they denied them out of wrongdoing, ﴿and arrogance﴾. Consider also the saying of Musa when he debated Pharaoh; Musa said to him: ﴿You certainly know that none has sent these down except the Lord of the heavens and the earth as clear evidence﴾ [al-Isra 102]. He said: ﴿You certainly know﴾, and Pharaoh did not deny him in this exchange, and did not say: "I do not know," whereas when he spoke to his people he said: ﴿I know of no god for you other than me; so kindle for me, O Haman, upon the clay﴾ [al-Qasas 38]. It seems to me—and Allah knows best—that Pharaoh did not tell Musa "I do not know," out of fear of the immediate punishment, or fear that a book would be sent down refuting him. In any case, the man acknowledged it, and the way of his acknowledgment was silence.

* From the benefits of this noble verse: that those who call to Allah should console themselves with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when they hear what they dislike from these obstinate deniers; let them console themselves with him and say to themselves and with their tongues: "Allah, Exalted is He, knows what you say, and He will recompense them."

* And among the benefits of the noble verse: that denial of the signs of Allah is disbelief, even if a person is certain of them, as long as he denies them, even if he believes in them in his heart; he becomes a disbeliever, because the rulings of this world are applied to what? They are applied to the outward. So we declare disbelief on whoever shows disbelief even if he believes in his heart, and we remain silent about whoever shows Islam even if he is a disbeliever in his heart; because these are the rulings of this world which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has obligated, since we do not know what is in people's hearts. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) disapproved of Usama ibn Zayd when he killed a polytheist after he had said: "There is no god but Allah." Usama argued that he had said it only as a refuge, that is, out of fear of being killed, not out of conviction. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "Did you kill him after he said, 'There is no god but Allah'? Did you split open his heart?"[[Recorded by Muslim (96/158) from the hadith of Usama ibn Zayd.]]

So the affairs of this world are judged by the outward, not the inward; but in the Hereafter—we ask Allah to conceal it for us and for you—they are judged by the inward, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Indeed, He is able to return him (to life). (8) On the Day when the secrets are tested﴾ [at-Tariq 8, 9], and He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Does he not know that when what is in the graves is scattered (9) and what is in the breasts is made apparent (10)﴾ [al-Adiyat 9, 10].

If it is asked: is there another attribute by which a person becomes a disbeliever? The answer: yes, arrogance. Apostasy has only two roots: denial (juhud), and the second, arrogance (istikbar). Denial: even if one performs the acts and does not outwardly show arrogance, he becomes a disbeliever, as if he said: "The five prayers are not obligatory, but I perform them out of scrupulousness and caution." What do we say to him? We say: he is a disbeliever, because he has denied.

And arrogance: that one is arrogant toward performing what he has left, which is disbelief, not arrogance about everything. However, if a person abandons an act of obedience out of arrogance, even if it is a supererogatory (nafilah) act, we doubt his faith, because the nature of arrogance is elevation above Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and above His commands and prohibitions. So if he abandons a recommended act out of arrogance and disdain, we fear that he may be a disbeliever; but not if he abandons it deliberately and carelessly.

There is a difference, as you know from yourselves: between a person who says, "I do not pray the regular sunnah prayers out of arrogance," and another who says, "I do not pray the regular sunnah prayers because they are not obligatory upon me."

The second does not become a disbeliever nor a sinner.

As for the first, a person is in doubt about his faith, because arrogance—may Allah protect us—is elevation above the Creator and above His commands, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿So they do not deny you, but the wrongdoers deny the signs of Allah﴾.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 6, verse 34 (part 1 of 2):

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, consoled him in another way, saying: ﴿And messengers were certainly denied before you﴾. Their number was great, so much so that the Prophet ﷺ saw in a dream that a man would have only two followers, or only one, while the Prophet had no one with him at all.[[Agreed upon (Bukhari, 5752, and Muslim, 220/374), from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]]

How long did Nuh (peace be upon him) remain among his people? A thousand years less fifty years. He reminded them of the signs of Allah, he proclaimed the call openly, and he also called them in secret. But this only increased them in aversion. He was patient for a thousand years, patient over harm and mockery. He was building the ship, and whenever groups of his people passed by him, ﴿they mocked him﴾ [Hud 38]. Consider the word (malaʾ, "chiefs"): the malaʾ are the nobles, and the mockery of the nobles is not the same as the mockery of ordinary people; it is more severe in crushing and belittling a person. They were denied and harmed, ﴿so they endured patiently what they were denied﴾. "They endured patiently" means they bore the message and conveyed it despite the confrontations and harm it involved.

﴿They endured patiently what they were denied and harmed﴾ may be understood as coordinated with ﴿they were denied﴾, meaning: they endured patiently what they were denied and what they were harmed by. It may also be coordinated with ﴿were denied﴾, meaning: messengers were denied before you, and they were harmed. The two meanings do not differ much.

Were they harmed by words, or by words and deeds? By both together. Some of them were even killed. Harm by words: people mock them for their physical form, their character, and other things. The Jews said to Musa: "He is a man with a swollen scrotum (ādar), that is, one with large testicles," and this is a defect in people's eyes. Musa, peace be upon him, did not expose his private parts to them. One day he removed his garment to bathe and placed it on a rock, and the rock fled with his garment. He pursued it saying: "My garment, O rock! My garment, O rock!" But the rock did not stop except before an assembly of the Children of Israel, until they saw that Musa was innocent of what had been said about him, and Allah made their lie manifest publicly.[[Agreed upon (Bukhari, 3404, and Muslim, 339/75), from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]]

In summary, the messengers, peace be upon them, were harmed in a way that only their like could endure. Allah said to His Prophet: ﴿So be patient as the resolute messengers were patient﴾ [al-Ahqaf 35]. Indeed, when He mentioned that He had sent down the Book to him, He said: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Qur'an in gradual revelation. So be patient for the decree of your Lord﴾ [al-Insan 23-24]. He did not say: "Be thankful for the blessing of Allah." He said: ﴿So be patient for the decree of your Lord﴾, indicating that what he would suffer of harm would be because of this Book that had been sent down to him.

* A student: We said that (lahw) is a heedlessness of the heart and a play of the limbs. Can it be said that these two terms are of those words which, when they are combined, become separate, and when they are separate...?

* The Shaykh: Perhaps it can be said: when one of them is mentioned alone, the other is implied by it.

* A student: May Allah forgive you, Shaykh. Reason, Shaykh: if we look at those who made musical instruments (...), we say: this is intelligence. But in reality it is a punishment, because in any case Allah will hold them accountable just as He holds the image-makers accountable.

* The Shaykh: That is, it is a trial from Allah, Mighty and Majestic. We must know the difference between intelligence (dhakāʾ) and reason ('aql). Intelligence is quickness of perception: quickly perceiving a thing is intelligence. But reason is good conduct, and not every intelligent person is reasonable, nor is every reasonable person intelligent. Isn't that so? Among the reasonable people who uphold the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in what pleases Allah, there is one who is dull. A weak hadith has even been related: "Most of the people of Paradise are the simpletons" [al-bulh].[[Narrated by al-Bazzar (6339) from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik.]] "Al-bulh" means the simpletons, but the hadith is fabricated. Some scholars gave it an interpretation, saying: they are simple in worldly matters but intelligent in the matters of the Hereafter. But praise be to Allah, the hadith is fabricated, and we are relieved of it.

* The student: (...) They make musical instruments, and the latest manufactured items of this kind, Shaykh. Are they punished for things like these just as the image-makers are punished for them?

* The Shaykh: No, we cannot say that about them. But everyone who does wrong by means of these instruments bears a share of the sin.

* The student: Like television, like the satellite dish...

* The Shaykh: Yes indeed. I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And messengers were certainly denied before you, so they endured patiently what they were denied and harmed﴾. We already said before that this sentence is emphasized with how many emphasizers?

* A student: The entry of the lam upon it.

* The Shaykh: You have now started with the last one. The first is the preceding oath.

* The student: The second is the lam, and the third is (qad).

* The Shaykh: Well done. ﴿Messengers were denied before you, so they endured patiently what they were denied and harmed﴾. Have we mentioned an example of this? Have we mentioned an example of a messenger who was denied and harmed? Musa, peace be upon him. Is there evidence for this example?

* A student: ﴿O you who believe, do not be like those who harmed Musa, but Allah cleared him of what they said, and he was honorable in the sight of Allah﴾ [al-Ahzab 69].

* The Shaykh: Yes, well done, may Allah bless you.

He said: ﴿and they were harmed﴾ is coordinated with what?

* A student: Either it is coordinated with ﴿were denied﴾, or it is coordinated with ﴿endured patiently﴾.

* The Shaykh: With ﴿endured patiently﴾?

* The student: Yes.

* The Shaykh: Yes, that is wrong.

* A student: With ﴿what they were denied﴾ (...).

* The Shaykh: With (what they were denied) and with (what they were harmed by). Yes, and this last is more eloquent, because it indicates that they endured both matters: the denial and the harm.

He said: ﴿until Our help came to them﴾. ("Until") here indicates the endpoint, meaning: the endpoint was that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, gave them victory. This is because Allah obligated Himself to support His messengers. He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Allah has decreed: "I and My messengers will surely prevail"﴾ [al-Mujadila 21]. He, Mighty and Majestic, also said: ﴿Indeed, We will surely support Our messengers and those who believed in the life of this world and on the day when the witnesses stand﴾ [Ghafir 51].

This is not contradicted by what happens to some prophets in terms of not being given victory. We say: those who were not given victory either were never commanded to fight, so that there would be victory, or we say that victory is of two kinds: an immediate victory for the Prophet, which he experiences in his lifetime, and a deferred victory for his call, which will have its triumph after him. There is also a deferred victory in the Hereafter.

﴿Until Our help came to them, and none can alter the words of Allah﴾ [al-An'am 34]. That is: no one is able to alter the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. None alters the words of Allah except Allah alone, just as no one can reverse His judgment, so none can alter His words.

His words are His revelation that He sent down to the messengers, and likewise they are His decreeing words, by which victory is given to His prophets and humiliation to their enemies.

What has come with abrogation (naskh, the replacement of a ruling by a later one) does not contradict this. For who alters an abrogated ruling? Allah. The verse indicates that no one alters the words of Allah, but Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has the right to alter them, as He said: ﴿Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten, We bring forth one better than it or similar to it﴾ [al-Baqarah 106].

He, Mighty and Majestic, also said: ﴿And when We substitute one verse in place of another, and Allah knows best what He sends down, they say, "You are but a fabricator." Rather, most of them do not know﴾ [al-Nahl 101].

﴿None can alter the words of Allah, and there has certainly come to you from the news of the messengers﴾. This sentence is emphasized with three emphasizers: the implied oath, the lam, and (qad).

The address is to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace. That is: there has certainly come to you, O Messenger, from the news of the messengers.

﴿From the news of the messengers﴾: that is, from the news that came to them, which is the revelation. This meaning is the one that comes to mind first.

The second meaning: ﴿There has certainly come to you from the news of the messengers﴾, that is, from their stories and their accounts, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And each [account] We relate to you from the news of the messengers, by which We strengthen your heart﴾ [Hud 120].

Accordingly, the verse has two meanings. The first: there has come to you news of the revelation that came to the messengers before you. The second: their accounts have come to you, and it has become clear to you what happened to the messengers from their opponents, and what happened to their followers.

﴿And there has certainly come to you from the news of the messengers﴾.

* In this verse there are benefits:

* Among them: a clarification that the denial of the prophets is not a new phenomenon of their time, but is ancient, as shown by His saying: ﴿And messengers were certainly denied before you, so they endured patiently﴾.

If someone asks: what is the wisdom in sending messengers when they will be denied?

The answer: it is to establish the proof against them, that is, against the deniers. For if no messenger had come to these deniers, they would have said: "Our Lord, why did You not send a messenger to us?" If no messenger had come to them, they would have had an argument. For this reason Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Nuh and the prophets after him﴾ [al-Nisa' 163], up to His saying: ﴿messengers as bearers of good news and warners, so that people will have no argument against Allah after the messengers﴾ [al-Nisa' 165].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the transgression of some of the children of Adam, for whom the signs come and yet they deny. For no messenger whom Allah sent failed to bring signs such that humans would believe on the basis of their like. This is a necessary matter: that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gives the messengers the signs by which the proof is established. So when they deny the messengers despite these signs, that becomes evidence of the great extent of the transgression of these deniers.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: Allah's consolation of His Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace. For when a person knows that others have suffered what he has suffered, the matter becomes easier for him. We have mentioned in the tafsir (exegesis) examples of this from the Qur'an and from the speech of the Arabs. From the Qur'an: a person is consoled by others.

* A student: ﴿And it will not benefit you today, since you have wronged, that you are sharing in the punishment﴾ [al-Zukhruf 39].

* The Shaykh: His saying, Exalted: ﴿And it will not benefit you today, since you have wronged, that you are sharing in the punishment﴾. And from the sayings of the Arabs?

* The student: The verse of al-Khansa':
"Were it not for the great number of those weeping around me over their brothers, I would have killed myself.
But they do not weep like my brother, yet I console myself for him with consolation."

* The Shaykh: Excellent. And reality bears witness to this. If a person is struck by an accident and his leg is broken, then another person is struck by an accident and his leg is severed at the thigh, what happens? Yes, he is consoled, and the calamity becomes easier for him.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: praise of the messengers, peace be upon them, for their patience over what they were denied and over what they were harmed by.

* And among its benefits as well: it is obligatory for us to take them as examples, and to console ourselves also with what happened to the messengers, peace be upon them. So we endure patiently the harm of whoever stands against our call. We endure patiently, and the good outcome belongs to the righteous, by His saying: ﴿So they endured patiently what they were denied and harmed, until Our help came to them﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the enemies of the messengers do not limit themselves to mere denial, but harm the messengers and their followers. Harm may be physical, may be financial, may be intellectual, may be military: many types. The disbeliever seeks the nearest means by which harm can reach the Muslim, there is no doubt about this, and if he could destroy the Muslim nations overnight, he would do so.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the relief of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, comes with the intensity of distress. Whenever distress intensifies, know that relief has drawn near. This is confirmed by His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿For indeed, with hardship there is ease. Indeed, with hardship there is ease﴾ [al-Sharh 5-6]. So Allah placed two eases against one hardship. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, said: "Know that victory comes with patience, that relief comes with distress, and that with hardship there is ease."[[Narrated by Ahmad (2803) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn 'Abbas.]]

This is the word of Allah and the word of His Messenger, true and sincere. But souls may fall into failure and so not be patient.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that victory is to be hoped for only from Allah. His saying: ﴿until Our help came to them﴾; He did not say "until so-and-so helped them." He said: ﴿until Our help came to them﴾. When we know that victory comes only from Allah, from whom do we seek victory? From Allah, Mighty and Majestic. For this reason the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, was brief on the day of Badr in his shelter, earnestly asking his Lord, Blessed and Exalted, for victory until Allah gave him victory.[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (2915) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]] Praise be to Allah, you should seek victory only from Allah. Even in scholarly debate, do not seek victory from so-and-so who agrees or disagrees with you; seek victory from Allah. If you have reached the truth, ask Allah to give you victory, or ask Allah to guide you to the straight path.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that none can alter the words of Allah. That is, no one can change them. If Allah decrees victory, no one can prevent it, and if He decrees humiliation, no one can prevent it. As for the cosmic words, the impossibility of altering them is clear: the cosmic words must come to pass, "Be, and it is." Allah, Exalted, said: "Be" for the descent of rain, and it descended; no one can stop it. He said: "Be" for the withholding of rain, and it is withheld; no one can send it down.

Thus it is settled that no one is able to alter the cosmic words. As for the legislative words, some people do alter them, but this alteration is false, and falsehood has no legal validity. Does this apply to whoever alters the legislative words, whether in the earlier nations or in this nation? But is this alteration not one of the characteristics of these words? No, they cannot do it; however much they try, it is impossible. If they alter them outwardly, what they alter is false, and falsehood has no authority.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the power, greatness, and dominion of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for none can alter His words except Allah, Mighty and Majestic. However great the authority, power, might, and armies may be, His words will not be changed.

If someone asks: what do you say about abrogation (naskh)? Does it not involve alteration? Yes, it involves alteration. But who alters it? Allah, Mighty and Majestic. His abrogating words cannot be altered, meaning it is impossible for us to nullify the abrogating ruling, because they are the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿None can alter the words of Allah, and there has certainly come to you from the news of the messengers﴾ [al-An'am 34].

* Also among the benefits of the verse: the establishment that Allah speaks. This is filled throughout the Qur'an. The noble verse in His saying, Exalted: ﴿And Allah spoke to Musa with direct speech﴾ [al-Nisa' 164] confirms this, because "direct speech" (taklīman) is an emphatic verbal noun, and an emphatic verbal noun negates the possibility of metaphor.

Are the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, with letters or without letters? With letters, otherwise they would not be speech. With sounds or without sounds? Yes, with sound: Allah speaks with an audible sound. It is impossible for speech to be a meaning existing within the soul, because this meaning existing in the soul, O our brothers, is it called speech? It is called an inner discourse (ḥadīth nafs), and is not called speech. Speech is what the tongue utters, not what lodges in the heart. For this reason, when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wants to express inner discourse, He describes it as in His saying: ﴿And they say to themselves, "Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?"﴾ [al-Mujadila 8].

Groups have differed about speech, groups that passed before us in the book al-Nuniyya (the poem of Ibn al-Qayyim). Among the clearest and most prominent of them: First, the school of the Mu'tazila. They say: the speech of Allah is created sounds. Allah created sounds, as He created the sounds of thunder and lightning. They are entirely created, separate from Allah, and are only attributed to Allah as an honor, as in His saying: "the she-camel of Allah," "the House of Allah," "the mosques of Allah," and what is similar to that.

The second group: the Ash'aris, who claim that they are the ones who debated the Mu'tazila. They said: the speech of Allah is the meaning existing in the self, a meaning existing in a self, which is not heard, has no sound and no letters. But He created sounds and letters to express what is in His self. By Allah, is there any difference between their school and the school of the Mu'tazila?
