Not a difference, as some of our scholars said. He said: there is no difference between them and the Mu'tazilah, because we all agree that what is in this mushaf is created. But the Mu'tazilah said: it is created in reality, and it is the speech of Allah in reality. And those Ash'aris said: it is not the speech of Allah in reality; the speech of Allah is that which subsists in His self, and this is an expression of the speech of Allah. So which of them is closer to the truth in terms of the principles? The Mu'tazilah are closer, the Mu'tazilah are closer to the truth.

As for the people of truth, the Salaf and those who followed them among the Imams, they said: Allah, may He be exalted, speaks in His own manner, speaks with audible speech, with ordered letters, and speech cannot be conceived except in this way.

If someone says: Is everything Allah creates, whether little or much, created by the word "Be" (kun)?

The answer: the apparent meaning of the texts is so. Everything Allah creates, He says to it: "Be." This is why the words of Allah are without end: ﴿Say: If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would be exhausted before the words of my Lord were exhausted, even if We brought the like of it as a supplement﴾ [al-Kahf 109]. It is also possible that He, may He be exalted, said "Be" at the beginning of the matter, and then the one addressed carries out what he was commanded, just as He said to the pen: "Write what will be," and it wrote what would be.[[Narrated by Abu Dawud (4700) and al-Tirmidhi (3319) from the hadith of 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit.]]

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: affirmation of the prophethood of the Prophet ﷺ, just as the messages of those before him were affirmed; by His saying: ﴿And there has certainly come to you the news of the messengers﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: emphasis on the prophethood of the Prophet (ﷺ), by means of the oath, the lam, and (qad).

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the Noble Qur'an observes the endings of verses (fawasil); by His saying: ﴿And there has certainly come to you the news of the messengers﴾, and He said in another verse: ﴿And We relate to you the news of the messengers, by which We strengthen your heart﴾ [Hud 120].
The observance of the endings is evident in the Noble Qur'an. Look at Surah Ta-Ha; look at Surah Iqtarabat al-Sa'ah, until He said: ﴿And We carried him upon a [vessel] of planks and nails﴾ [al-Qamar 13]. Dusur: plural of disar, which is the nail.
All of that is so that the surah's verses correspond in their endings; this is because it is from eloquence, and because it is something the ears attend to, and because it is something the hearts find delight in. These are three benefits of the correspondence of the noble verses.

* Among the benefits of the verse: it may contain an indication that Muhammad is the Seal of the Messengers; by His saying: ﴿And there has certainly come to you the news of the messengers﴾, meaning: those who were sent. If this benefit can be drawn from the verse, well and good; otherwise, that he is the Seal of the Prophets is a matter agreed upon, stated explicitly in the Noble Qur'an in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Muhammad is not the father of any one of your men, but he is the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets﴾ [al-Ahzab 40], meaning: but he was the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets. O Allah, send blessings and peace upon him.

* Student: May Allah be good to you. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while there has not yet come to you the example of those who passed on before you? Adversity and hardship touched them, and they were shaken until the Messenger and those who believed with him said, "When is the help of Allah?"﴾ [al-Baqarah 214]. There is no doubt that the Messenger of Allah is truthful, but what is the meaning of this saying, "When is the help of Allah?"

* The Shaykh: "When is the help of Allah?" They do not say this out of doubting its likelihood, but they say it out of haste; they are hastening the help of Allah, not out of doubt or uncertainty.

* The student: May Allah bless you, O Shaykh. In the previous tafsir lesson we established that the roots of apostasy lie in denial and arrogance, and that one may fear for a person who abandons a sunnah out of arrogance that he may disbelieve. Then yesterday there passed with us the hadith of the one who refused to eat except with his left hand, which the Prophet ﷺ explained by saying that nothing prevented him except arrogance. Does our caution in saying "one fears disbelief for him" indicate that there is arrogance and arrogance, that there is an arrogance which does not expel one from the religion?

* The Shaykh: "Yakhsha" (one fears) does not mean that it is certain. But if this arrogance proceeds from aversion to the law of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, then it is disbelief; as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿That is because they disliked what Allah sent down, so He nullified their deeds﴾ [Muhammad 9]. Therefore there must be humility in the heart and submission in the limbs.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 6, verse 35 (part 1 of 2):

I seek refuge with Allah from Satan the accursed. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And if their turning away is grievous to you﴾. There is no doubt that (kāna, "was/if it was") requires a subject and a predicate, and (kabura, "was grievous") requires a subject-agent. So do we say that the subject of (kāna) is a concealed pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and (kabura ʿalayka iʿrāḍuhum, "their turning away was grievous to you") is its predicate? Or do we say that (iʿrāḍuhum) is subject to a dispute: (kāna) requires it as its subject, and (kabura) requires it as its agent? Both are possible, but the first is more apt. That is: if the matter is that their turning away was grievous to you, meaning their turning away weighed heavily on you, owing to the grief and sorrow in your soul, then strive that they be guided through you. ﴿So if you are able to seek a tunnel in the earth or a ladder into the sky and bring them a sign﴾: meaning, then do it, but you have no duty except patience.

This sentence, ﴿if their turning away is grievous to you﴾, is followed by another conditional clause, ﴿so if you are able﴾, and this is the interlocking of two conditional clauses, such that the second clause stands in the place of the jussive (jazm) as the response of the first clause. This occurs in the Qur'an and in the speech of the Arabs.

As for the Qur'an: like this verse, and like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Then why, if you are not to be judged, do you not bring it back, if you are truthful?﴾ [al-Wāqiʿa 86–87]. This is a conditional within a conditional.

And from it is the saying of the Arabs:
"If you seek our aid, if you are frightened, you will find..." ∗∗∗ ..................................
The first conditional verb is followed by a second which qualifies it, and (tajidū, "you will find") is the response of the first condition.

In short, ﴿if their turning away is grievous to you﴾ is a conditional clause, meaning a conditional clause within another conditional clause. The first: ﴿if their turning away is grievous to you﴾; the second: ﴿so if you are able to seek a tunnel in the earth or a ladder into the sky﴾.

The response of the second clause is omitted. The estimate is: then do it, but you will not be able to do that. If you cannot do it, then you cannot bring the signs they proposed; and if you cannot do it, do not grieve over them, for a person does not grieve except over a thing he is able to do and did not do.

﴿Their turning away was grievous to you﴾: meaning, it was great and burdensome to you.

﴿So if you are able﴾: meaning, if you are capable of ﴿seeking a tunnel in the earth﴾: meaning, seeking a tunnel in the earth. The tunnel (nafaq) is a underground passage dug into the earth, into which a person enters to reach the depths of the earth. So the verse here: ﴿then bring them a sign﴾. ﴿Or a ladder into the sky﴾: you seek a ladder into the sky, meaning a means of ascent by which you rise into the air ﴿and bring them a sign﴾.

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has thus shown him descent and ascent: he is unable to go down into a tunnel in the earth to extract signs, nor to ascend into the sky to bring signs. Is the meaning clear? It is clear.

If he cannot do this, which is known to all, then he cannot bring what they have proposed of signs, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says in another verse: ﴿And they say: "Why has no sign been sent down to him from his Lord?" Say: "Signs are only with Allah, and I am only a clear warner."﴾ [al-ʿAnkabūt 50]. ﴿And had Allah willed, He would have gathered them upon guidance﴾. (law, "had") is a conditional particle; the verb of the condition is (shāʾa, "willed") and its response is (la-jamaʿahum, "He would have gathered them"). But where is the object of (shāʾa)? Do we estimate it to match the wording of the response, or do we estimate it with another meaning?

Some estimated it as: ﴿And had Allah willed﴾ their guidance ﴿He would have gathered them upon guidance﴾, and others estimated it as: ﴿And had Allah willed﴾ that He gather them upon guidance ﴿He would have gathered them upon guidance﴾. Which is more appropriate? The second, or the first?

The second: we estimate the omitted element to match what is present, that is: and had Allah willed to gather them upon guidance. Gathering them upon guidance is greater than mere guidance, for they might be guided without being gathered.

And we should apply this in every similar case: ﴿And had Allah willed, they would not have fought one another﴾ [al-Baqara 253]. What do we estimate? "And had Allah willed that they not fight, they would not have fought." Estimating the thing to match what is present is preferable to estimating something that does not match, and we do not know whether Allah willed it or not, so what is before us is the determined reading.

Thus: and had Allah willed to gather them upon guidance, He would have gathered them, because hearts are in the hand of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. This is like His saying: ﴿And had your Lord willed, He would have made mankind one community﴾ [Hūd 118]; that is, upon the religion of Islam. ﴿Had Allah willed, He would have guided all mankind﴾ [al-Raʿd 31], because the whole matter is in the hand of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

﴿So do not be among the ignorant﴾. A prohibition emphasized by what? The prohibition here is emphasized by what? ﴿So do not be among the ignorant﴾ with the emphatic nūn: meaning, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, forbids him with an emphatic prohibition from being among the ignorant.

Ignorance is of two kinds: ignorance of foolishness (safaha) and ignorance as the absence of knowledge. Which is meant? The second, without doubt.

An example of ignorance meaning foolishness is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Repentance is only incumbent upon Allah for those who do evil in ignorance and then repent soon﴾ [al-Nisāʾ 17]: in foolishness. The ignorance here does not mean the absence of knowledge, for absence of knowledge removes blame and sin.

So ﴿do not be among the ignorant﴾ in what sense? That is: among those who do not know the sunan (laws) of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in His creation.

If someone says: does his prohibition, blessed and exalted is He, of His Prophet from being among the ignorant necessarily mean that the Prophet ﷺ did the deeds of the ignorant?

The answer: No, as in His saying: ﴿The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters﴾ [al-Baqara 147], and He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿If you are in doubt about what We have sent down to you, then ask those who recite the Book before you. The truth has certainly come to you from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters﴾ [Yūnus 94].

So it does not follow from this conditional that the conditioned thing occurs, I mean ﴿If you associate others with Allah, your deeds will surely be nullified﴾ [al-Zumar 65] and similar verses.

﴿So do not be among the ignorant﴾: that is, among those of ignorance who do not know the laws of Allah in His creation. Pay attention: you, O Muhammad, are not ignorant, so that their turning away should weigh heavily upon you, and so that you should grieve over their not believing; for that is part of the wisdom of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Let us return to extracting the benefits:

* Among the benefits of this: that the Prophet ﷺ was grieved by the turning away of those invited to Islam.

Is this on behalf of himself, or out of desire for the guidance of Allah's servants?

The second, without doubt, and this is part of the completeness of his sincere counsel to the community, upon him be prayers and peace.

* And among the benefits of this verse: a person should not treat the turning away of people lightly; rather, he should be great in his soul, but without partisanship for what he is upon, but rather, for the sake of the benefit of others. If we see, for example, a man who is learned, devout, and generous, but who is not sound in the Names and Attributes, does this burden us or not? Yes, it burdens us, without doubt. And if we look at him with the eye of destiny, we pity him and say: "Glory be to Allah, how can this virtuous man be upon an unsound creed?!" We have mercy on him, for in truth he is deprived. But if we look at him with the eye of the Sharia, we debate with him; if he returns to the truth, this is what is sought; and if he does not return, we deal with him as al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "My ruling concerning the people of kalām is that they be beaten with palm stalks and sandals, paraded among the tribes, and it be said: 'This is the recompense of one who abandoned the Book and the Sunna and turned to the science of kalām.'"

A man who commits adultery, who is of the elite of the people and among the people of goodness: if we look at him with the eye of destiny, yes, we have mercy on him and feel tenderness for him; how could this proceed from him?! But if we look at him with the eye of the Sharia, we establish the legal punishment upon him and do not show him compassion, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿The adulterer and the adulteress, lash each one of them a hundred lashes, and let not pity for them detain you in the religion of Allah﴾ [al-Nūr 2]. He did not say "in the decree of Allah"; He said "in the religion of Allah" ﴿if you believe in Allah and the Last Day﴾ [al-Nūr 2]. Do you understand? And for this reason there came in the hadith, though there is discussion about it: "Overlook the slips of people of good standing, except in matters of the prescribed punishments (ḥudūd)." [Narrated by Abū Dāwūd (4375) from the hadith of ʿĀʾisha.]

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: Allah, glorified and exalted, may illustrate an impossible matter by setting forth an example of it without mentioning it explicitly. Its aspect: Allah said: ﴿So if you are able to seek a tunnel in the earth or a ladder into the sky and bring them a sign﴾. That is: then do it. Instead of saying: "If their turning away is grievous to you, then they will not believe," which is what would be expected, Allah, Exalted, set forth an example so that it would be persuasive to the Messenger ﷺ and to others also.

* And among the benefits of this verse: we say, and pay attention: the refuges (malājiʾ) are of two kinds: either a tunnel in the earth or an ascent into the sky. Does this hold? Or do we say that seeking evidence may come from the earth and may come from the sky? Seeking evidence for validity, the validity of what a person says?

The apparent view is that the second is more apt, because Allah only said that to him not so that he would take refuge, but so that he would bring what testifies for him; and for this reason He said: ﴿then bring them a sign﴾.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: every prophet must have a sign, and this is part of the wisdom of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Consider: if a man came from outside this community and claimed to be a messenger, and said: "I am a messenger, my method is such, my creed is such, my worship is such, so obey me," without any sign, would this be wise, or not? It is not wise. And whoever disbelieves him is excused; otherwise every liar and impostor would claim to be a prophet, or perhaps claim to be a lord.

So the signs contain victory for the messengers and mercy toward those to whom they are sent, so that they may believe with certainty.

* And among the benefits of these noble verses: guidance and misguidance are in the hand of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; by His saying: ﴿And had Allah willed, He would have gathered them upon guidance﴾.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of a level of faith in destiny, namely the will (mashīʾa): that Allah, Exalted, has willed all the actions of His servants. The levels of destiny have passed over us, I think, many times, and they are four:
Knowledge, writing, will, and creation. They are gathered in the saying of the poet:
"Knowledge, writing, our Lord's will, and His creation, which is origination and bringing into being."
These are the four levels.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: the wisdom of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in making people into two categories: believers and disbelievers.

This is a necessary matter, for were it not for disbelief, the worth of faith would not be known; and were it not for faith, the ugliness of disbelief would not be known, is that not so? Just as were it not for sweetness, bitterness would not be known, and this is clear. If there were no opposites, the excellence of praiseworthy things would not be known. Moreover, were it not for people differing over faith and disbelief, the banner of jihad would not have been raised, for they would all be either believers or disbelievers, so who would fight?

Were it not for this difference, the enjoining of good and forbidding of evil would not have been established, for people would all be either upon evil or upon good.

Were it not for this difference, the calling to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, would not have been established, for if they were all believers they would have no need of a call, and if they were all disbelievers, there would be no call. Is this clear? So among the wisdom is that Allah made creation into two categories. But someone may say: if one of the people is of the other category, the disbelieving one, would this not be an injustice to him?

This may occur to the soul, so long as we say that disbelief is by the will of Allah, and that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in His wisdom divided people into two divisions; would the disbeliever not say: "This is an injustice to me"?

The answer: No, as some of the People of the Sunna said when debating a Mu'tazilite who said: "Tell me: if He withheld guidance from me and decreed wretchedness for me, has He wronged me or not?"

The Sunni said to him: "If He withheld from you what was yours, then He has wronged you; but if He withheld what is His bounty, then that is the bounty of Allah, which He gives to whom He wills."

I repeat the first question: "Tell me: if He withheld guidance from me and decreed wretchedness upon me, has He done good to me or wronged me?"

He said to him: "If He withheld from you what was yours, then He has wronged you; but if He withheld what is His bounty, then that is the bounty of Allah, which He gives to whom He wills."

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who invents a lie against Allah or denies His signs?﴾ [al-Anʿām 21]. This interrogative is in the sense of what?

* Student: This interrogative is in the sense of negation, and the meaning is: no one is more unjust.

* The Shaykh: No one is more unjust. What is the benefit of using an interrogative for negation?

* Student: Emphasis of the negation.

* The Shaykh: Emphasis of the negation. And what else?

* Student: That is: no one is more unjust than this.

* The Shaykh: And what else?

* Student: Restricting it to this.

* The Shaykh: No. How is it more eloquent in negation?

* Student: It is infused with a challenge, I mean.

* The Shaykh: It is infused with a challenge, meaning it includes a challenge, as if it were said: "If you are truthful, then show me who is more unjust."

Now, such a phrase occurs with another sin, other than this, such as His saying: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who prevents the mention of Allah's name in His mosques and strives for their ruin?﴾ [al-Baqara 114]. So how do we answer?

* Student: We answer, may Allah be good to you, O Shaykh, that this is specific to this sin: that in preventing the mosques, no one is more unjust than one who prevents the mosques of Allah; and this is a fabrication against Allah, a lie; and each is specific to its own.

* The Shaykh: That is, its meaning is that preventing a place of worship, or of dealings, or of study, the greatest of these is preventing the mosques of Allah from His name being mentioned in them; so this is a relative matter. Now, the greatest fabrication?

* Student: Its greatest is one who fabricates a lie against Allah, or denies His signs.

* The Shaykh: Fabricating a lie against Allah. Is there another aspect?

* Student: That all of these share in being the most unjust, and each station is according to its own measure.

* The Shaykh: Good. You say: all of them share in being the most unjust thing, yes, and everything has its punishment.

His saying: ﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed﴾ [al-Anʿām 21]. Have we found someone who succeeded while being a wrongdoer?

* Student: It appears that they have succeeded in this world, but in reality we do not know their condition; there may befall them, in matters of the soul and the inner self, what we do not know. As for the Hereafter, there is no doubt that they will be held to account for what they did in this world; they did not succeed.

* The Shaykh: Yes, as if you are saying: success has kinds. These, although they succeed outwardly and materially, have not succeeded inwardly; you find their souls in regret, in sorrow, in pain, yes. Or something else may be said: ﴿the wrongdoers will not succeed﴾ meaning absolute success, after which they do not relapse; or it may be said: ﴿the wrongdoers will not succeed﴾ in the Hereafter, for even if it were supposed that these were not afflicted with illnesses and did not relapse from success, there is the Last Day after them, in which they will not succeed.

So the negation is to be taken according to one of three aspects.

* * *

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And among them are those who listen to you﴾ [al-Anʿām 25]. To whom does the pronoun refer?

* Student: To these deniers.

* The Shaykh: To these deniers. Now, do they benefit from this listening or not?

* Student: ﴿And We have placed over their hearts coverings﴾ [al-Anʿām 25].

* The Shaykh: Is the answer yes or no?

* Student: They do not benefit.

* The Shaykh: They do not benefit. The evidence?

* Student: His saying, glorified and exalted: ﴿And We have placed over their hearts coverings, lest they understand it, and in their ears deafness; and if they see every sign, they will not believe in it﴾ [al-Anʿām 25].

* The Shaykh: The completion of three things. Now, what is the end of their dispute?

* Student: It is mentioned in the verse.

* The Shaykh: What is it?

* Student: That they will say at the end a saying by which they deny, while their souls are certain of it: "This is nothing but the fables of the ancients."

**The Shaykh:** Obstinacy. The final stage of disputation is obstinacy. They said: ﴿This is nothing but the fables of the former peoples﴾ [al-An'am 25]. Is that clear?

It is like what exists now between the people of innovation (ahl al-bid'ah) and the people of the Sunnah (ahl al-Sunnah). You find one of them saying: "This has not been established for us, even if it is in al-Bukhari and Muslim." Or he says, regarding what he uses to support his innovation: "This is established for us by the transmission of trustworthy narrators ('udul)." This is most common among the Rafidah. For this reason it is said that some of them added about a third to the Qur'an and removed parts of it. This is a troubling obstinacy. You cannot convince the obstinate person at all, but Allah the Mighty and Majestic may guide him. So these contentious, obstinate disputants end up saying: "This is the fables of the former peoples," and that it is not revelation, and that they do not acknowledge it.

What is the difference between ﴿yanhawna 'anhu﴾ and ﴿yan'awna 'anhu﴾?

**Student:** ﴿yanhawna 'anhu﴾ means they forbid people from coming to it, and ﴿yan'awna 'anhu﴾ means they keep themselves away from hearing it.

**The Shaykh:** Yes. That is, they keep themselves far away and forbid people from listening to the Messenger (ﷺ). Now, is the harm in this case upon them or upon the Messenger?

**Student:** ﴿They destroy none but themselves, yet they perceive it not﴾.

**The Shaykh:** ﴿Yet they perceive it not﴾, may Allah bless you. The Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And if only you could see when they are made to stand over the Fire﴾ [al-An'am 27]. To whom is the address?

**Student:** The address is originally to the Prophet (ﷺ), and his ummah follows him.

**The Shaykh:** Or it is to everyone to whom this address can apply, meaning: if you, O seer, or O human being, could see, regardless of whether it is addressed to the Messenger (ﷺ).

﴿They are made to stand over the Fire﴾ [al-An'am 27]. Who makes them stand over it?

**Student:** Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

**The Shaykh:** Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, through the angels. Now, what is the meaning of their saying: ﴿Would that we could be returned, and not deny the signs of our Lord﴾ [al-An'am 27]?

**Student:** They wish to return to the world, so that they would not deny what the messengers brought.

**The Shaykh:** ﴿Would that we could be returned, and not deny﴾ is in the accusative (nasb), meaning they wish to return to the world while they do not deny.

There is also a second reading: ﴿Would that we could be returned﴾, while in fact we do not deny. The difference between the two meanings is that in the first they wish to be returned to the world and not deny the signs of Allah, so it falls within wishing. In the second, ﴿and we do not deny﴾, they wished to be returned to the world and then promised not to deny the signs of their Lord. Did Allah confirm what they said?

**Student:** No.

**The Shaykh:** What is the evidence?

**Student:** Allah the Mighty and Majestic refuted them: ﴿And if they were returned, they would certainly revert to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars﴾ [al-An'am 28].

**The Shaykh:** Yes, ﴿And if they were returned, they would certainly revert to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars﴾. So their saying "we do not deny" is a false promise. Does this indicate that people will speak on the Day of Resurrection?

**Student:** Yes.

**The Shaykh:** Yes. What is the aspect of that?

**Student:** That they are saying.

**The Shaykh:** That they are saying, and that they are wishing. People in the Hereafter are in the same state as they are in this world. They have minds, and they argue and defend themselves.

﴿Those who denied the meeting with Allah have certainly lost﴾ [al-An'am 31]. What is the meaning of their denial of the meeting with Allah?

**Student:** Their denial of resurrection.

**The Shaykh:** Their denial of resurrection. That is, they deny the saying of the Most High: ﴿O man, indeed you are laboring toward your Lord with labor, and you will meet Him﴾ [al-Inshiqaq 6]. And what is their loss? Is it in this world or in the Hereafter?

**Student:** Their loss is in the Hereafter.

**The Shaykh:** And in this world?

**Student:** In this world too, there are two kinds of loss...

**The Shaykh:** In this world and the Hereafter, because in their existence in this world they gained nothing. Is that clear? This is the truth: they are the losers in this world and in the Hereafter.

Their saying: ﴿Alas for us, for our neglect concerning it﴾ [al-An'am 31]. What is its meaning?

**Student:** ﴿Alas for us, for our neglect concerning it﴾: they say this out of regret, regret over what they missed of accepting faith. They said that out of remorse and grief over their neglect of faith.

**The Shaykh:** Over their neglect in this world, in that they did not make use of their times for what pleases Allah.

If someone said to you: ﴿Alas for us﴾, is grief (hasrah) called upon?

**Student:** The particle (ya) here is for alerting (tanbih).

**The Shaykh:** For alerting. What do you all say?

**Students:** Correct.

**The Shaykh:** Correct, because when (ya) is attached to something that cannot be addressed, it is for alerting. Similar to it is the Most High's saying: ﴿He said: "Would that my people knew"﴾ [Ya-Sin 26], and similar to the previous verse: ﴿Would that we could be returned, and not deny the signs of our Lord﴾ [al-An'am 27]. Good, well done.

His saying: ﴿while they carry their burdens upon their backs﴾ [al-An'am 31]. Is this to be taken literally?

**Student:** Yes, in the Hereafter it is literal.

**The Shaykh:** In the Hereafter it is literal. That is, these burdens are made like tangible things carried upon the backs, as an increase in their disgrace and punishment.

I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Only those who listen respond﴾ [al-An'am 36]. Yastajību (responds) and yujību (answers) have the same meaning.

The sentence contains restriction (ḥaṣr), whose means is (innamā) ("only"). The meaning is: none responds to your call, O Muhammad, except those who listen.

The listening intended here is listening of compliance and acceptance, not listening of mere perception, because listening of perception includes the righteous and the wicked, the believer and the disbeliever. What indicates this distinction, that is, between listening of acceptance and submission and listening of perception, is the saying of the Blessed and Exalted: ﴿And do not be like those who said, "We hear," while they do not hear﴾ [al-Anfal 21], meaning: they do not respond or submit. The Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿Only those who listen respond﴾. (alladhīna) is grammatically the subject (fā'il) of (yastajību).

Then He said: ﴿And the dead—Allah will resurrect them﴾ [al-An'am 36]. This is a new, independent sentence (jumla mustaʾnafa), and it is not correct to join it by conjunction to what precedes it, ﴿And the dead—Allah will resurrect them﴾.

Al-mawtā (the dead) is the plural of mayyit. Is the intended meaning the dead of hearts or the dead of bodies?

On this, the scholars have two opinions.

Some of them said: the dead are those whom Allah will resurrect, meaning the dead of hearts, and they are the disbelievers, whom Allah will resurrect and then recompense.

Others said: the dead are the dead of bodies, whom Allah will resurrect, in refutation of those who deny the resurrection.

When a verse admits two meanings, neither of which is more apparent than the other, and there is no contradiction between them, what is the rule?

It is that the verse is to be understood as referring to both together. So the dead among these disbelievers, Allah will resurrect them and recompense them. And the dead of bodies, whose souls have departed from their bodies, Allah will resurrect them. Thus the verse contains a threat and a warning, and a refutation of those who deny the resurrection. ﴿Allah will resurrect them﴾, meaning: He will bring them out of their graves on the Day of Resurrection.

﴿Then to Him they will be returned﴾, meaning: after the resurrection they will return to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and their affair will be with Allah the Exalted; at that time there will be no disputant or argumentative party.

In this noble verse, the response to the call of the messengers is restricted to those who—what? Those who listen with perception, or those who listen with acceptance and submission? Those who listen with acceptance and submission.

* Among the benefits of this verse: the more a person listens to the words of Allah and His Messenger, the stronger his response becomes. This is derived from the well-known principle: whatever is attached to a description increases in strength in proportion to the strength of that description to which the ruling is attached. An example of this is the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Indeed, the best one you could hire is the strong, the trustworthy﴾ [al-Qasas 28]. The stronger he is, the better and more beneficial he is; likewise trustworthiness: the more trustworthy, the better. The point of this beneficial principle is: everything attached to a description increases in strength in proportion to the strength of that description.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of the resurrection. It is one of the six pillars of faith which the Prophet (ﷺ) told Gabriel about when he said: "Tell me about faith." He said: "That you believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and divine decree, both its good and its evil." [Narrated by Muslim (1/8) from the hadith of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab.]

* Also among them: these disbelievers are in the position of the dead, because they do not benefit from what they hear, just as the dead do not benefit from what they hear, being a corpse. Likewise these disbelievers.

* Among them: a threat to those disbelievers who do not listen, that Allah will resurrect them and then recompense them.

* Among them: the complete power of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, shown in the resurrection. The resurrection, unlike the gradual giving of life (as in the growth of a child who comes out small and then grows until he is complete), is such that all of them are resurrected in a single moment. Read the saying of Allah the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿But it will be just one shout, and at once they will be on the surface of the earth﴾ [al-Nazi'at 13–14]; and He said: ﴿It will be but one shout, and at once they will all be brought before Us﴾ [Ya-Sin 53]; and He said: ﴿And Our command is but a single word, like a glance of the eye﴾ [al-Qamar 50].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the final return is to Allah the Mighty and Majestic, based on His saying: ﴿Then to Him they will be returned﴾ [al-An'am 36]. This return contains restriction, whose means is the fronting of the complement (taqdīm al-ma'mūl) in the saying ﴿to Him they will be returned﴾. The benefit of this fronting, that is, the fronting of the complement in this verse, is both verbal and semantic.

As for the semantic benefit, it is the conveying of restriction, and that there is no return except to Allah. As for the verbal benefit, it is to match the endings of the verses (ru'us al-ayat), because the matching of verse endings is part of eloquence. Look at the whole of Surah Ta-Ha, whose verse endings are almost all with alif. When the mention of Musa and Harun came, he placed Harun before Musa so that the verses would match, though it is well known that Musa is better than Harun.

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And they say, "Why has not a sign been sent down to him from his Lord?"﴾ [al-An'am 37]. ﴿They say﴾, meaning: the obstinate ones who denied the Messenger and sought to make things difficult for him. ﴿"Why has not a sign been sent down to him from his Lord?"﴾ They mean by this the signs they had proposed, such as their saying: ﴿And they say, "We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth, or [until] you have a garden of palm trees and grapevines and make rivers gush forth within them in force, or you make the sky fall upon us in fragments as you have claimed, or you bring Allah and the angels before us in opposition, or you have a house of gold, or you ascend into the sky"﴾ [al-Isra' 90-93]. And despite that they say: ﴿"We will not believe in your ascension until you bring down to us a book we can read"﴾ [al-Isra' 93]. Yes, and other signs they proposed. But it is part of the wisdom of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that He closed this door and blocked it, I mean the door of proposing [signs] to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. For signs are with whom? With Allah, Glorified and Exalted. It is He who brings them, not the proposals of creation. And when creation proposes a specific sign and then it is brought and they still do not believe, they are destroyed. This is the custom of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

It is not objected to this that the Quraysh said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Show us a sign, O Muhammad." So he pointed to the moon and it split into two halves. [Agreed upon: al-Bukhari (3636) and Muslim (2800/43), from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud.]

The scholars said: They were not destroyed only because they did not propose a sign.

This is the custom of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

It is not objected to this that "the Quraysh said to the Prophet (ﷺ): 'Show us a sign, O Muhammad,' so he pointed to the moon and it split into two halves" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3636) and Muslim (2800/43), in a similar wording, from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud]. The scholars said: They were not destroyed because they did not propose a specific sign; and had they proposed a specific sign, and it had come and they still did not believe, they would have been destroyed. Thus did the scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, establish.

As for His saying: ﴿"Why has not a sign been sent down to him from his Lord?"﴾ [al-An'am 37]. ﴿Sign (ayah)﴾ means: an indication that proves his truthfulness and the soundness of his message. Here we pause to clarify that some scholars—and how many of them there are—express the signs of the messengers as "miracles" (mu'jizat), and this is a grave deficiency. For if we named them miracles, what the magicians do would be an objection to us, for the magicians do what human beings are unable to do. But "ayah" specifies the meaning, which is: the sign of his truthfulness and the soundness of his message. Therefore you will never find in the Qur'an that Allah described the signs of the messengers as "miracles" at all; rather He describes them as what? As ayat (signs).

As for His saying: ﴿"from his Lord"﴾, they mean by it Allah, Mighty and Majestic. In this expression there is arrogance and haughtiness, for they said: ﴿"from his Lord"﴾ and did not say "from Allah," as though they were on one side and the Messenger (ﷺ) with Allah on another side. They did not say "from our Lord," nor "from Allah."

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say, "Indeed, Allah is able to send down a sign"﴾. He is not incapable of sending down a sign; rather He is able. When the disciples asked Jesus to send down upon them a table from the heaven, was Allah able to do it? Yes, Allah was able to do it, according to the view of those who say it was sent down. Likewise, the signs of the messengers, sensory and intellectual, are all from Allah. He is able to send down a sign, but He does not wish to bring what these people request, for if signs came according to proposals, each one would propose whatever he considered a sign, and he might propose what he considers a sign but is not one. Therefore we say: the signs are with Allah, Mighty and Majestic. For this reason He said: ﴿Say, "Indeed, Allah is able to send down a sign"﴾. But does He wish it or not? He does not wish it, and when He does not wish it, it does not occur.

﴿But most of them do not know﴾, meaning: they do not know that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is the One who sends down signs; He is able to bring a sign and able not to bring a sign. So they are ignorant. Had they had knowledge, they would have known that the Prophet (ﷺ) cannot bring a sign; rather it is Allah who brings it.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the obstinacy of these deniers, for they argued by this that Allah had not sent down a sign to them. But is this claim true or false? By Allah, it is false. The signs of the Prophet (ﷺ) are visible and well known. Among his great signs is this Qur'an, which caused the leaders of Quraysh to slip away secretly at night to listen to the Prophet's recitation, for it had enchanted their minds and amazed them greatly, yet they remained obstinate.

Likewise, there are many sensory signs, such as what happened to his uncle Abu Talib of blessings in his family and wealth because of his guardianship of the Prophet (ﷺ).

Likewise, also, the turning away of his enemies from him, peace and blessings be upon him: ﴿And We have put before them a barrier and behind them a barrier, and We have covered them, so they do not see﴾ [Ya-Sin 9]. The signs are many, and they know them, but they are what? Arrogant.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the arrogance and haughtiness of these people, for they said: ﴿"from his Lord"﴾; they did not say "from our Lord," nor "from Allah," as though they were on one side and the Messenger (ﷺ) and Allah on another side.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, defends His Prophet (ﷺ), for He answers on his behalf when they said: ﴿"Why has not a sign been sent down to him from his Lord?"﴾. There is no doubt that this places pressure on the Messenger, peace be upon him, so Allah the Exalted answers for him, supporting him: ﴿Say, "Indeed, Allah is able to send down a sign"﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of the power of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, by His saying: ﴿"Indeed, Allah is able to send down a sign"﴾. This power is complete power, to which no incapacity attaches, by the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿And Allah is not to be frustrated by anything in the heavens or on the earth. Indeed, He is ever Knowing and Competent﴾ [Fatir 44]. Because of the perfection of His knowledge and power, nothing can frustrate Him, for incapacity regarding a thing has a cause: either ignorance or weakness. Allah is Knowing and Competent.

This power relates to everything; He is competent over all things. Do not investigate as the over-deep and excessive theologians (mutakallimun) investigated, whether it relates to the possible, the necessary and the impossible, or only to the possible and necessary, excluding the impossible. This is empty talk. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has affirmed His power absolutely, and Allah is competent over all things.

There is a saying of some of them: "Power excludes its own essence, so He is not capable over Himself." This is empty talk, for reason indicates that Allah cannot act upon Himself. This would mean the nullification of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, from every act, since He would be unable to do anything concerning Himself; whereas we say: Allah is competent over all things.

If someone says: "Do you say that Allah is able to destroy Himself?" We seek Allah's protection from this. The answer: Allah, Glorified and Exalted, has affirmed for Himself perfection in every respect, and destruction is a deficiency, so it is impossible. This question does not arise, but the theologians raise it in order to reach the conclusion that power does not relate to the impossible.

It is related that Satan places his throne upon the sea and sends his armies to mislead people. When a worshipper dies, he is not concerned by that; when a scholar dies, he rejoices greatly. His armies said to him: "How can you rejoice so much at the death of a scholar, while you are not concerned by a worshipper?" He said: "Because the scholar is more harmful to me than the worshipper. When the worshipper dies, only he himself is lost, but when the scholar dies, the whole community is lost. When the scholar is guided, Allah guides a community through him, while the worshipper stays in his mosque."

If you wish, I will give you an example. It is said that he sent to a worshipper and said to him: "Such-and-such, can Allah, Mighty and Majestic, place the heavens and the earth all in an egg? Is He able to?" The worshipper said: "No; the heavens all in an egg—by my reasoning, I say, I do not know—he says: I, if I were in an egg, would not fit; how could the heavens and the earth? It is not possible." He then went to the scholar and said to him: "Can Allah place the heavens and the earth in an egg?" He said: "Yes; indeed His command, when He wills something, is to say to it 'Be,' and it is." So the messenger came and said: "Look, this worshipper has disbelieved and does not know; he denied the power of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, while that one believed. His command, when He wills something, is only to say to it 'Be,' and it is."

In any case, my intent is that going deep into these matters is an error. Affirm what Allah has affirmed for Himself, namely that Allah is competent over all things, and turn away from anything other than that.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the acts of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, are conditioned by His will; meaning that what He does not will does not occur, even though He is able to do it, by His saying: ﴿"Able to send down a sign"﴾, meaning: but He did not will it.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that most of these deniers do not know the reality of the matter, for they did not reflect; had they reflected, they would have known, but they are turning away.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 6, verse 38:

Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿There is no creature that crawls upon the earth, nor bird that flies on its two wings, but they are communities like you﴾ [al-An'am 38]. Glory be to God! ﴿There is no creature that crawls upon the earth﴾: by "creature" (dabbah) is meant everything that moves upon the earth on many feet, or four, or two, or that creeps on its belly. That is, any creature on the earth.

﴿Nor bird that flies on its two wings﴾: He mentions the earthly creatures and the airborne creatures that glide through the air. ﴿Nor bird that flies on its two wings but they are communities like you﴾: the birds of all their kinds, and likewise the creatures of the earth of all their kinds, are all communities like us. They differ in their species, differ in their colours, differ in their abilities, differ in their sustenance, differ in their languages, just as we too are communities.

His saying ﴿bird that flies on its two wings﴾ is an emphasis (tawkid), because it is well known that a bird flies only with its wings, just as when you say: "he walks on his legs," or "he sees with his eyes," or "he hears with his ears," and the like; it is an emphasis.

As for the claim of some that this is a qualifier that excludes aircraft, because aircraft fly without two wings, this is a mistake, because something that was not known at that time cannot be the subject of an exclusion, since it was not relevant at all. So the correct view is that His saying ﴿flies on its two wings﴾ is an emphasis.

Yet I say to you: the aircraft is modelled on the bird; it has a right and left wing that prevent it from tilting, it also has air, and the bird flies by the air, and it also has the lowering of the wings upon landing and their raising upon take-off. The point is that what we have heard, read and seen in pictures is that these aircraft are built according to the pattern of birds.

﴿But they are communities like you﴾: these communities, glory be to God, are diverse, varied, and different in sizes, in colours, in strengths, in everything; they are also different in languages and tongues. Do you know what the cow understands of the cat's sound? It does not, nor the reverse, but a cow with a cow understands, and a cat with a cat understands. Reflect, glory be to God, and you will find that the cat has different sounds: when it wants the male, it has a particular sound; when it wants to call its small kittens, it has a particular sound; you will find it entering a place and then calling to its young, and they gather around it. Glory be to God! It is a sound different from its usual one. Likewise, each of these communities does not know the language of the other communities.

Then God, Mighty and Majestic, gave each kind of these communities a guidance by which it finds its way in how to live. It is said that the most intelligent of creatures is the ant. The ant, glory be to God, has been given by God, Exalted, a wondrous intelligence; it is among the animals that look toward the future. When the time of grain comes, it gathers the grain into its holes. And what does it do? It bites off the head of the grain, so that it does not sprout, because if it sprouted it would spoil for it; so it eats it lest it sprout. Then, when the rains come and the rain reaches the grain, it brings it out, whatever it may be, bringing it out to spread it, lest it spoil and to protect it from its smell. This is observed; we have seen it, and others have seen it.

A questioner asked: "If you see this grain, the ant's store, which is measured by the sa', is it permissible for me to take it? What is your opinion, is it permissible?"

* Student: It is not permissible.

* The Shaykh: The ant does not own it, but it is its sustenance.

Shall we say: it is permissible to take it only in case of necessity; because the sanctity of a human being is greater than the sanctity of this? And we also say: it is permissible if the ant can feed on something else; because in the winter days the ant does not come out, it remains in its hole, so it is in need. So I say: what I see in this matter is that if the human being is in necessity, he takes precedence. If he is not in necessity, we consider: if it is possible to bring food other than it, there is no harm in his taking it; otherwise he leaves it for them, because I fear that this is of the kind of "the woman who was punished because of a cat she imprisoned: she neither fed it nor let it go to eat from the vermin of the earth"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3318) and Muslim (2619 / 135) in a similar version, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]].

Similar to this: if you found, with a cat, meat that it had brought from the neighbours, meat worth something, may you take it from this cat? Yes, this is correct, because the cat has now stolen, so it is taken from it and returned to its owner, especially if it is a hen and alive; it is known that you rescue it and give it to the neighbours.

The point is that these creatures are communities like us, and they have wonders. Ibn al-Qayyim, may God have mercy on him, in the book Miftah Dar al-Sa'adah, mentioned the marvellous wonders of these communities.

* Student: (...)?

* The Shaykh: This is also a difficult question. He says: we see some cats in Makkah catching pigeons; may we prevent them? If you are able to rescue this bird, you must rescue it; but if you see it dead with it, leave it.

* Student: Are things without life, such as cars and aircraft, called creatures (dawabb), or is this term restricted to living things?

* The Shaykh: No, what is meant is that which has a soul.

* Student: The hadith in which it is said that "when he mounted his animal he said the basmalah, and when he settled upon it he praised God"[[Narrated by Abu Dawud (2602) and al-Tirmidhi (3446) in a similar version, from the hadith of Ali ibn Abi Talib.]], then he said: Do we say this even when we ride in a car, although it is not a creature?

* The Shaykh: Yes, but it is a mount.

* Student: We mentioned the grains in the ant's hole; may I take half and leave half? Many people here take it.

* The Shaykh: It is a reconciliation (musalahah), I mean, you take half. Now, if you take half, shall we not say: you must return it to its owner? What is the ant's hole? The farm around it, because in most cases it takes from what is around it. Shall we say: take this grain and give it to the owner of the farm?

* Student: It was reported from some brothers that they speak to the ants. It is said: a nest of ants in a house, or a garden, or the like, and he says: "Come out," and recites the verses in Surat al-Naml. One of them tried it, a relative of mine. She left his house and entered the house of his neighbour?

* The Shaykh: You mean he addressed her?

* Student: Yes.

* The Shaykh: What did he say?

* Student: He says: "I ask you by God to leave this place," and he gives her provision. He says: "She left my farm and entered my neighbour's farm (...)."

* The Shaykh: Glory be to God!

* Student: In our neighbourhood mosque, near the door of the mosque, there were very many ants. One of the brothers, an upright man among our brothers, came and said: "I ask you by God to leave this place." The mosque's muezzin, from a country where there are Sufis and the like, when he came in the morning he did not find the ants and said: "That is a saint, by God, Shaykh!"

* The Shaykh: We hear from some brothers who sit on a small chair, then recite verses of the Qur'an, and then the ants depart from his house. God is greater! This shows that they understand, and in the story of Solomon it is clear that they understand.

* Student: As for the ant, it lives, for example, in the house as a dwelling, and there are small children, and it generally bites them; it may harm them. May we kill it?

* The Shaykh: Yes, it is known that if its harm is not averted except by killing, then [kill it]. But we have tried kerosene, this fuel: if you pour it on its hole and around it, it will leave and depart.

I seek refuge with God from Satan the accursed. God, Exalted, said: ﴿There is no creature that crawls upon the earth, nor bird that flies on its two wings, but they are communities like you﴾. What is meant by His saying ﴿on its two wings﴾?

* Student: The emphasis.

* The Shaykh: No, "on its two wings," ﴿flies on its two wings﴾: what is meant by it?

* Student: All birds.

* The Shaykh: Yes, but what is meant? If someone said: can the saying ﴿bird﴾ dispense with "its two wings"?

* Student: For emphasis, Shaykh.

* The Shaykh: This is for emphasis, as one says?

* Student: "He hears with his ears."

* The Shaykh: He hears with his ears, sees with his eyes, and the like.

What is the meaning of His saying ﴿but they are communities like you﴾?

* Student: "But they are creatures like you."

* The Shaykh: Creatures; the meaning of "communities" is not (creatures).

* Student: Ummah: a group. ﴿Like you﴾, meaning: they take counsel among themselves in managing affairs.

* The Shaykh: That is: kinds.

* Student: Yes.

* The Shaykh: ﴿But they are communities like you﴾: kinds, each kind has its particular state. Correct.

Does that include the young ants?

* Student: Yes, it includes them.

* The Shaykh: It includes them; how is that, how does it include them? Explain to me.

* Student: That they (...).

* The Shaykh: And they crawl upon the earth or not? This is the point of evidence: they crawl upon the earth.

If someone said: is there one who walks on his belly included in this?

* Student: It is included.

* The Shaykh: It is included in this, because?

* Student: It crawls upon the earth.

* The Shaykh: It crawls upon the earth, correct.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿We have neglected nothing in the Book﴾: what is meant by "the Book"?

* Student: We have explained it.

* The Shaykh: How, did we stop at this?

* Student: Yes.

* The Shaykh: God, Mighty and Majestic, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿We have neglected nothing in the Book﴾. ﴿Neglected﴾ means: We omitted. And "the Book" is the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), not the Noble Book. The Noble Book, God said about it: ﴿And We have sent down to you the Book as an explanation of all things﴾ [al-Nahl 89]. So what is meant by "the Book" here is the Preserved Tablet; that is, God has omitted nothing without recording it in the Preserved Tablet.

Let it not trouble you to say: how is everything written, even the kinds of creatures? Because we say: it is obligatory upon the human being to believe in what God has informed of, whether his intellect grasps it or not; and if a person believed only in what his intellect grasps, he would not be a true believer. So everything God has informed of, from this and other things, it is obligatory upon us to believe in it, without objecting or raising doubts, whether we grasp it with our intellects or not. Moreover, there now exist small things made by humans that can hold very many words; these discs they call laser hold very many words.

His saying: ﴿We have neglected nothing in the Book﴾, the "min" here (in min shay') is superfluous for emphasis; and let it be known that there is nothing superfluous without meaning in the Book of God, ever, because the Qur'an is both wording and meaning. But our saying "superfluous" refers to grammatical superfluity; that is, superfluous in i'rab, but not in meaning. There is nothing superfluous in the Book of God. Is that clear? That is, everything God, Exalted, has recorded in this Preserved Tablet.

﴿Then to their Lord they will be gathered﴾. Glory be to God! That is: then, after this world ends, to their Lord who created them, Mighty and Majestic, and recorded them in the Preserved Tablet; ﴿they will be gathered﴾, meaning they will be assembled. Everything will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection.

Do not be surprised either, saying: how will these creatures, the beasts, the animals, the birds and others, be gathered? Do not be astonished. What is obligatory upon you? To believe. The matter is beyond what the intellect can grasp. All of them will be gathered to God; all of them will have retribution taken for the wronged from the wrongdoer: "Even the hornless sheep will have retribution taken from the horned sheep if it butted it in the world"[[Narrated by Muslim (2582 / 60) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]. Glory be to God! It is the perfection of justice. Therefore, it becomes manifest on the Day of Resurrection, from the perfection of God's justice, mercy, and also His wrath, what was not manifest before, until the perfection of justice becomes apparent to all creation. ﴿Then to their Lord they will be gathered﴾: that is, they will be assembled after life.

* From this noble verse: there is no living creature that crawls upon the earth or flies in the sky except that it is recorded with God, Mighty and Majestic.

* Among its benefits: the noble Qur'an came in the Arabic style, meaning that it proceeded according to what the Arabs express in their language. So if it is customary among the Arabs, for example, to emphasize a thing by what strengthens it, the Qur'an came with it. Therefore you find in the noble Qur'an many oaths upon things: ﴿By the sky and the night-comer﴾ [al-Tariq 1], ﴿By the sky with its constellations﴾ [al-Buruj 1], and the like. Is this out of doubt about what God has informed of? No; because God is truthful whether He swears or not, but the noble Qur'an was revealed in a clear Arabic tongue, so it proceeds in expression according to what the Arabs used to express by.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: a person must know his own worth. Compared to the greatness of God, Mighty and Majestic, he is like the ant: ﴿communities like you﴾. So do not be haughty or arrogant; you are nothing but like these creatures in relation to the greatness of God, Mighty and Majestic. Although God, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And We have honoured the children of Adam, and carried them on land and sea, and provided them with good things, and preferred them above many of what We have created with a clear preference﴾ [al-Isra' 70], He did not prefer the children of Adam over all that God created, but over many of what God created. What some people understand, that the children of Adam are the best of creatures, is an error. Why?

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Wrong.

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Because of His saying: ﴿And preferred them above many of what We have created﴾ [al-Isra' 70]. He did not say "above whatever We have created." ﴿Above many of what We have created with a clear preference.﴾ Have you understood? And beware of offering a rationale when there is a textual proof. Have you understood?

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: God, Mighty and Majestic, did not neglect anything in the Preserved Tablet; He recorded everything, because of His saying: ﴿We have neglected nothing in the Book﴾, and because God commanded the Pen, that is, commanded it, to write what will be until the Day of Resurrection.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the final destiny of these creatures, the flying and the crawling, is to God, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Then to their Lord they will be gathered﴾.

Then Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿Those who deny Our signs are deaf and dumb, in darkness.﴾ [al-An'am 39] This sentence is joined to the previous one by conjunction of sentences (ʿaṭf jumal). ﴿Those who deny Our signs﴾ means: they said that they are lies and did not believe in them. They came to the cosmic signs and said: this is sorcery, just as Pharaoh said when he saw the signs of Musa: "This is sorcery." And as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said about the Quraysh: ﴿The Hour has drawn near and the moon has split. (1) And if they see a sign, they turn away and say: "This is continuous sorcery."﴾ [al-Qamar 1, 2]. So they denied the cosmic signs, and they likewise denied the legislative signs (al-āyāt al-shar‘iyyah); they described the messengers as liars, as poets, as soothsayers, as madmen, as those bewitched, and the like. And this is denial of what? Of the legislative signs.

﴿Those who denied the signs of Allah are deaf and dumb, in darkness﴾ — they have three states. Deaf with their ears: they do not hear the Book with a hearing that benefits them, so the path of truth is closed to them from the direction of hearing. (Dumb) is the plural of (abkam), the one who cannot speak; so they do not speak the truth, but they speak falsehood. ﴿In darkness﴾: they do not see; the darkness surrounds them from every side, because (fī) indicates containment, and the container encompasses what it contains. Thus the doors of knowledge and recognition are closed to them: hearing, sight, and speech — and we seek refuge in Allah. Concerning this, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said in Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿Deaf, dumb, blind; so they do not understand﴾ [al-Baqarah 171].

﴿Whomever Allah wills to leave astray, He leaves him astray﴾ — this is a conditional sentence: the conditional verb is ﴿wills﴾ (yashaʾ), and its response is ﴿He leaves him astray﴾ (yuḍlilhu), meaning: whomever Allah wills to lead astray, He leads astray, because the matter is His, the Mighty and Majestic; there is no one to repel His judgment, none to object to Him, and He is not questioned about what He does. So we ask Allah to guide us among those whom He guides. ﴿Whomever Allah wills to leave astray, He leaves him astray﴾: he becomes blind to the truth and does not reach it.

﴿And whoever He wills, He places him upon a straight path﴾ — here we supply: and whoever He wills to guide, ﴿He places him﴾ meaning He makes him, ﴿upon a straight path﴾ meaning upon a direct way without crookedness, which is Islam.

* Among the benefits of this verse: the description of the state of those who deny the signs of Allah, and that there is no way to guide them. Why? Because they are deaf and do not hear the truth with a hearing that benefits them; likewise they are in darkness, and they do not speak the truth.

* Among the benefits of these noble verses: whoever Allah wills to guide is guided, and whoever He wills to lead astray goes astray.

* Following from this benefit: a person should turn to his Lord, blessed and exalted, seeking guidance and seeking refuge from misguidance, because the matter is in the hand of Allah.

If someone asks: Is this will a bare will, in the sense that whoever He wills to guide He guides, and whoever He wills to lead astray He leads astray, without any wisdom; or is it a will joined with wisdom?

The answer: the second. It is a will joined with wisdom, and this is the correct view, because all the acts of Allah, blessed and exalted, and all His rulings, are joined with wisdom. Consider His rulings: Allah the Exalted said in the verse of inheritance: ﴿An obligation from Allah; indeed Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾ [an-Nisa' 11], and He the Exalted said regarding matters of decree: ﴿And you do not will except that Allah wills; indeed Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾ [al-Insan 30]. So there is no bare will in the acts of Allah or His rulings; rather it is joined with wisdom. But is this wisdom known to creation?

The answer: it may be known, and this, praise be to Allah, is the most common case; it may be unknown to some people and not others; and it may be unknown to all people, who cannot encompass Allah in knowledge.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the Path, which is the religion of Islam, is straight, with no crookedness in it, no deviation in it, no wretchedness in it; it is straight. To this is added: there is no contradiction in it, because if it contained contradiction it would not be straight.

If someone says: Does a person have a proof against Allah if He leads him astray and guides others?

The answer: No. Because guidance is a bounty from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and the bounty of Allah He gives to whom He wills. Also, leading astray must necessarily be based on the state of the servant, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾ [as-Saff 5], and His saying: ﴿But if they turn away, know that Allah intends to afflict them for some of their sins; and indeed, many of the people are defiantly disobedient﴾ [al-Ma'idah 49]. The conclusion is that Allah the Exalted leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills, for a wisdom, and leading astray must be a consequence of the servant's own action.

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Say: Tell me, if the punishment of Allah comes upon you, or the Hour comes upon you, will you call upon other than Allah, if you are truthful?﴾ [al-An'am 40] ﴿Say﴾ means: O Muhammad. And if you wish, you may say: the address is general, to whom? To everyone whose address is valid.

﴿Tell me (ara'aytakum)﴾: The scholars said: (ara'ayta) means (akhbirni, "inform me"). The taa' is the subject pronoun, the kaf is a particle of address for emphasis and has no place in the grammatical structure, and the meem is the plural marker. (Ara'ayta) requires a first object and a second object, because the seeing here is cognitive (ʿilmiyyah). They said: the first object is omitted, and the second object is the interrogative clause: ﴿Will you call upon other than Allah?﴾ This omitted object is to be estimated according to what suits the situation, so the estimate here is: Tell me your condition at the time of hardship, will you call upon other than Allah? Allah then specified whom they call upon in hardship, saying: ﴿Rather, it is Him you call upon﴾ [al-An'am 41].

Returning to the grammar, I say: the hamzah is for interrogation, the seeing here is cognitive, the taa' is the subject, the kaf is for address for emphasis, and the meem is the plural marker. The cognitive (ra'a) takes two objects. The first object here is omitted and is estimated according to what suits the context, and what suits the context here is: your condition at the time of hardship. The clause ﴿will you call upon other than Allah?﴾ occupies the place of the second object in the accusative. That is: inform me, if you fall into hardship, do you call upon other than Allah? The answer is no: ﴿When a wave covers them like shadows, they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion﴾ [Luqman 32]. So when they fall into hardship, they recognize Allah.

What is strange is that the polytheists, when they fall into hardship, call upon Allah, while some groups of this Ummah, when they fall into hardship, call upon other than Allah. When they fall into hardship, they call upon ʿAbd al-Qadir al-Jilani, they call upon ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, they call upon al-Husayn, and similar figures. Thus the condition of the polytheists is better than the condition of these people.

As for His saying: ﴿if you are truthful﴾, it means: if you are truthful in that other than Allah will save you. But when they call upon Allah in hardship, they become liars in their claim that these deities will save them.

Then He said: ﴿Rather, it is Him you call upon﴾. (Bal) is for the retraction that nullifies (al-idrab al-ibtali), nullifying that they call upon other than Allah. And ﴿Him (iyyahu)﴾ is a fronted object of ﴿you call upon﴾, and fronting the object conveys restriction. The meaning: rather, you call upon none but Allah.

﴿Then He removes that for which you call upon Him﴾: (yakshif) means (yuzil, "removes"), as one uncovers what is hidden, removing its covering until it appears and becomes manifest. ﴿He removes that for which you call upon Him﴾, that is: what you called upon Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to remove, the supplication you addressed to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

He said ﴿if He wills﴾ only so that these people will not hope for the removal of distress; if it is not removed, they would argue against Allah. When He says ﴿if He wills﴾, the matter falls under Allah's will: Allah may will to remove this distress and may not will it, according to what His wisdom, blessed and exalted, requires.

﴿And you forget what you associate﴾: (tansawna) means you become distracted from it because of the intensity of what has befallen you; you forget everything. It has also been said that forgetting here means abandoning; that is, they call upon Allah, Mighty and Majestic, with presence of heart and remembrance, and these two are mutually implied, because a person in astonishment forgets his objects of worship, and because in hardship he also believes that his object of worship will not benefit him. So the verse admits both meanings. Many exegetes explained it as meaning abandonment here, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿So taste, for what you forgot the meeting of this your day﴾ — what? ﴿Indeed We have forgotten you﴾ [as-Sajdah 14], and He said: ﴿They forgot Allah, so He forgot them﴾ [at-Tawbah 67]. The forgetting attributed to Allah in such contexts means abandonment.

As for His saying: ﴿My Lord neither errs nor forgets﴾ [Ta-Ha 52], the forgetting intended here is that what He was aware of before becomes absent from Him. But the affirmed forgetting for Allah must be understood as abandonment, not as distraction from a known matter; as for what is negated of Allah, yes, it is the kind that means distraction from a known matter.

* Student: Explaining (ara'aytakum) as (akhbirni, "inform me") and the meaning of (ara'ayta) here: the seeing here is cognitive?

* Shaykh: Yes, the meaning is: you have known, so inform me.

* Student: So "inform me" is necessarily included?

* Shaykh: No, that is not it. It is an explanation by meaning, not by wording. Explaining it as "inform me" or "tell me" is an explanation by meaning. As for what corresponds exactly to the wording, the meaning is: have you known this, then inform me.

* Student: The Exalted's saying: ﴿We have neglected nothing in the Book﴾. If it is said that the verse may refer to the Preserved Tablet or to the Book, and the rule in tafsir is that if a verse may bear more than one meaning, it is interpreted by all of them?

* Shaykh: That is not correct, because the context determines one of the two meanings; here the context specifies that it is the Preserved Tablet.

* Student: The justification of the saying (...): if someone says that the removal of the punishment occurred through the means of attributing partners to Allah?

* Shaykh: What is the concept of this, what does it mean?

* Student: Opposition.

* Shaykh: (...).

* Student: (...) the removal occurred through denial, meaning?

* Shaykh: It did not occur, because Allah restricted it by His will.

* Student: May Allah reward you well. Do those who distort the verses enter the Exalted's saying: ﴿those who denied Our signs﴾ [al-An'am 150]?

* Shaykh: Distortion, may Allah bless you, means interpretation. If it is an interpretation of denial, they may perhaps be included in this. But if it is an interpretation from honest effort (ijtihad), they are not included in this. An acceptable interpretation is one the wording can bear; and if there is something that favors the other meaning while the wording still allows it, then they are not obstinate. But if the wording does not allow it, they are obstinate and resemble those who rejected.

* Student: Shaykh, may Allah bless you: ﴿those who disbelieved in Our signs﴾ regarding some people (...) the signs of Allah (...), but they do not act like the People of the Book; are these people liars?

* Shaykh: No, they did not lie; these people are included among the arrogant.

* Student: May Allah be pleased with you. I heard that the Messenger ﷺ (...) to the Ka'bah: "How great you are, and how great your sanctity is, and the sanctity of the believer is greater than yours"[[Narrated by Ibn Majah (3932) from the hadith of ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar.]], and this has often come up for us, O Shaykh: is anything better than the believer (...)?

* Shaykh: I do not know this hadith. But there is no doubt that the believer is better than the Ka'bah and has greater sanctity.

* Student: (...)?

* Shaykh: Not absolutely, that is not permitted, because Allah said: ﴿And We have preferred them over many of those We have created, with preference﴾ [al-Isra' 70].

* Student: Does the Exalted's saying ﴿We have neglected nothing in the Book﴾ imply that the supplication "O Allah, we do not ask You to reverse the decree" is not valid?

* Shaykh: No, it is known to be objectionable (munkar), and this objectionable supplication is not permitted. "I do not ask You to reverse the decree, but I ask You for gentleness in it" is an error. It indicates that this person is as if saying: I do not care; I do not ask Allah to grant you well-being, and nothing turns away the decree except supplication. But you will find this phrase is a saying of a Sufi or the like, and it has spread on people's tongues.

Like the question: is man compelled or free? Glory be to Allah! Does anyone ask this question?! The one who asks it is himself free or compelled? The answer: the free one is the one who chooses; it is man.

* Student: May Allah bless you. It is often repeated on the tongues of preachers and also in the introductions of books: "And prayer and peace upon the most noble of Allah's creation, Muhammad ﷺ"?

* Shaykh: No, it is an error, although (...) said:

"And the most excellent of creation absolutely is our Prophet, so turn away from dispute."

But the word "creation" must be restricted to the children of Adam, for the Messenger, may prayer and peace be upon him and his family, said: "I am the master of the children of Adam"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3340) and Muslim (2278) with the wording of Muslim, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]], and it came in a hadith: "and the choice of His creation"[[Narrated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (7249) from the hadith of ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab.]], and what is meant is His creation of the children of Adam.

I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿Say: Tell me, if the punishment of Allah comes upon you, or the Hour comes upon you, will you call upon other than Allah, if you are truthful? (40) Rather, it is Him you call upon﴾.

* In this verse and what follows there are benefits. Among them: the establishing of proof against a person by something he cannot repel: a person is made to acknowledge something he cannot deny. This is in His saying: ﴿Tell me, if the punishment of Allah comes upon you, or the Hour comes upon you, will you call upon other than Allah?﴾, because in this state they call upon none but Allah. If that is so, why do they become sincere in hardship and associate partners in ease?!

As for His saying: ﴿the punishment of Allah or the Hour comes upon you﴾, the meaning is that Allah may not punish these deniers and may delay that until the Hour is established; that is, it is necessary that the punishment either strike them in this world, or strike them on the Day of Resurrection.

* Among its benefits: that these deniers, in adversity, turn to none but Allah; by His saying: ﴿Rather, it is Him you call upon﴾.

* Among its benefits: that Allah, Exalted, answers the supplication of the one in distress even if he is a disbeliever; indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knows that he will disbelieve if he is saved. Because Allah saves them from distress while knowing that if they are saved they will associate partners, yet their falling into hardship requires the mercy of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to answer their supplication. Likewise the oppressed: Allah answers his supplication even if he is a disbeliever. These are two categories whose supplication is answered: the one in distress, and the second, the oppressed, whose supplication Allah, Exalted, answers. As for the one in distress, it is because the mercy of Allah precedes His wrath, so He has mercy on the one in distress and answers his supplication. As for the oppressed, it is because of the perfect justice of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that He answers the oppressed, granting him victory over the oppressor.

* Among the benefits of this verse: that none removes evil except Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

* It follows from it: that if evil befalls you, do not turn to anyone but Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Is this turning innate or is it legislated and rational? The apparent view is the second; because some of those afflicted with harm do not turn to Allah. The Rafidah, for example, when harm befalls them, turn to whom? To their imams: ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, al-Husayn, or others of their imams. We do not deny that their true imams have a rank with Allah, Mighty and Majestic according to their deeds, but we deny that these be called upon besides Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

* Among the benefits of this verse: caution against practicing evil deeds, for a person may repent to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, then return; therefore He said: ﴿and you forget what you associate﴾. The meaning of (tansawna) here is (tatrukūna, "you abandon"); that is, the deities you were associating with Allah you abandon. We have mentioned in the tafsir that it may mean abandonment or, what? Or distraction, because of the intensity of what has descended upon them.

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Say: Tell me, if the punishment of Allah comes upon you, or the Hour comes upon you, will you call upon other than Allah, if you are truthful?﴾ [al-An'am 40] ﴿Say﴾ means: O Muhammad. And if you wish, you may say: the address is general, to whom? To everyone whose address is valid.

﴿Tell me (ara'aytakum)﴾: The scholars said: (ara'ayta) means (akhbirni, "inform me"). The taa' is the subject pronoun, the kaf is a particle of address for emphasis and has no place in the grammatical structure, and the meem is the plural marker. (Ara'ayta) requires a first object and a second object, because the seeing here is cognitive (ʿilmiyyah). They said: the first object is omitted, and the second object is the interrogative clause: ﴿Will you call upon other than Allah?﴾ This omitted object is to be estimated according to what suits the situation, so the estimate here is: Tell me your condition at the time of hardship, will you call upon other than Allah? Allah then specified whom they call upon in hardship, saying: ﴿Rather, it is Him you call upon﴾ [al-An'am 41].

Returning to the grammar, I say: the hamzah is for interrogation, the seeing here is cognitive, the taa' is the subject, the kaf is for address for emphasis, and the meem is the plural marker.
