The cognitive (ra'a) takes two objects. The first object here is omitted and is estimated according to what suits the context, and what suits the context here is: your condition at the time of hardship. The clause ﴿will you call upon other than Allah?﴾ occupies the place of the second object in the accusative. That is: inform me, if you fall into hardship, do you call upon other than Allah? The answer is no: ﴿When a wave covers them like shadows, they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion﴾ [Luqman 32]. So when they fall into hardship, they recognize Allah.

What is strange is that the polytheists, when they fall into hardship, call upon Allah, while some groups of this Ummah, when they fall into hardship, call upon other than Allah. When they fall into hardship, they call upon ʿAbd al-Qadir al-Jilani, they call upon ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, they call upon al-Husayn, and similar figures. Thus the condition of the polytheists is better than the condition of these people.

As for His saying: ﴿if you are truthful﴾, it means: if you are truthful in that other than Allah will save you. But when they call upon Allah in hardship, they become liars in their claim that these deities will save them.

Then He said: ﴿Rather, it is Him you call upon﴾. (Bal) is for the retraction that nullifies (al-idrab al-ibtali), nullifying that they call upon other than Allah. And ﴿Him (iyyahu)﴾ is a fronted object of ﴿you call upon﴾, and fronting the object conveys restriction. The meaning: rather, you call upon none but Allah.

﴿Then He removes that for which you call upon Him﴾: (yakshif) means (yuzil, "removes"), as one uncovers what is hidden, removing its covering until it appears and becomes manifest. ﴿He removes that for which you call upon Him﴾, that is: what you called upon Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to remove, the supplication you addressed to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

He said ﴿if He wills﴾ only so that these people will not hope for the removal of distress; if it is not removed, they would argue against Allah. When He says ﴿if He wills﴾, the matter falls under Allah's will: Allah may will to remove this distress and may not will it, according to what His wisdom, blessed and exalted, requires.

﴿And you forget what you associate﴾: (tansawna) means you become distracted from it because of the intensity of what has befallen you; you forget everything. It has also been said that forgetting here means abandoning; that is, they call upon Allah, Mighty and Majestic, with presence of heart and remembrance, and these two are mutually implied, because a person in astonishment forgets his objects of worship, and because in hardship he also believes that his object of worship will not benefit him. So the verse admits both meanings. Many exegetes explained it as meaning abandonment here, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿So taste, for what you forgot the meeting of this your day﴾ — what? ﴿Indeed We have forgotten you﴾ [as-Sajdah 14], and He said: ﴿They forgot Allah, so He forgot them﴾ [at-Tawbah 67]. The forgetting attributed to Allah in such contexts means abandonment.

As for His saying: ﴿My Lord neither errs nor forgets﴾ [Ta-Ha 52], the forgetting intended here is that what He was aware of before becomes absent from Him. But the affirmed forgetting for Allah must be understood as abandonment, not as distraction from a known matter; as for what is negated of Allah, yes, it is the kind that means distraction from a known matter.

* Student: Explaining (ara'aytakum) as (akhbirni, "inform me") and the meaning of (ara'ayta) here: the seeing here is cognitive?

* Shaykh: Yes, the meaning is: you have known, so inform me.

* Student: So "inform me" is necessarily included?

* Shaykh: No, that is not it. It is an explanation by meaning, not by wording. Explaining it as "inform me" or "tell me" is an explanation by meaning. As for what corresponds exactly to the wording, the meaning is: have you known this, then inform me.

* Student: The Exalted's saying: ﴿We have neglected nothing in the Book﴾. If it is said that the verse may refer to the Preserved Tablet or to the Book, and the rule in tafsir is that if a verse may bear more than one meaning, it is interpreted by all of them?

* Shaykh: That is not correct, because the context determines one of the two meanings; here the context specifies that it is the Preserved Tablet.

* Student: The justification of the saying (...): if someone says that the removal of the punishment occurred through the means of attributing partners to Allah?

* Shaykh: What is the concept of this, what does it mean?

* Student: Opposition.

* Shaykh: (...).

* Student: (...) the removal occurred through denial, meaning?

* Shaykh: It did not occur, because Allah restricted it by His will.

* Student: May Allah reward you well. Do those who distort the verses enter the Exalted's saying: ﴿those who denied Our signs﴾ [al-An'am 150]?

* Shaykh: Distortion, may Allah bless you, means interpretation. If it is an interpretation of denial, they may perhaps be included in this. But if it is an interpretation from honest effort (ijtihad), they are not included in this. An acceptable interpretation is one the wording can bear; and if there is something that favors the other meaning while the wording still allows it, then they are not obstinate. But if the wording does not allow it, they are obstinate and resemble those who rejected.

* Student: Shaykh, may Allah bless you: ﴿those who disbelieved in Our signs﴾ regarding some people (...) the signs of Allah (...), but they do not act like the People of the Book; are these people liars?

* Shaykh: No, they did not lie; these people are included among the arrogant.

* Student: May Allah be pleased with you. I heard that the Messenger ﷺ (...) to the Ka'bah: "How great you are, and how great your sanctity is, and the sanctity of the believer is greater than yours"[[Narrated by Ibn Majah (3932) from the hadith of ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar.]], and this has often come up for us, O Shaykh: is anything better than the believer (...)?

* Shaykh: I do not know this hadith. But there is no doubt that the believer is better than the Ka'bah and has greater sanctity.

* Student: (...)?

* Shaykh: Not absolutely, that is not permitted, because Allah said: ﴿And We have preferred them over many of those We have created, with preference﴾ [al-Isra' 70].

* Student: Does the Exalted's saying ﴿We have neglected nothing in the Book﴾ imply that the supplication "O Allah, we do not ask You to reverse the decree" is not valid?

* Shaykh: No, it is known to be objectionable (munkar), and this objectionable supplication is not permitted. "I do not ask You to reverse the decree, but I ask You for gentleness in it" is an error. It indicates that this person is as if saying: I do not care; I do not ask Allah to grant you well-being, and nothing turns away the decree except supplication. But you will find this phrase is a saying of a Sufi or the like, and it has spread on people's tongues.

Like the question: is man compelled or free? Glory be to Allah! Does anyone ask this question?! The one who asks it is himself free or compelled? The answer: the free one is the one who chooses; it is man.

* Student: May Allah bless you. It is often repeated on the tongues of preachers and also in the introductions of books: "And prayer and peace upon the most noble of Allah's creation, Muhammad ﷺ"?

* Shaykh: No, it is an error, although (...) said:

"And the most excellent of creation absolutely is our Prophet, so turn away from dispute."

But the word "creation" must be restricted to the children of Adam, for the Messenger, may prayer and peace be upon him and his family, said: "I am the master of the children of Adam"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3340) and Muslim (2278) with the wording of Muslim, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]], and it came in a hadith: "and the choice of His creation"[[Narrated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (7249) from the hadith of ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab.]], and what is meant is His creation of the children of Adam.

I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿Say: Tell me, if the punishment of Allah comes upon you, or the Hour comes upon you, will you call upon other than Allah, if you are truthful? (40) Rather, it is Him you call upon﴾.

* In this verse and what follows there are benefits. Among them: the establishing of proof against a person by something he cannot repel: a person is made to acknowledge something he cannot deny. This is in His saying: ﴿Tell me, if the punishment of Allah comes upon you, or the Hour comes upon you, will you call upon other than Allah?﴾, because in this state they call upon none but Allah. If that is so, why do they become sincere in hardship and associate partners in ease?!

As for His saying: ﴿the punishment of Allah or the Hour comes upon you﴾, the meaning is that Allah may not punish these deniers and may delay that until the Hour is established; that is, it is necessary that the punishment either strike them in this world, or strike them on the Day of Resurrection.

* Among its benefits: that these deniers, in adversity, turn to none but Allah; by His saying: ﴿Rather, it is Him you call upon﴾.

* Among its benefits: that Allah, Exalted, answers the supplication of the one in distress even if he is a disbeliever; indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knows that he will disbelieve if he is saved. Because Allah saves them from distress while knowing that if they are saved they will associate partners, yet their falling into hardship requires the mercy of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to answer their supplication. Likewise the oppressed: Allah answers his supplication even if he is a disbeliever. These are two categories whose supplication is answered: the one in distress, and the second, the oppressed, whose supplication Allah, Exalted, answers. As for the one in distress, it is because the mercy of Allah precedes His wrath, so He has mercy on the one in distress and answers his supplication. As for the oppressed, it is because of the perfect justice of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that He answers the oppressed, granting him victory over the oppressor.

* Among the benefits of this verse: that none removes evil except Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

* It follows from it: that if evil befalls you, do not turn to anyone but Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Is this turning innate or is it legislated and rational? The apparent view is the second; because some of those afflicted with harm do not turn to Allah. The Rafidah, for example, when harm befalls them, turn to whom? To their imams: ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, al-Husayn, or others of their imams. We do not deny that their true imams have a rank with Allah, Mighty and Majestic according to their deeds, but we deny that these be called upon besides Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

* Among the benefits of this verse: caution against practicing evil deeds, for a person may repent to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, then return; therefore He said: ﴿and you forget what you associate﴾. The meaning of (tansawna) here is (tatrukūna, "you abandon"); that is, the deities you were associating with Allah you abandon. We have mentioned in the tafsir that it may mean abandonment or, what? Or distraction, because of the intensity of what has descended upon them.

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And We certainly sent [messengers] to nations before you﴾ [al-An'am 42]. How often this expression recurs in the Noble Qur'an, like this one. The scholars said: the lam (لَ) here is a preface to an oath (muwatti'a lil-qasam), meaning that it prepares for an oath, so there is an implied oath before it. The lam prefaces the oath and emphasizes it, and qad (قَدْ) is also emphatic, so there are three emphases in this.

﴿We sent to nations before you﴾, meaning: We sent messengers to nations before you. ﴿Umam﴾ is the plural of ﴿ummah﴾, and the word ummah in the Noble Qur'an carries several meanings. It is used to mean an imam (leader), as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, Abraham was a [complete] ummah, devoutly obedient to Allah﴾ [al-Nahl 120], meaning an imam. It is used to mean a period of time, as in the words of Allah: ﴿And he remembered after a period (ummah) [of time]﴾ [Yusuf 45], meaning after a time. And it is used to mean a group, as here, meaning a group and a people, and similar.

Does it have any other meaning? It has a fourth meaning, which I have forgotten, namely religion (millah), as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, we found our fathers upon an ummah﴾ [al-Zukhruf 22], meaning upon a religion. So it has four meanings in the Noble Qur'an.

His saying ﴿to nations before you﴾ means all the nations to which messengers were sent, all of them, before the Messenger (ﷺ), because he is their seal.

﴿So We seized them with adversity and hardship﴾. ﴿So We seized them with adversity﴾: the fa' (فَ) here is conjunctive. Is it conjoined to the sending of the messengers, meaning that the messengers were sent so that these people would be seized with adversity and hardship? No. Rather, there is an ellipsis in the verse, whose implied meaning is: "so they denied," or "so they disbelieved," or something similar. This is called ijaz hadhf (brevity through omission), because brevity according to the rhetoricians is of two kinds: ijaz qasr (brevity by compression), which is when few words carry many meanings, and ijaz hadhf, which is when something is omitted from a short utterance and the context indicates it. Here there is no doubt that something has been omitted from this statement, and the implied meaning is: "so they denied."

﴿So We seized them with adversity and hardship﴾. ﴿Al-ba'sa'﴾ means hardship, and ﴿al-darra'﴾ means harm. ﴿That they might humble themselves﴾: the la'alla (لَعَلَّ) here indicates cause, meaning in order that they might humble themselves before Allah, Mighty and Majestic. But did this happen?

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Then why, when Our punishment came to them, did they not humble themselves?﴾ [al-An'am 43], meaning: Our punishment. The word ﴿lawla﴾ (لَوْلَا) here means ﴿halla﴾ (هَلَّا), meaning: why, when the punishment came to them, did they not humble themselves? The answer is: no. Therefore He said: ﴿But their hearts became hardened﴾, meaning they became rigid and did not soften, and they remained upon what they were upon. ﴿And Satan made attractive to them what they were doing﴾. The word ﴿zayyana﴾ (زَيَّنَ) means ﴿hassana﴾ (حَسَّنَ), meaning he made appealing to them what they were doing, that is, of sins, disbelief and polytheism. He did not limit himself to making the matter trivial in their hearts, but rather he made it attractive to them.

﴿And Satan made attractive to them what they were doing﴾. ﴿Al-Shaytan﴾ here refers to the category and not one specific devil, just as you say "al-insan" (the human) to refer to the category.

﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We opened for them the gates of all things﴾ [al-An'am 44]. ﴿When they forgot what they had been reminded of﴾: ﴿nasu﴾ here means they abandoned and turned away from what they had been reminded of. ﴿We opened for them the gates of all things﴾ means: of worldly bounties. Allah opened for them the gates of every worldly bounty: provision, security, ease, and other kinds of luxury.

﴿Until when they rejoiced in what they had been given, We seized them suddenly﴾. ﴿Until when they rejoiced﴾: that is, rejoiced with arrogance and exultation. ﴿In what they had been given﴾: that is, in what they had been given of what Allah had opened to them. ﴿We seized them suddenly﴾: We seized them with what? With punishment. ﴿Suddenly﴾: that is, something unexpected that had not occurred to them, because they had immersed themselves in luxury and forgotten the punishment. ﴿We seized them suddenly, and at once they were in despair﴾. ﴿Then at once﴾: this "idha" (إذا) is for sudden occurrence, and the meaning is: despair overtook them, and it is ibla's (إبلاس), which is despair of the mercy of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

* In these noble verses, first: the establishment of proof against the creation by sending messengers. This is like His saying in Surat al-Nisa': ﴿Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him, and We revealed to Abraham and Ishmael﴾ [al-Nisa' 163], up to His saying: ﴿as bringers of good news and warners, so that mankind will have no argument against Allah after the messengers﴾ [al-Nisa' 165]. And among the completeness of the proof in sending messengers is that the messengers [speak] in the language of their people, meaning in the tongue of the people to whom they were sent, so that they may understand the proof.

* From this it follows that proof is not established merely by delivery, until the addressed people understand it; otherwise, what is the benefit? Rather, it is obligatory upon whoever has received it but did not understand to seek [understanding]. This last point may perhaps close off their excuse if they say: "We did not understand." We say: it is obligatory upon you to seek [understanding]. But sometimes seeking is hindered because they cannot find anyone they trust, so they remain ignorant.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse is the mercy of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, toward the creation, in that He sent messengers to them to establish the proof and to clarify the right path (al-mahajjah). Al-mahajjah means the road. Were it not for the messengers, we would not have known. Were it not for the Prophet (ﷺ) explaining to us how to perform wudu', we would not have known; how to pray, we would not have known; how to pay zakat, how to fast, how to perform Hajj, how to deal with others, we would not have known. So the sending of messengers is from the mercy of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse is the omission of the cause, so that the effect and the result are more forceful and awe-inspiring for the addressee. The cause is omitted and the consequence is mentioned, so that it is more forceful and awe-inspiring in the hearts of the addressee; this is due to His saying: ﴿So We seized them﴾, and He did not mention the denial, so that it would be more intense, and the mind would ask: why were they seized? Thus it becomes more awe-inspiring and forceful in the hearts of the addressee.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse is that Allah, Exalted, tests with adversity and hardship, but for a wisdom, not merely to inflict harm upon the creation. What is the wisdom? He explained it in His saying: ﴿that they might humble themselves﴾. Otherwise Allah cannot intend mere harm; rather, whatever harm befalls people from Allah's decrees, its purpose is the benefit of the creation.

* Among the benefits of this verse is that seizing may be by hardship, and may be by harm. It may be by hardship that a person is pained by without harm, such as fear, hunger and similar; this is hardship. A disease directly affecting a person is harm. So the seizing is either this or that.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse is the affirmation of wisdom in the acts of Allah. It is derived from His saying: ﴿that they might humble themselves﴾. The fact that Allah has wisdom in His acts and in His legislation is known to every person of intellect, because the fact that actions and rulings proceed from wisdom indicates the perfection of the Doer and the Lawgiver.

But is the wisdom of every act or ruling that comes from Allah known to us?
The answer is: no, because our intellects are too limited to encompass the wisdom of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Yet we know with certainty that it is for a wisdom. This is why, when Mother of the Believers 'A'ishah was asked: "Why does a menstruating woman make up fasts but not make up prayers?" she did not go on to give a reason by saying: "Fasting comes only once a year and its making up is easy, whereas prayer comes five times a day and night, so making it up is difficult; fasting has no equivalent within the year to take its place, whereas prayer has an equivalent: if you do not pray today, you pray tomorrow." She did not say this. She said: "This used to happen to us, and we were commanded to make up the fast, and we were not commanded to make up the prayer." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (321), and Muslim (335/69), with his wording, from the hadith of 'A'ishah.] So she made the bare ruling itself the wisdom.

Likewise, every believer must believe that all of Allah's acts and all of Allah's laws are for a wisdom, but sometimes we know it and sometimes we do not.

The jurists, may Allah have mercy on them, describe a thing whose wisdom is unknown as ta'abbudi (devotional), meaning that we are only obliged to worship through it, not to know its wisdom. Sometimes they call a thing ta'abbudi while its wisdom is known, and sometimes that statement is correct.

Some in this community denied wisdom and said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does whatever He wills merely by will, and rules as He wills merely by will. This is an error and a deficiency. They said: because if He did something for a wisdom, that would be for a purpose, and doing something for a purpose is a deficiency.

And among their corrupt expressions, pleasing in appearance or sound, is: "Allah is exempt from accidents (a'rad), parts (ab'ad), and purposes (aghrad)." So according to them He is exempt from accidents, the second is parts, and the third is purposes.

As for accidents, they mean by this what befalls the doer, such as doing or not doing and the like. That is why they deny the istiwa' (settling) upon the Throne, and deny the descent to the lowest heaven.

As for parts, they mean the face, the hands and similar.

As for purposes, they mean wisdom. They say: if His acts or His laws were for a wisdom, He would have a purpose, and Allah, Exalted, is exempt from purposes.

The answer to this is easy: is the purpose contained in wisdom for the benefit of Allah or for the benefit of the creation? The second, certainly. Otherwise Allah says: ﴿If you disbelieve, then indeed Allah is free of need of you; and He does not approve disbelief for His servants. And if you are grateful, He approves it for you﴾ [al-Zumar 7]. So this wisdom contained in the act, the legislation or the ruling is for the benefit of the creation. Then is it perfection or deficiency? It is perfection.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse is the obligation of humbling oneself to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Tadarru' means seeking refuge and turning in repentance to Allah, Exalted, and performing all that is obligatory toward Him, of every kind: belief, speech or action.

Then He said: ﴿Then why, when Our punishment came to them...﴾ to the end.

* Among its benefits: clarifying the severity of hardness of these punished people. When punishment came to them, so that they would humble themselves, their situation was reversed; rather, that increased the hardness of their hearts. We ask Allah for well-being. What should have happened is that they humble themselves before Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

This may befall a person: that adversity and hardship only increase him in hardness of heart and discontent with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, may Allah protect us, and in feelings that are not appropriate. For some people, when afflicted with a trial, say: "What is this? Why is He wronging me? Why does this befall me and not befall others?" Then their hearts harden. We seek refuge in Allah.

Therefore patience is required of one who is struck by a calamity, so that his heart does not harden. It is said to him: "You are a servant of Allah, are you not? A servant is subject to the action of his master, and Allah does with His servant what He wills, just as He does in the heavens what He wills, on the earth what He wills, with the winds what He wills. Likewise you, you are a creature among creatures, and He does with you what He wills. But upon you is patience in hardship, and gratitude in ease."

Moreover, praise be to Allah, the harm that befalls a person is an expiation for his sins, and how many sins there are. Anything that befalls you, even a thorn, if it strikes you, it expiates sins. If you seek reward for it, it establishes the reward of the patient. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has not neglected anything that benefits the creation.

* Among the benefits of this verse: the affirmation of the hardening of the heart after its softness, due to His saying: ﴿But their hearts became hardened﴾, and as in the verse of al-Baqarah: ﴿Then your hearts became hard after that﴾ [al-Baqarah 74]. So hardness of the heart occurs, and softness of the heart also occurs; both are occurrences. It is obligatory upon a person to constantly observe his heart: is it softer or not? Is it humble before Allah or not? Is it sincere to Allah or not? Outward deeds, every person can perform them in the best manner, can he not?

* Student: Yes.

* Shaykh: The hypocrite may perform prayer in the best manner and may give charity, but the actions of the heart are, by Allah, the difficult ones. Free your heart from the bondage of sins so that the Lord may open [it to you].

If someone asks: "What is the remedy for hardness of heart?" This is a question that often comes from some of the upright whom Allah has blessed with steadfastness, but then they experience a shock and their hearts harden.

The answer: among the causes of removing hardness is:

Frequent recitation of the Qur'an with reflection, and that you feel while reading that this is the speech of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, not the speech of humans, the speech of Allah, Creator of the heavens and the earth. Then you will glorify this speech and benefit from it.

Second: frequent remembrance (dhikr), remembrance of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Increase the remembrance of Allah. Remembering Allah, Mighty and Majestic, involves no difficulty, because what moves is the tongue and the lips, and there is no difficulty in it. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Unquestionably, by the remembrance of Allah are hearts assured﴾ [al-Ra'd 28].

Among them: keeping company with the righteous, for keeping company with the righteous brings a person much good. In the hadith: "The righteous companion is like the carrier of musk: either he will give you some, or you will buy from him, or you will smell a pleasant fragrance from him" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5534), and Muslim (2628/146), from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari]. Be keen to keep company with the righteous, but benefit from them and benefit them, for not everyone is infallible. You benefit them and they benefit you.

Among them, i.e., among the causes of softening the heart: showing mercy to the young, especially orphans, for it necessitates tenderness of heart. Try it and you will find out. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Show mercy to those on the earth, and He who is in heaven will show mercy to you" [narrated by Abu Dawud (4941), and al-Tirmidhi (1924), with his wording, from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr].

There are other causes that appear to one who reflects on the remedy for hardness of heart. I ask Allah, Exalted, to soften all our hearts for His remembrance and His obedience. Indeed, He is over all things capable.

* Student: Disciplining the self with some sort of [hunger], starving it and punishing it. Is this correct?

* Shaykh: This does not appear so, and it is not from the Sharia either, because the self has a right. It is true that excess in food, drink, clothing, dwellings and means of transport is not praiseworthy. But making oneself hungry is not part of the Sharia.

* Student: On the basis that one knows oneself, meaning for example if one reduces the quantity of food or reduces...?

* Shaykh: That is not contrary. Reduce, without going hungry; let one eat a third for food, a third for drink, and a third for breath. But the problem now is that some people say: "Abu Hurayrah drank milk until he could not find a passage for it" [narrated by al-Bukhari (6452) in similar wording, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah]. Abu Hurayrah did that once, but these people make it every time. The common people say: "Water is heavy and passes through even if the stomach is full of food, and breath is a spear that the self finds hard." It is as if this common person says: fill the belly. But the truth is that a full belly always harms, and that when a person reduces, it is healthier for him. Try it and you will see. Yes, at times the food is good and appetizing and you cannot eat little, or you come to it while hungry, and from the intensity of hunger your appetite is strong and you eat a lot. But discipline yourself.

* Student: The mercy: "Show mercy to those on the earth, and He who is in heaven will show mercy to you" [narrated by Abu Dawud (4941), and al-Tirmidhi (1924), with his wording, from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr]. Does it include even creatures and animals, does it encompass everything?

* Shaykh: Yes, it encompasses everything. Do you show mercy to animals? Yes, show mercy to animals. Do not burden the camel with more than it can bear.

* Student: (...) The common people say: "This is permissible, this is an animal that does not feel, so beat it"?

* Shaykh: No, I seek refuge in Allah. It feels. How could it not feel?! Does not a camel, when you strike it, foam at the mouth?

* Student: Regarding those whom it is predominantly thought that the proof has not been established against them because they follow great scholars and so on, how should one deal with them if they are doing acts of shirk? Does one treat them as Muslims or as disbelievers?

* Shaykh: With these we withhold judgment, and when their funerals are brought, one makes an exception, saying: "O Allah, forgive him if he was a believer."

* Among the benefits of the verse: the affirmation of hardness of heart, which is its rigidity and its failure to soften to the truth, due to His saying: ﴿But their hearts became hardened﴾.

* Among its benefits: that Satan makes evil deeds attractive to the children of Adam, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And Satan made attractive to them what they were doing﴾, and in another verse: ﴿Satan made their deeds attractive to them﴾ [al-Anfal 48].

* Among the benefits: God, blessed and exalted, may give power over a servant to someone who is his enemy, and this is not considered injustice on the part of God, Mighty and Majestic. Rather, God has made this enemy clear to us and warned us against following his footsteps, so we have no excuse.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: when Satan is given power over a man, what is bad in his eyes becomes good, and what is good becomes bad. This is based on His saying: ﴿And Satan made attractive to them what they were doing﴾, and it is well known that they were engaged in sins.

Then the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of﴾, to the end of the verse.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: God hastened punishment for them, but in the manner of gradual deception (istidraj). This is based on His saying: ﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We opened to them the gates of everything﴾.

* Among the benefits: a person should beware of the punishment of God, Mighty and Majestic, when God bestows upon him the ease of worldly affairs, such as food, drink, marriage, mounts and dwelling. He should not be deceived by this, for it may be istidraj. For this reason some of the early generations (salaf) said: "When you see God, Mighty and Majestic, bestowing favors upon a person while he persists in disobedience, know that this is istidraj."[[Recorded by Ahmad in al-Musnad (17311) as a marfu' hadith from the narration of 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir; we have not found it as a saying of anyone other than him.]] They have spoken truly. So do not be deceived, O human being, for you may be tested with blessings just as you may be tested with afflictions, and the trial through blessings may be more severe than the trial through afflictions.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the one in whose hand is ease and hardship is God, based on His saying: ﴿We opened to them the gates of everything﴾.

* Among the benefits of the verse: it is obligatory to beware of exultation that is arrogant joy (fara' al-batar) in the blessings of God, Mighty and Majestic, based on His saying: ﴿They rejoiced in what they had been given﴾, meaning, joy of arrogance. As for when a person rejoices in what pleases him of the affairs of this world or of the Hereafter, with the joy of happiness and delight in the blessing of God, there is no harm in this. God, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Say: "By the grace of God and His mercy, let them rejoice in that"﴾ [Yunus 58].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: punishment may come to a person suddenly. While he is in his comfort and joy in this world, immersed in disobedience to God, behold, punishment comes upon him unexpectedly. Whether this punishment is general and comprehensive or specific, he may be afflicted with illness, or with accidents that break and crush him, or with sudden death. For this reason He said: ﴿We seized them suddenly﴾, meaning, they were seized abruptly; that is, sudden (mubaghat), and the sudden is a thing a person does not expect, so it befalls him unforeseen.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: this seizing with which God threatened is a destructive seizure, based on His saying: ﴿Then behold, they were despairing﴾, meaning, they were hopeless of every good.

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And We certainly sent [messengers] to nations before you﴾ [al-An'am 42]. How often this expression recurs in the Noble Qur'an, like this one. The scholars said: the lam (لَ) here is a preface to an oath (muwatti'a lil-qasam), meaning that it prepares for an oath, so there is an implied oath before it. The lam prefaces the oath and emphasizes it, and qad (قَدْ) is also emphatic, so there are three emphases in this.

﴿We sent to nations before you﴾, meaning: We sent messengers to nations before you. ﴿Umam﴾ is the plural of ﴿ummah﴾, and the word ummah in the Noble Qur'an carries several meanings. It is used to mean an imam (leader), as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, Abraham was a [complete] ummah, devoutly obedient to Allah﴾ [al-Nahl 120], meaning an imam. It is used to mean a period of time, as in the words of Allah: ﴿And he remembered after a period (ummah) [of time]﴾ [Yusuf 45], meaning after a time. And it is used to mean a group, as here, meaning a group and a people, and similar.

Does it have any other meaning? It has a fourth meaning, which I have forgotten, namely religion (millah), as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, we found our fathers upon an ummah﴾ [al-Zukhruf 22], meaning upon a religion. So it has four meanings in the Noble Qur'an.

His saying ﴿to nations before you﴾ means all the nations to which messengers were sent, all of them, before the Messenger (ﷺ), because he is their seal.

﴿So We seized them with adversity and hardship﴾. ﴿So We seized them with adversity﴾: the fa' (فَ) here is conjunctive. Is it conjoined to the sending of the messengers, meaning that the messengers were sent so that these people would be seized with adversity and hardship? No. Rather, there is an ellipsis in the verse, whose implied meaning is: "so they denied," or "so they disbelieved," or something similar. This is called ijaz hadhf (brevity through omission), because brevity according to the rhetoricians is of two kinds: ijaz qasr (brevity by compression), which is when few words carry many meanings, and ijaz hadhf, which is when something is omitted from a short utterance and the context indicates it. Here there is no doubt that something has been omitted from this statement, and the implied meaning is: "so they denied."

﴿So We seized them with adversity and hardship﴾. ﴿Al-ba'sa'﴾ means hardship, and ﴿al-darra'﴾ means harm. ﴿That they might humble themselves﴾: the la'alla (لَعَلَّ) here indicates cause, meaning in order that they might humble themselves before Allah, Mighty and Majestic. But did this happen?

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Then why, when Our punishment came to them, did they not humble themselves?﴾ [al-An'am 43], meaning: Our punishment. The word ﴿lawla﴾ (لَوْلَا) here means ﴿halla﴾ (هَلَّا), meaning: why, when the punishment came to them, did they not humble themselves? The answer is: no. Therefore He said: ﴿But their hearts became hardened﴾, meaning they became rigid and did not soften, and they remained upon what they were upon. ﴿And Satan made attractive to them what they were doing﴾. The word ﴿zayyana﴾ (زَيَّنَ) means ﴿hassana﴾ (حَسَّنَ), meaning he made appealing to them what they were doing, that is, of sins, disbelief and polytheism. He did not limit himself to making the matter trivial in their hearts, but rather he made it attractive to them.

﴿And Satan made attractive to them what they were doing﴾. ﴿Al-Shaytan﴾ here refers to the category and not one specific devil, just as you say "al-insan" (the human) to refer to the category.

﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We opened for them the gates of all things﴾ [al-An'am 44]. ﴿When they forgot what they had been reminded of﴾: ﴿nasu﴾ here means they abandoned and turned away from what they had been reminded of. ﴿We opened for them the gates of all things﴾ means: of worldly bounties. Allah opened for them the gates of every worldly bounty: provision, security, ease, and other kinds of luxury.

﴿Until when they rejoiced in what they had been given, We seized them suddenly﴾. ﴿Until when they rejoiced﴾: that is, rejoiced with arrogance and exultation. ﴿In what they had been given﴾: that is, in what they had been given of what Allah had opened to them. ﴿We seized them suddenly﴾: We seized them with what? With punishment. ﴿Suddenly﴾: that is, something unexpected that had not occurred to them, because they had immersed themselves in luxury and forgotten the punishment. ﴿We seized them suddenly, and at once they were in despair﴾. ﴿Then at once﴾: this "idha" (إذا) is for sudden occurrence, and the meaning is: despair overtook them, and it is ibla's (إبلاس), which is despair of the mercy of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

* In these noble verses, first: the establishment of proof against the creation by sending messengers. This is like His saying in Surat al-Nisa': ﴿Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him, and We revealed to Abraham and Ishmael﴾ [al-Nisa' 163], up to His saying: ﴿as bringers of good news and warners, so that mankind will have no argument against Allah after the messengers﴾ [al-Nisa' 165]. And among the completeness of the proof in sending messengers is that the messengers [speak] in the language of their people, meaning in the tongue of the people to whom they were sent, so that they may understand the proof.

* From this it follows that proof is not established merely by delivery, until the addressed people understand it; otherwise, what is the benefit? Rather, it is obligatory upon whoever has received it but did not understand to seek [understanding]. This last point may perhaps close off their excuse if they say: "We did not understand." We say: it is obligatory upon you to seek [understanding]. But sometimes seeking is hindered because they cannot find anyone they trust, so they remain ignorant.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse is the mercy of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, toward the creation, in that He sent messengers to them to establish the proof and to clarify the right path (al-mahajjah). Al-mahajjah means the road. Were it not for the messengers, we would not have known. Were it not for the Prophet (ﷺ) explaining to us how to perform wudu', we would not have known; how to pray, we would not have known; how to pay zakat, how to fast, how to perform Hajj, how to deal with others, we would not have known. So the sending of messengers is from the mercy of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse is the omission of the cause, so that the effect and the result are more forceful and awe-inspiring for the addressee. The cause is omitted and the consequence is mentioned, so that it is more forceful and awe-inspiring in the hearts of the addressee; this is due to His saying: ﴿So We seized them﴾, and He did not mention the denial, so that it would be more intense, and the mind would ask: why were they seized? Thus it becomes more awe-inspiring and forceful in the hearts of the addressee.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse is that Allah, Exalted, tests with adversity and hardship, but for a wisdom, not merely to inflict harm upon the creation. What is the wisdom? He explained it in His saying: ﴿that they might humble themselves﴾. Otherwise Allah cannot intend mere harm; rather, whatever harm befalls people from Allah's decrees, its purpose is the benefit of the creation.

* Among the benefits of this verse is that seizing may be by hardship, and may be by harm. It may be by hardship that a person is pained by without harm, such as fear, hunger and similar; this is hardship. A disease directly affecting a person is harm. So the seizing is either this or that.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse is the affirmation of wisdom in the acts of Allah. It is derived from His saying: ﴿that they might humble themselves﴾. The fact that Allah has wisdom in His acts and in His legislation is known to every person of intellect, because the fact that actions and rulings proceed from wisdom indicates the perfection of the Doer and the Lawgiver.

But is the wisdom of every act or ruling that comes from Allah known to us?
The answer is: no, because our intellects are too limited to encompass the wisdom of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Yet we know with certainty that it is for a wisdom. This is why, when Mother of the Believers 'A'ishah was asked: "Why does a menstruating woman make up fasts but not make up prayers?" she did not go on to give a reason by saying: "Fasting comes only once a year and its making up is easy, whereas prayer comes five times a day and night, so making it up is difficult; fasting has no equivalent within the year to take its place, whereas prayer has an equivalent: if you do not pray today, you pray tomorrow." She did not say this. She said: "This used to happen to us, and we were commanded to make up the fast, and we were not commanded to make up the prayer." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (321), and Muslim (335/69), with his wording, from the hadith of 'A'ishah.] So she made the bare ruling itself the wisdom.

Likewise, every believer must believe that all of Allah's acts and all of Allah's laws are for a wisdom, but sometimes we know it and sometimes we do not.

The jurists, may Allah have mercy on them, describe a thing whose wisdom is unknown as ta'abbudi (devotional), meaning that we are only obliged to worship through it, not to know its wisdom. Sometimes they call a thing ta'abbudi while its wisdom is known, and sometimes that statement is correct.

Some in this community denied wisdom and said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does whatever He wills merely by will, and rules as He wills merely by will. This is an error and a deficiency. They said: because if He did something for a wisdom, that would be for a purpose, and doing something for a purpose is a deficiency.

And among their corrupt expressions, pleasing in appearance or sound, is: "Allah is exempt from accidents (a'rad), parts (ab'ad), and purposes (aghrad)." So according to them He is exempt from accidents, the second is parts, and the third is purposes.

As for accidents, they mean by this what befalls the doer, such as doing or not doing and the like. That is why they deny the istiwa' (settling) upon the Throne, and deny the descent to the lowest heaven.

As for parts, they mean the face, the hands and similar.

As for purposes, they mean wisdom. They say: if His acts or His laws were for a wisdom, He would have a purpose, and Allah, Exalted, is exempt from purposes.

The answer to this is easy: is the purpose contained in wisdom for the benefit of Allah or for the benefit of the creation? The second, certainly. Otherwise Allah says: ﴿If you disbelieve, then indeed Allah is free of need of you; and He does not approve disbelief for His servants. And if you are grateful, He approves it for you﴾ [al-Zumar 7]. So this wisdom contained in the act, the legislation or the ruling is for the benefit of the creation. Then is it perfection or deficiency? It is perfection.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse is the obligation of humbling oneself to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Tadarru' means seeking refuge and turning in repentance to Allah, Exalted, and performing all that is obligatory toward Him, of every kind: belief, speech or action.

Then He said: ﴿Then why, when Our punishment came to them...﴾ to the end.

* Among its benefits: clarifying the severity of hardness of these punished people. When punishment came to them, so that they would humble themselves, their situation was reversed; rather, that increased the hardness of their hearts. We ask Allah for well-being. What should have happened is that they humble themselves before Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

This may befall a person: that adversity and hardship only increase him in hardness of heart and discontent with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, may Allah protect us, and in feelings that are not appropriate. For some people, when afflicted with a trial, say: "What is this? Why is He wronging me? Why does this befall me and not befall others?" Then their hearts harden. We seek refuge in Allah.

Therefore patience is required of one who is struck by a calamity, so that his heart does not harden. It is said to him: "You are a servant of Allah, are you not? A servant is subject to the action of his master, and Allah does with His servant what He wills, just as He does in the heavens what He wills, on the earth what He wills, with the winds what He wills. Likewise you, you are a creature among creatures, and He does with you what He wills. But upon you is patience in hardship, and gratitude in ease."

Moreover, praise be to Allah, the harm that befalls a person is an expiation for his sins, and how many sins there are. Anything that befalls you, even a thorn, if it strikes you, it expiates sins. If you seek reward for it, it establishes the reward of the patient. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has not neglected anything that benefits the creation.

* Among the benefits of this verse: the affirmation of the hardening of the heart after its softness, due to His saying: ﴿But their hearts became hardened﴾, and as in the verse of al-Baqarah: ﴿Then your hearts became hard after that﴾ [al-Baqarah 74]. So hardness of the heart occurs, and softness of the heart also occurs; both are occurrences. It is obligatory upon a person to constantly observe his heart: is it softer or not? Is it humble before Allah or not? Is it sincere to Allah or not? Outward deeds, every person can perform them in the best manner, can he not?

* Student: Yes.

* Shaykh: The hypocrite may perform prayer in the best manner and may give charity, but the actions of the heart are, by Allah, the difficult ones. Free your heart from the bondage of sins so that the Lord may open [it to you].

If someone asks: "What is the remedy for hardness of heart?" This is a question that often comes from some of the upright whom Allah has blessed with steadfastness, but then they experience a shock and their hearts harden.

The answer: among the causes of removing hardness is:

Frequent recitation of the Qur'an with reflection, and that you feel while reading that this is the speech of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, not the speech of humans, the speech of Allah, Creator of the heavens and the earth. Then you will glorify this speech and benefit from it.

Second: frequent remembrance (dhikr), remembrance of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Increase the remembrance of Allah. Remembering Allah, Mighty and Majestic, involves no difficulty, because what moves is the tongue and the lips, and there is no difficulty in it. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Unquestionably, by the remembrance of Allah are hearts assured﴾ [al-Ra'd 28].

Among them: keeping company with the righteous, for keeping company with the righteous brings a person much good. In the hadith: "The righteous companion is like the carrier of musk: either he will give you some, or you will buy from him, or you will smell a pleasant fragrance from him" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5534), and Muslim (2628/146), from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari]. Be keen to keep company with the righteous, but benefit from them and benefit them, for not everyone is infallible. You benefit them and they benefit you.

Among them, i.e., among the causes of softening the heart: showing mercy to the young, especially orphans, for it necessitates tenderness of heart. Try it and you will find out. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Show mercy to those on the earth, and He who is in heaven will show mercy to you" [narrated by Abu Dawud (4941), and al-Tirmidhi (1924), with his wording, from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr].

There are other causes that appear to one who reflects on the remedy for hardness of heart. I ask Allah, Exalted, to soften all our hearts for His remembrance and His obedience. Indeed, He is over all things capable.

* Student: Disciplining the self with some sort of [hunger], starving it and punishing it. Is this correct?

* Shaykh: This does not appear so, and it is not from the Sharia either, because the self has a right. It is true that excess in food, drink, clothing, dwellings and means of transport is not praiseworthy. But making oneself hungry is not part of the Sharia.

* Student: On the basis that one knows oneself, meaning for example if one reduces the quantity of food or reduces...?

* Shaykh: That is not contrary. Reduce, without going hungry; let one eat a third for food, a third for drink, and a third for breath. But the problem now is that some people say: "Abu Hurayrah drank milk until he could not find a passage for it" [narrated by al-Bukhari (6452) in similar wording, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah]. Abu Hurayrah did that once, but these people make it every time. The common people say: "Water is heavy and passes through even if the stomach is full of food, and breath is a spear that the self finds hard." It is as if this common person says: fill the belly. But the truth is that a full belly always harms, and that when a person reduces, it is healthier for him. Try it and you will see. Yes, at times the food is good and appetizing and you cannot eat little, or you come to it while hungry, and from the intensity of hunger your appetite is strong and you eat a lot. But discipline yourself.

* Student: The mercy: "Show mercy to those on the earth, and He who is in heaven will show mercy to you" [narrated by Abu Dawud (4941), and al-Tirmidhi (1924), with his wording, from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr]. Does it include even creatures and animals, does it encompass everything?

* Shaykh: Yes, it encompasses everything. Do you show mercy to animals? Yes, show mercy to animals. Do not burden the camel with more than it can bear.

* Student: (...) The common people say: "This is permissible, this is an animal that does not feel, so beat it"?

* Shaykh: No, I seek refuge in Allah. It feels. How could it not feel?! Does not a camel, when you strike it, foam at the mouth?

* Student: Regarding those whom it is predominantly thought that the proof has not been established against them because they follow great scholars and so on, how should one deal with them if they are doing acts of shirk? Does one treat them as Muslims or as disbelievers?

* Shaykh: With these we withhold judgment, and when their funerals are brought, one makes an exception, saying: "O Allah, forgive him if he was a believer."

* Among the benefits of the verse: the affirmation of hardness of heart, which is its rigidity and its failure to soften to the truth, due to His saying: ﴿But their hearts became hardened﴾.

* Among its benefits: that Satan makes evil deeds attractive to the children of Adam, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And Satan made attractive to them what they were doing﴾, and in another verse: ﴿Satan made their deeds attractive to them﴾ [al-Anfal 48].

* Among the benefits: God, blessed and exalted, may give power over a servant to someone who is his enemy, and this is not considered injustice on the part of God, Mighty and Majestic. Rather, God has made this enemy clear to us and warned us against following his footsteps, so we have no excuse.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: when Satan is given power over a man, what is bad in his eyes becomes good, and what is good becomes bad. This is based on His saying: ﴿And Satan made attractive to them what they were doing﴾, and it is well known that they were engaged in sins.

Then the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of﴾, to the end of the verse.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: God hastened punishment for them, but in the manner of gradual deception (istidraj). This is based on His saying: ﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We opened to them the gates of everything﴾.

* Among the benefits: a person should beware of the punishment of God, Mighty and Majestic, when God bestows upon him the ease of worldly affairs, such as food, drink, marriage, mounts and dwelling. He should not be deceived by this, for it may be istidraj. For this reason some of the early generations (salaf) said: "When you see God, Mighty and Majestic, bestowing favors upon a person while he persists in disobedience, know that this is istidraj."[[Recorded by Ahmad in al-Musnad (17311) as a marfu' hadith from the narration of 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir; we have not found it as a saying of anyone other than him.]] They have spoken truly. So do not be deceived, O human being, for you may be tested with blessings just as you may be tested with afflictions, and the trial through blessings may be more severe than the trial through afflictions.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the one in whose hand is ease and hardship is God, based on His saying: ﴿We opened to them the gates of everything﴾.

* Among the benefits of the verse: it is obligatory to beware of exultation that is arrogant joy (fara' al-batar) in the blessings of God, Mighty and Majestic, based on His saying: ﴿They rejoiced in what they had been given﴾, meaning, joy of arrogance. As for when a person rejoices in what pleases him of the affairs of this world or of the Hereafter, with the joy of happiness and delight in the blessing of God, there is no harm in this. God, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Say: "By the grace of God and His mercy, let them rejoice in that"﴾ [Yunus 58].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: punishment may come to a person suddenly. While he is in his comfort and joy in this world, immersed in disobedience to God, behold, punishment comes upon him unexpectedly. Whether this punishment is general and comprehensive or specific, he may be afflicted with illness, or with accidents that break and crush him, or with sudden death. For this reason He said: ﴿We seized them suddenly﴾, meaning, they were seized abruptly; that is, sudden (mubaghat), and the sudden is a thing a person does not expect, so it befalls him unforeseen.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: this seizing with which God threatened is a destructive seizure, based on His saying: ﴿Then behold, they were despairing﴾, meaning, they were hopeless of every good.

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And We certainly sent [messengers] to nations before you﴾ [al-An'am 42]. How often this expression recurs in the Noble Qur'an, like this one. The scholars said: the lam (لَ) here is a preface to an oath (muwatti'a lil-qasam), meaning that it prepares for an oath, so there is an implied oath before it. The lam prefaces the oath and emphasizes it, and qad (قَدْ) is also emphatic, so there are three emphases in this.

﴿We sent to nations before you﴾, meaning: We sent messengers to nations before you. ﴿Umam﴾ is the plural of ﴿ummah﴾, and the word ummah in the Noble Qur'an carries several meanings. It is used to mean an imam (leader), as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, Abraham was a [complete] ummah, devoutly obedient to Allah﴾ [al-Nahl 120], meaning an imam. It is used to mean a period of time, as in the words of Allah: ﴿And he remembered after a period (ummah) [of time]﴾ [Yusuf 45], meaning after a time. And it is used to mean a group, as here, meaning a group and a people, and similar.

Does it have any other meaning? It has a fourth meaning, which I have forgotten, namely religion (millah), as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, we found our fathers upon an ummah﴾ [al-Zukhruf 22], meaning upon a religion. So it has four meanings in the Noble Qur'an.

His saying ﴿to nations before you﴾ means all the nations to which messengers were sent, all of them, before the Messenger (ﷺ), because he is their seal.

﴿So We seized them with adversity and hardship﴾. ﴿So We seized them with adversity﴾: the fa' (فَ) here is conjunctive. Is it conjoined to the sending of the messengers, meaning that the messengers were sent so that these people would be seized with adversity and hardship? No. Rather, there is an ellipsis in the verse, whose implied meaning is: "so they denied," or "so they disbelieved," or something similar. This is called ijaz hadhf (brevity through omission), because brevity according to the rhetoricians is of two kinds: ijaz qasr (brevity by compression), which is when few words carry many meanings, and ijaz hadhf, which is when something is omitted from a short utterance and the context indicates it. Here there is no doubt that something has been omitted from this statement, and the implied meaning is: "so they denied."

﴿So We seized them with adversity and hardship﴾. ﴿Al-ba'sa'﴾ means hardship, and ﴿al-darra'﴾ means harm. ﴿That they might humble themselves﴾: the la'alla (لَعَلَّ) here indicates cause, meaning in order that they might humble themselves before Allah, Mighty and Majestic. But did this happen?

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Then why, when Our punishment came to them, did they not humble themselves?﴾ [al-An'am 43], meaning: Our punishment. The word ﴿lawla﴾ (لَوْلَا) here means ﴿halla﴾ (هَلَّا), meaning: why, when the punishment came to them, did they not humble themselves? The answer is: no. Therefore He said: ﴿But their hearts became hardened﴾, meaning they became rigid and did not soften, and they remained upon what they were upon. ﴿And Satan made attractive to them what they were doing﴾. The word ﴿zayyana﴾ (زَيَّنَ) means ﴿hassana﴾ (حَسَّنَ), meaning he made appealing to them what they were doing, that is, of sins, disbelief and polytheism. He did not limit himself to making the matter trivial in their hearts, but rather he made it attractive to them.

﴿And Satan made attractive to them what they were doing﴾. ﴿Al-Shaytan﴾ here refers to the category and not one specific devil, just as you say "al-insan" (the human) to refer to the category.

﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We opened for them the gates of all things﴾ [al-An'am 44]. ﴿When they forgot what they had been reminded of﴾: ﴿nasu﴾ here means they abandoned and turned away from what they had been reminded of. ﴿We opened for them the gates of all things﴾ means: of worldly bounties. Allah opened for them the gates of every worldly bounty: provision, security, ease, and other kinds of luxury.

﴿Until when they rejoiced in what they had been given, We seized them suddenly﴾. ﴿Until when they rejoiced﴾: that is, rejoiced with arrogance and exultation. ﴿In what they had been given﴾: that is, in what they had been given of what Allah had opened to them. ﴿We seized them suddenly﴾: We seized them with what? With punishment. ﴿Suddenly﴾: that is, something unexpected that had not occurred to them, because they had immersed themselves in luxury and forgotten the punishment. ﴿We seized them suddenly, and at once they were in despair﴾. ﴿Then at once﴾: this "idha" (إذا) is for sudden occurrence, and the meaning is: despair overtook them, and it is ibla's (إبلاس), which is despair of the mercy of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

* In these noble verses, first: the establishment of proof against the creation by sending messengers. This is like His saying in Surat al-Nisa': ﴿Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him, and We revealed to Abraham and Ishmael﴾ [al-Nisa' 163], up to His saying: ﴿as bringers of good news and warners, so that mankind will have no argument against Allah after the messengers﴾ [al-Nisa' 165]. And among the completeness of the proof in sending messengers is that the messengers [speak] in the language of their people, meaning in the tongue of the people to whom they were sent, so that they may understand the proof.

* From this it follows that proof is not established merely by delivery, until the addressed people understand it; otherwise, what is the benefit? Rather, it is obligatory upon whoever has received it but did not understand to seek [understanding]. This last point may perhaps close off their excuse if they say: "We did not understand." We say: it is obligatory upon you to seek [understanding]. But sometimes seeking is hindered because they cannot find anyone they trust, so they remain ignorant.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse is the mercy of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, toward the creation, in that He sent messengers to them to establish the proof and to clarify the right path (al-mahajjah). Al-mahajjah means the road. Were it not for the messengers, we would not have known. Were it not for the Prophet (ﷺ) explaining to us how to perform wudu', we would not have known; how to pray, we would not have known; how to pay zakat, how to fast, how to perform Hajj, how to deal with others, we would not have known. So the sending of messengers is from the mercy of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse is the omission of the cause, so that the effect and the result are more forceful and awe-inspiring for the addressee. The cause is omitted and the consequence is mentioned, so that it is more forceful and awe-inspiring in the hearts of the addressee; this is due to His saying: ﴿So We seized them﴾, and He did not mention the denial, so that it would be more intense, and the mind would ask: why were they seized? Thus it becomes more awe-inspiring and forceful in the hearts of the addressee.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse is that Allah, Exalted, tests with adversity and hardship, but for a wisdom, not merely to inflict harm upon the creation. What is the wisdom? He explained it in His saying: ﴿that they might humble themselves﴾. Otherwise Allah cannot intend mere harm; rather, whatever harm befalls people from Allah's decrees, its purpose is the benefit of the creation.

* Among the benefits of this verse is that seizing may be by hardship, and may be by harm. It may be by hardship that a person is pained by without harm, such as fear, hunger and similar; this is hardship. A disease directly affecting a person is harm. So the seizing is either this or that.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse is the affirmation of wisdom in the acts of Allah. It is derived from His saying: ﴿that they might humble themselves﴾. The fact that Allah has wisdom in His acts and in His legislation is known to every person of intellect, because the fact that actions and rulings proceed from wisdom indicates the perfection of the Doer and the Lawgiver.

But is the wisdom of every act or ruling that comes from Allah known to us?
The answer is: no, because our intellects are too limited to encompass the wisdom of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Yet we know with certainty that it is for a wisdom. This is why, when Mother of the Believers 'A'ishah was asked: "Why does a menstruating woman make up fasts but not make up prayers?" she did not go on to give a reason by saying: "Fasting comes only once a year and its making up is easy, whereas prayer comes five times a day and night, so making it up is difficult; fasting has no equivalent within the year to take its place, whereas prayer has an equivalent: if you do not pray today, you pray tomorrow." She did not say this. She said: "This used to happen to us, and we were commanded to make up the fast, and we were not commanded to make up the prayer." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (321), and Muslim (335/69), with his wording, from the hadith of 'A'ishah.] So she made the bare ruling itself the wisdom.

Likewise, every believer must believe that all of Allah's acts and all of Allah's laws are for a wisdom, but sometimes we know it and sometimes we do not.

The jurists, may Allah have mercy on them, describe a thing whose wisdom is unknown as ta'abbudi (devotional), meaning that we are only obliged to worship through it, not to know its wisdom. Sometimes they call a thing ta'abbudi while its wisdom is known, and sometimes that statement is correct.

Some in this community denied wisdom and said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does whatever He wills merely by will, and rules as He wills merely by will. This is an error and a deficiency. They said: because if He did something for a wisdom, that would be for a purpose, and doing something for a purpose is a deficiency.

And among their corrupt expressions, pleasing in appearance or sound, is: "Allah is exempt from accidents (a'rad), parts (ab'ad), and purposes (aghrad)." So according to them He is exempt from accidents, the second is parts, and the third is purposes.

As for accidents, they mean by this what befalls the doer, such as doing or not doing and the like. That is why they deny the istiwa' (settling) upon the Throne, and deny the descent to the lowest heaven.

As for parts, they mean the face, the hands and similar.

As for purposes, they mean wisdom. They say: if His acts or His laws were for a wisdom, He would have a purpose, and Allah, Exalted, is exempt from purposes.

The answer to this is easy: is the purpose contained in wisdom for the benefit of Allah or for the benefit of the creation? The second, certainly. Otherwise Allah says: ﴿If you disbelieve, then indeed Allah is free of need of you; and He does not approve disbelief for His servants. And if you are grateful, He approves it for you﴾ [al-Zumar 7]. So this wisdom contained in the act, the legislation or the ruling is for the benefit of the creation. Then is it perfection or deficiency? It is perfection.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse is the obligation of humbling oneself to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Tadarru' means seeking refuge and turning in repentance to Allah, Exalted, and performing all that is obligatory toward Him, of every kind: belief, speech or action.

Then He said: ﴿Then why, when Our punishment came to them...﴾ to the end.

* Among its benefits: clarifying the severity of hardness of these punished people. When punishment came to them, so that they would humble themselves, their situation was reversed; rather, that increased the hardness of their hearts. We ask Allah for well-being. What should have happened is that they humble themselves before Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

This may befall a person: that adversity and hardship only increase him in hardness of heart and discontent with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, may Allah protect us, and in feelings that are not appropriate. For some people, when afflicted with a trial, say: "What is this? Why is He wronging me? Why does this befall me and not befall others?" Then their hearts harden. We seek refuge in Allah.

Therefore patience is required of one who is struck by a calamity, so that his heart does not harden. It is said to him: "You are a servant of Allah, are you not? A servant is subject to the action of his master, and Allah does with His servant what He wills, just as He does in the heavens what He wills, on the earth what He wills, with the winds what He wills. Likewise you, you are a creature among creatures, and He does with you what He wills. But upon you is patience in hardship, and gratitude in ease."

Moreover, praise be to Allah, the harm that befalls a person is an expiation for his sins, and how many sins there are. Anything that befalls you, even a thorn, if it strikes you, it expiates sins. If you seek reward for it, it establishes the reward of the patient. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has not neglected anything that benefits the creation.

* Among the benefits of this verse: the affirmation of the hardening of the heart after its softness, due to His saying: ﴿But their hearts became hardened﴾, and as in the verse of al-Baqarah: ﴿Then your hearts became hard after that﴾ [al-Baqarah 74]. So hardness of the heart occurs, and softness of the heart also occurs; both are occurrences. It is obligatory upon a person to constantly observe his heart: is it softer or not? Is it humble before Allah or not? Is it sincere to Allah or not? Outward deeds, every person can perform them in the best manner, can he not?

* Student: Yes.

* Shaykh: The hypocrite may perform prayer in the best manner and may give charity, but the actions of the heart are, by Allah, the difficult ones. Free your heart from the bondage of sins so that the Lord may open [it to you].

If someone asks: "What is the remedy for hardness of heart?" This is a question that often comes from some of the upright whom Allah has blessed with steadfastness, but then they experience a shock and their hearts harden.

The answer: among the causes of removing hardness is:

Frequent recitation of the Qur'an with reflection, and that you feel while reading that this is the speech of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, not the speech of humans, the speech of Allah, Creator of the heavens and the earth. Then you will glorify this speech and benefit from it.

Second: frequent remembrance (dhikr), remembrance of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Increase the remembrance of Allah. Remembering Allah, Mighty and Majestic, involves no difficulty, because what moves is the tongue and the lips, and there is no difficulty in it. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Unquestionably, by the remembrance of Allah are hearts assured﴾ [al-Ra'd 28].

Among them: keeping company with the righteous, for keeping company with the righteous brings a person much good. In the hadith: "The righteous companion is like the carrier of musk: either he will give you some, or you will buy from him, or you will smell a pleasant fragrance from him" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5534), and Muslim (2628/146), from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari]. Be keen to keep company with the righteous, but benefit from them and benefit them, for not everyone is infallible. You benefit them and they benefit you.

Among them, i.e., among the causes of softening the heart: showing mercy to the young, especially orphans, for it necessitates tenderness of heart. Try it and you will find out. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Show mercy to those on the earth, and He who is in heaven will show mercy to you" [narrated by Abu Dawud (4941), and al-Tirmidhi (1924), with his wording, from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr].

There are other causes that appear to one who reflects on the remedy for hardness of heart. I ask Allah, Exalted, to soften all our hearts for His remembrance and His obedience. Indeed, He is over all things capable.

* Student: Disciplining the self with some sort of [hunger], starving it and punishing it. Is this correct?

* Shaykh: This does not appear so, and it is not from the Sharia either, because the self has a right. It is true that excess in food, drink, clothing, dwellings and means of transport is not praiseworthy. But making oneself hungry is not part of the Sharia.

* Student: On the basis that one knows oneself, meaning for example if one reduces the quantity of food or reduces...?

* Shaykh: That is not contrary. Reduce, without going hungry; let one eat a third for food, a third for drink, and a third for breath. But the problem now is that some people say: "Abu Hurayrah drank milk until he could not find a passage for it" [narrated by al-Bukhari (6452) in similar wording, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah]. Abu Hurayrah did that once, but these people make it every time. The common people say: "Water is heavy and passes through even if the stomach is full of food, and breath is a spear that the self finds hard." It is as if this common person says: fill the belly. But the truth is that a full belly always harms, and that when a person reduces, it is healthier for him. Try it and you will see. Yes, at times the food is good and appetizing and you cannot eat little, or you come to it while hungry, and from the intensity of hunger your appetite is strong and you eat a lot. But discipline yourself.

* Student: The mercy: "Show mercy to those on the earth, and He who is in heaven will show mercy to you" [narrated by Abu Dawud (4941), and al-Tirmidhi (1924), with his wording, from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr]. Does it include even creatures and animals, does it encompass everything?

* Shaykh: Yes, it encompasses everything. Do you show mercy to animals? Yes, show mercy to animals. Do not burden the camel with more than it can bear.

* Student: (...) The common people say: "This is permissible, this is an animal that does not feel, so beat it"?

* Shaykh: No, I seek refuge in Allah. It feels. How could it not feel?! Does not a camel, when you strike it, foam at the mouth?

* Student: Regarding those whom it is predominantly thought that the proof has not been established against them because they follow great scholars and so on, how should one deal with them if they are doing acts of shirk? Does one treat them as Muslims or as disbelievers?

* Shaykh: With these we withhold judgment, and when their funerals are brought, one makes an exception, saying: "O Allah, forgive him if he was a believer."

* Among the benefits of the verse: the affirmation of hardness of heart, which is its rigidity and its failure to soften to the truth, due to His saying: ﴿But their hearts became hardened﴾.

* Among its benefits: that Satan makes evil deeds attractive to the children of Adam, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And Satan made attractive to them what they were doing﴾, and in another verse: ﴿Satan made their deeds attractive to them﴾ [al-Anfal 48].

* Among the benefits: God, blessed and exalted, may give power over a servant to someone who is his enemy, and this is not considered injustice on the part of God, Mighty and Majestic. Rather, God has made this enemy clear to us and warned us against following his footsteps, so we have no excuse.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: when Satan is given power over a man, what is bad in his eyes becomes good, and what is good becomes bad. This is based on His saying: ﴿And Satan made attractive to them what they were doing﴾, and it is well known that they were engaged in sins.

Then the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of﴾, to the end of the verse.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: God hastened punishment for them, but in the manner of gradual deception (istidraj). This is based on His saying: ﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We opened to them the gates of everything﴾.

* Among the benefits: a person should beware of the punishment of God, Mighty and Majestic, when God bestows upon him the ease of worldly affairs, such as food, drink, marriage, mounts and dwelling. He should not be deceived by this, for it may be istidraj. For this reason some of the early generations (salaf) said: "When you see God, Mighty and Majestic, bestowing favors upon a person while he persists in disobedience, know that this is istidraj."[[Recorded by Ahmad in al-Musnad (17311) as a marfu' hadith from the narration of 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir; we have not found it as a saying of anyone other than him.]] They have spoken truly. So do not be deceived, O human being, for you may be tested with blessings just as you may be tested with afflictions, and the trial through blessings may be more severe than the trial through afflictions.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the one in whose hand is ease and hardship is God, based on His saying: ﴿We opened to them the gates of everything﴾.

* Among the benefits of the verse: it is obligatory to beware of exultation that is arrogant joy (fara' al-batar) in the blessings of God, Mighty and Majestic, based on His saying: ﴿They rejoiced in what they had been given﴾, meaning, joy of arrogance. As for when a person rejoices in what pleases him of the affairs of this world or of the Hereafter, with the joy of happiness and delight in the blessing of God, there is no harm in this. God, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Say: "By the grace of God and His mercy, let them rejoice in that"﴾ [Yunus 58].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: punishment may come to a person suddenly. While he is in his comfort and joy in this world, immersed in disobedience to God, behold, punishment comes upon him unexpectedly. Whether this punishment is general and comprehensive or specific, he may be afflicted with illness, or with accidents that break and crush him, or with sudden death. For this reason He said: ﴿We seized them suddenly﴾, meaning, they were seized abruptly; that is, sudden (mubaghat), and the sudden is a thing a person does not expect, so it befalls him unforeseen.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: this seizing with which God threatened is a destructive seizure, based on His saying: ﴿Then behold, they were despairing﴾, meaning, they were hopeless of every good.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿So the last remnant of the people who did wrong was cut off. And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.﴾ [al-An'am 45]

﴿Fa-qutiʿa﴾ (the fa') is a conjunction (ʿatf) and indicates sequence and immediacy (al-tartib wa'l-taʿqib). ﴿Qutiʿa dabir al-qawm﴾ means: they were destroyed to the last one of them. For when the dabir (the last, i.e., the end) is cut off, what came before it is even more so. The Exalted did not name the one who cut them off, because he is known, and he is Allah, Mighty and Majestic. However, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, in matters that are displeasing, uses the passive form (sigha ma lam yusamma fa'iluh): ﴿fa-qutiʿa dabir﴾. This is like the saying of the jinn: ﴿And we do not know whether evil is intended for those on the earth, or whether their Lord intends for them guidance﴾ [al-Jinn 10]. The jinn believe that the one who intends evil is Allah, Mighty and Majestic; they know that good and evil are in the hand of Allah, that He is the Governor. But they disliked attributing evil to Allah, so they said: ﴿whether evil is intended for those on the earth, or whether their Lord intends for them guidance﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of causes (ithbat al-asbab), by His saying ﴿who did wrong﴾, since this punishment is ordained upon a people characterized by wrongdoing. So wrongdoing is a cause for punishment. This is from the perfection of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: that His acts are for a wisdom, and His legislative rulings are for a wisdom.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that wrongdoing is a cause of punishment and destruction, because when a ruling is linked to an attribute, that attribute becomes its cause; the ruling grows stronger with its strength and weakens with its weakness.

﴿The last remnant of the people who did wrong. And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.﴾
