* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that Allah is praised for cutting off the last remnant of the wrongdoers. And so He is, for He, glorified and exalted, is praised for bringing blessings and for warding off calamities. When Allah destroys a wrongdoer, that is part of the completeness of His justice and His mercy, because it becomes a warning (nakal) to what lies before it and what lies after it.

As for the meaning, there is no difficulty in it. We have said: ﴿dabir al-qawm alladhina zalamu﴾ means its last part, and when the last is cut off, the first is cut off too. As for ﴿alladhina zalamu﴾, the intended meaning is the disbelievers, because every disbeliever is a wrongdoer toward whom? Toward himself, as the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And they did not wrong Us, but they wronged themselves﴾ [al-Baqarah 57]. And he is a transgressor toward Allah, in that he has not fulfilled the right that is obligatory upon him.

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Say: Tell me, if Allah were to take away your hearing and your sight and seal your hearts, who is a god other than Allah to bring them back to you?﴾ [al-An'am 46] ﴿Say: Tell me﴾, i.e., say, O Muhammad: inform me, ﴿if Allah were to take away your hearing﴾ so that you do not hear speech, ﴿and your sight﴾ so that you do not see deeds, ﴿and seal your hearts﴾ so that there is no awareness or intellect in you, ﴿who is a god other than Allah to bring them back to you?﴾ Their answer would be: no one; because they acknowledge and confess the lordship of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and what follows from it.

He, Exalted, said: ﴿Look﴾, meaning a look of consideration (i'tibar); i.e., a look of insight, ﴿how We vary the signs﴾, i.e., We diversify them. The word (ayat) is the plural of (ayah), which is the sign by which tranquility is attained, because it contains evidence. That is: an ayah is not merely a sign, but a sign that serves as proof of something, so it is more specific than a sign in general. The meaning of ﴿We vary﴾ is that He diversifies the signs: sun and moon, night and day, ease and hardship, heat and cold, and so on, varied signs.

﴿Yet they turn away﴾, i.e., they turn away from the truth and from the signs. Consider His saying ﴿Yet﴾, which denotes delay; that is: then, after the matter has become clear to them and manifest, they turn away and gain no benefit.

* In this noble verse: a challenge to those who associate partners with Allah, through this matter which is easy for Allah compared with other things; namely, that if Allah takes away their hearing and sight and seals their hearts, they will not turn except to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and this is a challenge to them.

* Among the benefits of this verse: when a person is afflicted in his hearing, his sight, his heart, or the rest of his body, he should turn to whom? To Allah, Mighty and Majestic, because no one can benefit him.

If someone says: Then should we not go to doctors, nor to reciters, nor use medicines?

The answer: No, rather go to doctors, use medicines, and go to reciters; but those who seek cure by incantation (istirqa') have their rank lowered in comparison with those who enter Paradise without reckoning or punishment. A person is commanded to take the means, and indeed the command to seek treatment has come; only we do not seek treatment with what is forbidden.[[Narrated by Abu Dawud (3874) from the hadith of Abu al-Darda'.]]

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the danger of these three faculties being blocked; namely, hearing, so that one does not hear the signs, sight, so that one does not see them, and the heart, so that it does not comprehend them. So a person must be mindful of these three matters.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the mercy of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in that He varies the signs for His servants. Had He willed, He could have withheld the variation and left people stumbling blindly; but it is among Allah's blessings that He shows His servants the signs, varies them and diversifies them. This is from the mercy of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; that is, if a person is not moved by one sign, he is moved by another sign and the purpose is achieved. How many a person misses many signs and does not take heed from them, and then is afflicted by one sign and takes heed. Indeed, some upright people have told me about themselves that they were slipping into desires and distraction, and when a close relative of theirs died, they became upright. All the previous signs had not benefited them, but when the relative died they became upright and realized that their end would be like that of this one, so they returned to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the rebuke of those to whom signs were displayed but who turned away; because of His saying: ﴿Look how We vary the signs, yet they turn away﴾, i.e., they turn away from them and do not take heed from them. Therein is a warning against a person turning away after the signs have become manifest; for if he turns away after the signs have become manifest, he becomes of the category of what? We have three categories: those who earned anger, those who went astray, and the people of uprightness. He becomes of the category of those who earned anger, because he knew the truth but rebelled against it: ﴿Yet they turn away﴾.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 6, verse 47:

He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿Say: Tell me, if the punishment of Allah comes upon you suddenly or openly, will any be destroyed except the wrongdoing people?﴾ [al-An'am 47] Meaning: inform me. The discussion of the grammatical analysis (i'rab) of this sentence has already passed. ﴿If the punishment of Allah comes upon you﴾ i.e., the retribution of Allah, ﴿suddenly﴾ as if it came upon you while you were asleep, ﴿or openly﴾ as if it came upon you while you were awake. This is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Do the people of the towns feel secure that Our punishment will not come upon them by night while they are asleep? Or do the people of the towns feel secure that Our punishment will not come upon them in the morning while they are at play?﴾ [al-A'raf 97-98]. The first is ﴿suddenly﴾ and the second is ﴿openly﴾.

﴿Suddenly or openly, will any be destroyed except the wrongdoing people?﴾ Meaning: if it comes upon you, are you wronged when the punishment of Allah comes upon you? In either case the answer is no. So the sentence in His saying ﴿will any be destroyed except the wrongdoing people?﴾ affirms the seizing by punishment, and that they were not seized unjustly but because of their evil deeds.

In this verse there is a warning against the descent of punishment, whether suddenly or openly. So a person who is disobedient should not feel secure that punishment will descend upon him. But do you think that punishment is only bodily punishment? No. Bodily punishment is without doubt a punishment, but greater than that is turning away from the religion of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, as He said: ﴿But if they turn away, then know that Allah only intends to afflict them for some of their sins﴾ [al-Ma'idah 49]. For this reason the scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, said: sins are the courier of disbelief; a person brings them down stage by stage, just as the post delivers a distance stage by stage, until he arrives at disbelief, and we seek refuge in Allah. The reason for this is clear: sins harden the heart, blacken the heart and dry up the heart until it becomes dead, and calamity descends. But, praise be to Allah, Allah has placed a remedy for every disease. Accompany the sin with repentance, and when you repent, repentance demolishes what came before it, so it is as if you had not sinned. And to Allah belongs praise.

Indeed, when a person repents to Allah with sincere repentance, his condition after repentance may be even more complete than his condition before the sin. Consider the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿And Adam disobeyed his Lord, and so he erred. Then his Lord chose him, accepted his repentance, and guided him﴾ [Ta-Ha 121-122]. His rank was raised when he repented of disobedience. This is an observed matter, because when a person remains continuously in his state of obedience to Allah, his heart remains unmoved, doing these things as if they were instinct. When he commits a sin, he feels shame before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is ashamed before Allah, and turns humbly to Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and he remembers this sin at every moment. For this reason some of the early generations (salaf) said: sin, for the dissolute person, is like a fly that lands on his nose and he drives it away, meaning it is light to him; but for the people of living hearts, sin is like a mountain which they feel as a heavy burden and fear, until they repent to Allah, Blessed and Exalted.

His saying: ﴿will any be destroyed except the wrongdoing people?﴾ is an interrogative with the meaning of negation, so (hal) here means (ma). We have mentioned earlier that when the interrogative carries the meaning of negation, it becomes stronger than plain negation, because it includes both negation and challenge, as if the speaker says to the addressee: "Produce for me this thing," so the interrogative with the meaning of negation is stronger than plain negation.

﴿Will any be destroyed except the wrongdoing people?﴾ Wrongdoing is divided into two types: wrongdoing against the right of Allah, and wrongdoing against the rights of the servants. As for wrongdoing against the right of Allah, its remedy is repentance, however great it is, even if it is shirk with Allah, Blessed and Exalted; indeed, even if it is cursing Allah, according to the preponderant view, repentance is permitted. The right of a human being is not removed except by returning it to him or by his pardoning it. Otherwise, however much a person repents, sincerely turns to Allah and feels remorse, it does not suffice him until he returns it. Indeed, returning wrongful takings to their owners is among the conditions of repentance, because among the conditions of repentance is that a person abandons the sin, and there is no abandoning of sin while continuing to take the property of others.

Then the Exalted said: ﴿And We do not send the messengers except as bringers of good news and warners﴾ [al-An'am 48]. ﴿We do not send﴾: (ma) is a negation particle, and (illa) is a particle of restriction. Irsal (sending) means entrusting another person with conveying a message from the one who sent him. For this reason, the preferred view on the matter is that the messengers were given revelation of the sharia and were commanded to convey it.

﴿Except as bringers of good news and warners﴾: ﴿bringers of good news﴾ to whoever follows them with good, namely Paradise, and ﴿warners﴾ to whoever opposes them with the Fire. This is their function. Tabshir (giving good news) is informing someone of what gladdens him, and indhar (warning) is frightening someone with what distresses him.

If someone says: How can you say that tabshir is informing of what gladdens, when Allah the Exalted has made it informing of what distresses? Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of Allah - give them tidings of a painful punishment (34) On the Day it will be heated in the fire of Hell﴾, to the end of the verse [at-Tawbah 34-35]?

The answer: Warning affects the skin just as good news does, does it not? And the origin of tabshir is informing of what gladdens; the origin of its being called tabshir is that the skin (bashrah) is affected by it, so you see a man's face brighten and his chest expand.

... Is that not so? And the origin of tabshir is informing of what gladdens; the origin of its being called tabshir is that the skin is affected by it, so you see a man's face brighten and his chest expand.

Or it may be said: ﴿So give them tidings of a painful punishment﴾ [Aal Imran 21] is used in the manner of mockery (tahakkum), where warning is expressed with the word tabshir as a parallel to this. Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿Taste! Indeed you are the mighty, the noble﴾ [ad-Dukhan 49]. ﴿Taste﴾ is an imperative of humiliation, and ﴿indeed you are the mighty, the noble﴾ [ad-Dukhan 49]. Some exegetes said: this is of the type of mockery against him, so that his grief increases upon his grief. It was also said: the meaning is ﴿you are the mighty, the noble﴾ in this world, and in the Hereafter you have nothing but humiliation.

He said: ﴿And We do not send the messengers except as bringers of good news and warners﴾ [al-An'am 48]. Why is this restricted to good news and warning? So that no claimant may assert that the function of the messengers relates to lordship (rububiyyah), and that they have a share in managing creation. This is clear: the messengers have nothing but to give good news to people and warn them, only that. As for guiding them, providing for them, or repelling evil from them, these are not among their functions.

Then He said: ﴿Whoever believes and makes amends﴾ [al-An'am 48], ﴿And those who deny﴾, to the end of the verse [al-An'am 49].

The distinction is evident. The nabi (prophet) is from naba', which means news. He was informed by revelation but was not charged with conveying it; he worships by it himself, and whoever follows him is upon guidance. But the rasul (messenger) is charged to convey what he was sent with. This is what the majority of scholars hold, and it is clear, because Adam was a prophet and was not completing the sharia of anyone before him; rather his sharia was independent. This shows that the view that a prophet is one who worships by the sharia of one who came before him is a weak view, and that the view of the majority is more correct.

* * *
I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And We do not send the messengers except as bringers of good news and warners﴾. The discussion of this has already preceded; we now proceed to the benefits.

* Among the benefits: ﴿And We do not send the messengers except as bringers of good news and warners. Whoever believes and makes amends﴾, meaning: believes in his heart and makes righteous deeds, ﴿there is no fear for them, nor will they grieve﴾ [al-An'am 48]. However, ﴿believes﴾ here is unrestricted, not limited by anything, except that the texts have restricted it, as in the saying of the Exalted: ﴿But righteousness is [in] one who believes in Allah and the Last Day and the angels and the Book and the prophets﴾ [al-Baqarah 177], and as the Prophet (ﷺ) said in his answer to Jibril when he asked him about iman: "That you believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and divine decree, its good and its evil." [Narrated by Muslim (8/1) from the hadith of Umar ibn al-Khattab.]

﴿And makes amends﴾, meaning: makes his deeds righteous. The righteousness of deeds is not complete except by two matters:

The first: sincerity to Allah the Mighty and Majestic. Whoever associates others with Allah in worship has not made his deed righteous, even if the shirk is minor, due to the word of Allah Tabaraka wa Ta'ala in the hadith qudsi: "I am the most self-sufficient of partners in need of partners. Whoever does a deed in which he associates another with Me, I abandon him and his shirk." [Narrated by Muslim (2985/46) from the hadith of Abu Hurairah.]

The second: following the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Whoever does not follow the Messenger (ﷺ) in worship, his worship is not valid, and he is not a doer of righteousness, even if he is humble, his heart softens, and his eyes shed tears; this does not benefit him, due to the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever does a deed that is not upon our command, it is rejected." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2697) and Muslim (1718/18), and the wording is his, from the hadith of Aishah.] That is, it is rejected from him.

﴿Whoever believes and makes amends, there is no fear for them, nor will they grieve﴾. Following is not realized except when the deed agrees with the sharia in the six matters that we have often passed over, which are: agreement in the cause, the genus, the quantity, the manner, the time, and the place.

And His saying: ﴿There is no fear for them﴾ means regarding what is to come.

﴿Nor will they grieve﴾ means regarding what has passed, so they do not grieve over what passed of the world, because they were absorbed in obedience to Allah; and they do not fear punishment, because they are saved from punishment.

Ibn 'Uthaymin's commentary on surah 6, verse 49 (part 1 of 2)

Then He said: ﴿And those who denied Our signs﴾ [al-An'am 49]. This is the second category of those to whom the messengers were sent. The first category is those who believed and did righteous deeds. The second is: ﴿And those who denied Our signs﴾, meaning they rejected them and did not accept them.

﴿The punishment will touch them﴾ [al-An'am 49]. ﴿Will touch them﴾ means it will reach them directly, like the touch of one body to another. ﴿The punishment﴾ means the punishment of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

﴿For what they used to defiantly disobey﴾. This means for what they used to depart from obedience to Allah. The letter بِـ (bi) here indicates causation, meaning "because of their being," and مَا (ma) is a verbal-source particle (مصدرية), so the sentence is understood as "because they were defiantly disobeying."

* This noble verse contains benefits. Among them: Allah's favour upon His servants by sending the messengers, and the sending of messengers is necessary. That is, the wisdom of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, requires the sending of messengers, because human reason cannot independently know what is due to Allah of names, attributes and rulings, nor can it independently know the acts of worship. People are in extreme need of the messengers. ﴿Mankind was one nation﴾ [al-Baqarah 213], meaning upon one religion. Then, when they disbelieved, they split apart and differed. ﴿So Allah sent the prophets as bringers of good news and warners, and sent down with them the Book﴾, ﴿to judge between the people concerning that over which they differed﴾ [al-Baqarah 213].

* Among them: the message of the messengers includes these two things: good news (al-bishārah) and warning (al-indhār). For whom is the good news, and for whom is the warning? The good news is for whoever obeys and follows the messengers, and the warning is for whoever denies, with punishment, meaning he is warned of the punishment of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

* It follows from this benefit that the messengers, peace be upon them, did not come merely with rulings, that is, merely saying "this is lawful, this is unlawful." Rather, they combined that with good news and warning, because good news moves a person to do what is commanded. Isn't that so? For if you gave a person good news that he will obtain a treasure in such-and-such a place, you would find him racing toward it and doing what leads him to it. Warning brings about distance from sins. On this basis the call of the messengers is constructed.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: people divide, in their acceptance and reception of the call of the messengers, into two categories: believer and denier.

* A benefit of the verse: the wisdom of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in dividing people, regarding acceptance of the messengers' call, into two categories: a believer who does righteous deeds, and a denier. This is from wisdom, and even from mercy. Why? Because if there were no disbelief, the worth of Islam would not be known. For this reason 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said, as it is related from him: "Islam will not be unraveled strand by strand except by one who does not know disbelief."[[Narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah in his Musannaf (33012), and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak (8523), and its wording is: "I have known, by the Lord of the Ka'bah, when the Arabs will be destroyed: when someone who did not accompany the Messenger (ﷺ) and did not deal with the affair of the Jahiliyyah is put in charge of their affairs."]] Whoever knows disbelief cannot unravel Islam.

It is from the mercy and wisdom of Allah that people divide into two categories. Were it not for this division, would jihad occur? No. Would enjoining good and forbidding evil occur? No. Would trial and testing occur? No, because people would all be on one level. Even a person cannot (...) from people. But when they divide into believer and disbeliever, testing and examination occur for both the believer and the disbeliever. So do not think that when Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, makes the hearts of the disbelievers swerve, that there is any futility in that. Rather, it is the very essence of wisdom.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: whoever combines these two attributes, faith and reform (al-islāh), should be given good news that there is no fear upon him and no grief upon him, because of His saying: ﴿So there is no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve﴾.

If someone says: Do not believers who reform still suffer fear from enemies?

The answer: Yes, they suffer fear from enemies, but this is not the fear negated in the verse, because that fear is followed by security. With strong faith, the believer does not regard this as fear. For this reason we find the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, in their jihad and fighting alongside the Prophet (ﷺ), and after him, also receiving death themselves with a wide and open breast.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: encouraging a person toward faith and righteous deeds, and urging that by mentioning the outcome of this believer who reforms: ﴿So whoever believes and reforms﴾.

* Among the benefits in the noble verse: faith alone is not sufficient; there must be reform. But do we say that merely by corruption, or merely by abandoning righteous deeds, a person becomes a disbeliever? We say: we cannot judge a person to be a disbeliever or a believer except with evidence from the Book and the Sunnah. Who judges disbelief and judges faith? Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and His Messenger. We have no right to say "this is a disbeliever" or "this is a believer" except by evidence from the Law.

For this reason we rebuke those who repeat questions such as: Are deeds a condition for the perfection of faith, or a condition for the essence of faith? Or similar phrases. We say: all of this is unnecessary, because we have, O brothers, clear evidences: disbelief is established from the Qur'an and the Sunnah, and faith is established from the Qur'an and the Sunnah.

If the matter is between this man being a disbeliever or a believer, while he is one of the Muslims, then the basic principle is the continuation of his Islam, and it is not lawful for us to declare him a disbeliever. Can we make the white black, or the black white? No. Likewise with the legal rulings: we have no right to declare anyone a disbeliever except with evidence, nor to say "this is a believer" except with evidence. By this we are relieved of plunging into and playing with people's opinions and people's minds.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the argument from the implicit meaning (mafhūm), namely that ﴿whoever believes and reforms, there is no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve﴾, and whoever is not like that, upon him is fear and grief.

* Among the benefits of the verse that follows: that denying the signs of Allah is a cause of punishment, because of His saying: ﴿And those who denied Our signs, the punishment will touch them for what they used to defiantly disobey﴾. It should be known that the signs of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, are divided into two categories: legislative signs (āyāt sharʿiyyah) and cosmic signs (āyāt kawniyyah). The legislative signs are what the messengers brought of the laws of Allah. For if you reflect upon these rulings, whether in the Islamic nation or in earlier nations, you will find them perfectly in accord with wisdom and benefit, and that if all the people of the earth gathered to bring the like of it, they would not bring it. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Do they seek the judgement of the time of ignorance? And who is better than Allah in judgement for a people who are certain?﴾ [al-Ma'idah 50].

So do not think that any system or law reforms creation as the Islamic Shari'ah reforms it. For this reason those people went astray who went toward ruling by man-made laws that were enacted by a human. Is this human exposed to error or not? He is exposed. Second: Does he encompass all the interests of creation in all the regions of the world? No. Does he encompass the interests of creation in all future times? No. Matters change. Therefore it is not permissible to rely on these laws. Laws must be taken from the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), because Allah, exalted is He, is more knowing of creation in their present and future state, and because He is more merciful to creation, and because He is the Most Wise of judges. These are the legislative signs.

The cosmic (qadari) signs: the night and the day, meaning created things: the night and the day, the sun and the moon, the reviving of the earth after its death, and other things.

How can denial occur regarding these and those? We say: as for denial of the laws, it is either by denying the reports, saying "this is not true, reason does not accept it, and it is impossible," or by distorting the texts, distorting the text, like the statement of some of them: the meaning of "istawā" (ascended) is "istawlā" (seized dominion), and the meaning of "yad" (hand) is power, strength, or favour, and similar things. A third case is arrogance toward them, not acting upon them.

As for the cosmic signs of Allah: either a person attributes them to other than Allah, as the causalist atheists do, who attribute things to their mere causes and hold that the cause acts by itself. Or he says: they are from Allah but with another associated with Him. This too is denial of the cosmic signs of Allah, because it is shirk. Or he says: they are from Allah alone, but He has a helper. This too is disbelief regarding the cosmic signs. Thus the cosmic signs are all created things, and the legislative signs are what the messengers brought of revelation.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that these deniers will be struck by the punishment directly, because of His saying: ﴿the punishment will touch them﴾. And if they escape punishment in this world, they will not escape it in the Hereafter.

* Among the benefits of the verse: the establishment of causes (al-asbāb), because of His saying: ﴿for what they used to defiantly disobey﴾. The letter بِـ (bi) is for causation. The establishment of causes is indicated by reason and by revelation, and only a fool denies it. The Qur'an is full of this. Were it not that we are in a near period of examinations, I would have asked each of you to take, for example, half a juz' and bring the verses in which mention of causes occurs, because it has been said that there are more than a thousand proofs in the Qur'an indicating the establishment of causes. This is indeed the case. The Qur'an itself is a cause. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We sent down to you the Reminder so that you may make clear to the people what was sent down to them﴾ [al-Nahl 44], and He said: ﴿Allah makes clear to you, lest you go astray﴾ [al-Nisa' 176]. But because examinations are near, I fear that this would be an imposition. Do you agree? If Allah wills, at another time each of you can take, for example, half a juz', five pages, and derive the verses in which causes are mentioned, and they are very numerous.

People have divided regarding causes into three categories:

The first category regarded causes as effective in themselves, and that whenever the cause exists the caused thing must exist. These are the naturalists (al-tab'iyyūn), who do not acknowledge Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and their ruling is clear: they are, what? Disbelievers.

The second category denied causes. They denied the effect of causes upon their effects, and said: these causes are merely signs, and the caused thing occurs at the cause, not by the cause. These went astray in both transmitted and rational terms. For even if a person threw a bottle with a stone and struck it, and then it broke, the stone did not break the bottle. Why? You may not say "it broke the bottle." If you said this you would be a polytheist, Allah forbid. But if I said this, I would in reality be a monotheist, affirming wisdom for Allah. Could you, if you came to a child who struck the bottle and broke it, have him say, "I did not break it, the breaking occurred at my act, not by my act"? Absolutely not. But some elderly people of mature intellects, though not of right guidance, say: "There are no causes. The thing occurred at the cause, not by the cause."

The third category affirmed causes, but made their effect on their effects depend upon the effective powers that Allah placed in them, and made the Creator, first and last, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. They said: If Allah willed, these causes would not have an effect. For example, fire burns, there is no difficulty. And when Abraham, peace be upon him, was thrown into it, Allah said to it: ﴿O fire, be cool and safe upon Abraham﴾ [al-Anbiya' 69], and it became cool and safe. Did this cause have an effect on its effect? No, because Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Be cool and safe﴾ [al-Anbiya' 69]. This statement is the one that is definitively correct, and I do not say merely "the preponderant," it is the definitively correct one. Whatever else is opposed to it is error and falsehood.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that defiant disobedience (al-fisq) is applied to disbelief, because of His saying: ﴿for what they used to defiantly disobey﴾. For He said "those who denied Our signs," which is disbelief without difficulty, since denial of the signs is disbelief. Then He said "for what they used to defiantly disobey." Read the saying of Allah, exalted is He, in Surat al-Sajdah: ﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, for them are gardens of refuge as a lodging, for what they used to do. But as for those who defiantly disobeyed, their refuge is the Fire. Every time they wish to leave it, they are returned into it, and it is said to them: Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny﴾ [al-Sajdah 19-20]. What is "fisq" here? Disbelief. But fisq may also be applied to what is less than disbelief, and this is what the jurists (al-fuqaha') meant, may Allah have mercy on them. And from it is the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿But Allah has endeared faith to you and made it beautiful in your hearts, and made disbelief, defiant disobedience (al-fusūq), and rebellion (al-'iṣyān) hateful to you﴾ [al-Hujurat 7]. Here, is "fusūq" what is less than disbelief, or disbelief? It is what is less than disbelief, it is definite, and the reason for its definiteness is that it is conjoined (ʿaṭf) to disbelief, and conjunction implies difference.

* A benefit of the verse: the perfect justice of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in that He punished these only because they deserved punishment for their defiant disobedience, as a fitting recompense.

If someone says: There came in the authentic hadith: "Indeed, if Allah were to punish the people of His heavens and His earth, He would punish them, and He would not be unjust to them"?[[Narrated by Abu Dawud (4699) and Ibn Majah (77), from the hadith of Ubayy ibn Ka'b.]]

The answer: There is no difficulty in this. That is, if the punishment of the people of the earth and the heavens were to occur, this punishment would be deserved by them, and He would not be unjust to them. The meaning is not that if He punished them without a crime He would not be unjust, because punishing them without injustice is something Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has made impossible for Himself and forbidden Himself. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And your Lord would never destroy the towns unjustly while their people are reforming﴾ [Hud 117], and He said: ﴿And your Lord is not ever unjust to the servants﴾ [Fussilat 46]. But if He were to punish them, they would deserve the punishment, and with this the difficulty in this hadith is removed.

* Student: In the verse we mentioned here that fisq is applied to disbelief in some of the benefits, and that disbelief is applied to fisq.

* The Shaykh: And the question?

* The student: The question is the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, those are the disbelievers﴾ [al-Ma'idah 44]. Is this merely a change of wording?

* The Shaykh: A change of wording. And where are the wordings?

* Student: In the verse after it: ﴿Those are the defiantly disobedient﴾ [al-Ma'idah 47].

* The Shaykh: ﴿Those are the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Ma'idah 45]. The wrongdoers, then the defiantly disobedient. Yes. And what is the difficulty? Some of them say that this is revealed in terms of states. Whoever is a ruler by other than what Allah revealed is a disbeliever. Whoever judges by other than what Allah revealed out of love for transgression and wrongdoing and oppression of people is a wrongdoer. And whoever judges by other than what Allah revealed not rejecting the ruling of Allah, but because his own self desires it, this is defiantly disobedient.

We illustrate this with three rulers. A ruler who judged by a law and rejected the ruling of Allah, and said: "We do not accept it," this is a disbeliever. The second had something against a particular person and ruled against him, excluding his opponent. We describe this one as a wrongdoer. The third judged by other than what Allah revealed, not rejecting what Allah revealed and not intending injustice, but his self desires it. Meaning, he ruled for a person that he owns a certain land, and there was no injustice in it, but his self desired it, either because of friendship with him, or kinship with him, or because he says: "The land is between me and him." This we say is defiant disobedience. So we apply these according to states.

Others said: they apply in one state only, and that the disbeliever is defiantly disobedient and a wrongdoer, as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And the disbelievers are the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Baqarah 254].

The closer view to me is that they apply according to states, because if we said these descriptions refer to one subject, they would become nearly repetitive.

* Student: May Allah reward you well, Shaykh. Those who cite evidence in this issue, I mean the issue of whether deeds enter faith, do we say that they have some resemblance to the Kharijites?

Shaykh: In truth, their line of argument here has no basis. If they applied to the rulings of the Sharia the same method they apply to the Names and Attributes of Allah, (we would say:) what Allah affirmed for Himself we affirm, and what He negated from Himself we negate. Here we say: whoever Allah has declared a disbeliever (kafir), we declare him a disbeliever, and whoever He has not declared a disbeliever, we do not declare him a disbeliever. Nor have people gone so far as this interpretation: this is a disbelief that expels one from the religion (kufr mukhrij 'an al-milla), while another group says it is not expelling, to the point that some of them denied what was reported from Ibn 'Abbas: "Kufr duna kufr" (lesser disbelief) [[Narrated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (3258), from a hadith of Abdullah ibn Abbas.]], and said: "This report is not authentic." One of our students verified it and said that it is authentic, and all the scholars transmit from Ibn 'Abbas, acknowledging it; it is well known from him.

I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Say: I do not tell you that with me are the treasuries of Allah﴾ [al-An'am 50]. The address here is to the Prophet (ﷺ), and it is a command from Allah to him, that is, to the Prophet (ﷺ). This is a command for a specific delivery; otherwise, the Prophet (ﷺ) was commanded to convey the entire Qur'an. However, some rulings are introduced with "Say," to indicate their importance, such as His saying: ﴿Say to the believing men that they lower their gaze﴾ [an-Nur 30], ﴿And say to the believing women that they lower their gaze﴾ [an-Nur 31], and ﴿Say to My servants who have believed that they establish prayer﴾ [Ibrahim 31]. Examples of this are numerous.

Therefore, in this ruling there is a specific charge to convey it to them; otherwise, the Prophet (ﷺ) was commanded to convey the entire Qur'an, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So that you may make clear to the people what has been sent down to them﴾ [an-Nahl 44].

﴿Say: I do not tell you﴾. The address in His saying ﴿you﴾ is to the polytheists who denied the Prophet (ﷺ).

﴿With me are the treasuries of Allah﴾ is the content of the statement. That is, "I do not say: with me are the treasures of Allah," meaning the treasuries of His provision, so that I provide for you and deprive whom I will.

﴿Nor do I know the unseen﴾ [al-An'am 50], meaning: nor do I tell you that I know the unseen. The unseen (al-ghayb) is that which is hidden, and it is of two kinds:

Relative unseen (ghayb nisbi): this may be known. For example, there are people in the market whom I do not know, but whoever sees them knows them. This is relative unseen.

Absolute, true unseen (ghayb mutlaq haqiqi): this is what is hidden from all people. No one knows it, such as knowing what will happen in the future. No one can know this, not the Messenger (ﷺ) nor anyone else. ﴿Nor do I know the unseen﴾.

So, the unseen is everything that is hidden, and it is of two types: relative and true. The relative is what is hidden from some people but not others, and the true is what is hidden from all people. The Prophet (ﷺ) does not know the unseen, neither the relative nor the true. But in the relative, whoever witnesses it knows it.

For this reason, when Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) slipped away from him while he was in a state of janabah, the Prophet (ﷺ) asked him: "Where were you?" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (283) and Muslim (371), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah]. So he did not know. Likewise, when he entered his house and asked for food, and they brought him dates, and he asked for meat, he said: "Did I not see the cooking pot on the fire?" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5097) and Muslim (1504/14), from the hadith of 'A'ishah]. Here he did not state with certainty that there was meat in it, although it was in his house, because the Prophet (ﷺ) does not know the unseen.

﴿Nor do I tell you that I am an angel﴾ [al-An'am 50]. He addressed them with a different form of address, meaning he repeated the address, because the context here, which is the negation of being an angel, is more eloquent and emphatic: ﴿Nor do I tell you that I am an angel﴾. The use of the second-person pronoun (kaf al-khitab) indicates the intensity of directing the address to the one addressed. For this reason, read in Surah al-Kahf the words of al-Khidr to Musa. In the first, he said: ﴿He said: Did I not say that you would not be able to have patience with me?﴾ [al-Kahf 72], and in the second he said: ﴿He said: Did I not say to you that you would not be able to have patience with me?﴾ [al-Kahf 75].

﴿Nor do I tell you that I am an angel﴾: "malak" is the singular of "malā'ikah" (angels). So he is a human being from the children of Adam. Then Allah the Exalted mentioned his function, which he states, saying: ﴿I only follow what is revealed to me﴾ [al-An'am 50]. "In" (إن) here means "ma" (what), so it is negating. "In" in the Arabic language has several meanings depending on context. It may be negating, as in: "In" (if) you strive, you succeed, and it may be conditional. It may be a lightened form of the heavy particle, as in: ﴿And indeed, they were before that in clear error﴾ [Al 'Imran 164], meaning: indeed they were. It may be superfluous, having no meaning except emphasis, as in the words of the poet:

"Banu Ghudanah, you are not gold, nor silver, but you are clay."

Sarif means silver. The evidence is in his saying "ma in antum dhahab" (you are not gold), where "in" is superfluous. For this reason, if the poet had said "ma antum dhahaban" it would be correct. What determines these meanings? It is the context. This shows that the meaning of words is determined by context. This supports the view of Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah (may Allah have mercy on him) that there is no majaz (figurative usage) in the language, because the meaning of a word is determined by its context, even if it is used in another meaning in a different context. So what determines it is context, and likewise, the meaning is determined by the situational indicator (al-qarinah al-hāliyyah), because context is a verbal indicator. The situational indicator is that the state of those spoken about indicates the meaning, such as his saying:

"........................ and indeed Malik was of noble origins."

Here it cannot be negating, because he was boasting about his people, so it must be a lightened form of the heavy particle.

﴿In I follow﴾, meaning: I do not follow ﴿except what is revealed to me﴾, meaning: except what Allah has revealed to me. Revelation (wahy) is Allah, may He be blessed and exalted, informing one of His prophets about the law. This is revelation, and it is called so from "iha'," which means secrecy and concealment, because revelation occurs in a hidden way, and not everyone knows about it.

His saying ﴿except what is revealed to me﴾ does not specify the One who reveals, because it is known, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And if I am guided, it is by what my Lord reveals to me﴾ [Saba' 50]. The One who reveals is Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

﴿Except what is revealed to me﴾: this is the function of the Prophet (ﷺ), and this is not specific to him, nor does it come from him.

﴿Say﴾, meaning: O Muhammad, after this has been made clear.

﴿Are the blind and the seeing equal?﴾ "Hal" here means "ma" (not), and the interrogative particle came with the meaning of negation, because it carries the meaning of challenge. It means: the blind and the seeing are not equal, and if you are truthful, then show me.

﴿The blind﴾ is an adjective of resemblance (sifah mushabbahah). ﴿The seeing﴾ is one who sees. It is well known that no one says that the blind and the seeing are equal, so what is meant by the blind here, and what is meant by the seeing? The blind refers to the disbeliever, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Deaf, dumb, and blind, so they do not return﴾ [al-Baqarah 18]. The seeing refers to the believer, seeing in the sense of insight (basirah) and seeing in the sense of sight (basar).

﴿Then will you not reflect?﴾ [al-An'am 50]. The interrogation here is for rebuke, meaning: after all this, will you turn away and not reflect?!

* In this verse there are great benefits, among them: it is obligatory upon the Prophet (ﷺ) to announce to the nation what Allah has commanded him: ﴿I do not tell you that with me are the treasuries of Allah, nor do I know the unseen, nor do I tell you that I am an angel. I only follow what is revealed to me﴾.

* Among them: that what is introduced with "Say" in regard to the Messenger (ﷺ) is evidence of its importance, and that Allah the Exalted commanded His Prophet to convey it specifically, which indicates care for it.

* Among the benefits of this verse: the Prophet (ﷺ) does not possess the treasuries of Allah, meaning the treasuries of provision. For this reason, the Prophet (ﷺ) lived for two or three months without fire being lit in his house [Narrated by Ahmad (9249) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah]. If he had the treasuries of Allah, he would have obtained them. Although if he had wished, he could have asked his Lord to fulfill what he desired, but he (ﷺ) was given the choice between being a servant and a prophet, or a king and a prophet, and he chose to be a servant and a prophet [Narrated by al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra (6710) from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: if the Prophet (ﷺ) does not possess the treasuries of Allah, then it is not permissible to ask provision directly from the Messenger, because if provision were requested directly from the Messenger, that would be shirk (polytheism) and an overstepping of what he is. As for asking him during his lifetime, it has details which this is not the place to mention. He may give and he may not give, as he refused the Ash'aris when they asked for mounts to fight upon. He said: "I cannot find anything to carry you on" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3133) and Muslim (1649/9), from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, with the wording: "By Allah, I will not carry you, and I do not have anything to carry you on"].

* Among the benefits of this verse: the Prophet (ﷺ) does not know the unseen, because of His saying: ﴿Nor do I know the unseen﴾.

If someone says: Does the Prophet (ﷺ) not speak about future matters?

The answer: Yes, but by revelation from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and Allah, may He be blessed and exalted, knows the unseen. For this reason, we say: everything the Prophet (ﷺ) informed of concerning future matters is by a special revelation from Allah, Mighty and Majestic. In that case, what he informed of regarding the unseen does not contradict what Allah mentioned in this verse: ﴿Nor do I know the unseen﴾, because his knowledge of the future through what Allah revealed to him is not knowledge he attained on his own, but knowledge from Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Just as a person sees a righteous dream during sleep and benefits from it in the future, and "the righteous dream is one part of forty-six parts of prophethood" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6989) and Muslim (2263/8), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah].

* Among the benefits of this verse: a clear refutation of those who said that the Prophet (ﷺ) knows the unseen, and then they confused and made analogies with what he informed of the hidden matters that Allah revealed to him. It is said: the principle is that he does not know the unseen, and when something is narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) about the future, we know that it is by a special revelation from Allah, may He be blessed and exalted.

* Among the benefits of this verse: the Prophet (ﷺ) is a human being like others. He does not know the unseen, and he forgets as we forget, and he feels hunger and thirst, cold and heat. All human characteristics apply to the Prophet (ﷺ).

* Among the benefits of this verse: an angel may appear in the form of a human being, because of His saying: ﴿Nor do I tell you that I am an angel﴾. If it were not possible for him to appear in human form, there would be no need for negation, since it would be known without negation. This is the reality, and Jibril (peace be upon him) came in the form of a man.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: a refutation of those who said: ﴿Why was an angel not sent down to him?﴾ [al-An'am 8], and said: Why were angels not sent down? The angels cannot descend to be messengers to humans, as the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And if We had made him an angel, We would have made him a man, and We would have covered for them what they cover﴾ [al-An'am 9].

* Among the benefits of the verse: the perfection of the Prophet's (ﷺ) servitude to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, because of His saying: ﴿I only follow what is revealed to me﴾, neither adding nor subtracting. Even if what was sent down to him concerned his own person (peace be upon him), he could not leave it. Consider the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And when you said to him on whom Allah bestowed favor and you bestowed favor: Keep your wife and fear Allah, while you concealed within yourself what Allah was to disclose, and you feared the people, while Allah has more right that you fear Him﴾ [al-Ahzab 37]. These are great words which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, addressed to His Prophet (ﷺ). If he had concealed anything of what Allah revealed to him, he would have concealed this, because it is a great matter, or like His saying: ﴿O Prophet, fear Allah and do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites﴾ [al-Ahzab 1].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the laws are determined by revelation (tawqifi), and it is not permissible for anyone to innovate anything from them. Like His saying: ﴿I only follow what is revealed to me﴾. For this reason, the people of knowledge established that the principle in acts of worship is prohibition and restriction, and that it is not permissible for a person to worship Allah with anything except what Allah has legislated. This truth is supported by multiple verses and by the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever introduces into this matter of ours something that is not part of it, it is rejected" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2697) and Muslim (1718/17), from the hadith of 'A'ishah].

Would it be good if someone considered something good and worshipped Allah with it? It would never be good. With this, the division of innovation (bid'ah) into two types, misguidance and good, or into five types, is invalidated, because this is undoubtedly false. The most knowledgeable of creation regarding the law of Allah, the most eloquent, and the most sincere of creation is Muhammad (ﷺ), who said: "Every innovation is misguidance" [Narrated by Muslim (867/43), from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah]. "Every" (kull) is in the form of generality, which is the most general of general expressions. The most general form of generality is "kull": "Every innovation is misguidance," and this firm generality does not admit any exception.

Nor is this refuted by what was established from Amir al-Mu'minin 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), when he gathered the people in Ramadan behind Ubayy ibn Ka'b and Tamim al-Dari. The people, after the Prophet (ﷺ) had refrained from establishing the Ramadan night prayer in congregation for them, had begun praying individually, or a man with another, or a man with two, and similar arrangements, causing confusion. 'Umar went out one night while they were in this state, and commanded Ubayy ibn Ka'b and Tamim al-Dari to lead the people in eleven rak'ahs. They did so, and they led the people in eleven rak'ahs. Then he went out again and saw them in this condition, and said: "What an excellent innovation this is" [Narrated by al-Bukhari (2010), and Malik in al-Muwatta' (301), and the wording is his, from the hadith of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab]. So he called it an innovation and praised it. Do you understand? All the people of innovation have used this report to justify their innovations, and we respond to them with two matters:

The first matter: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) is one of the rightly guided caliphs, whose innovation, if it became an innovation, what is it? It is a sunnah. So are you, O later generation, like 'Umar? No. Therefore, even if it were correct that it is a legislated innovation, 'Umar would be one to be followed, and his sunnah is to be followed by the command of the Prophet (ﷺ).

Second: it is a relative innovation (bid'ah nisbiyyah), considering that it had been abandoned from the time of the Messenger (peace be upon him) until 'Umar established it. This is a relative innovation. We cannot say it is a linguistic innovation (bid'ah lughawiyyah), because a linguistic innovation must be something without precedent. But we say it is a relative innovation, considering that it had been abandoned from the time of the Messenger (ﷺ), passing through the time of Abu Bakr, until the beginning of 'Umar's caliphate.

Third: this innovation has a basis, a basis and a sunnah. The Prophet (ﷺ) prayed with his companions in the Ramadan night prayer for three nights, and then abstained on the fourth. He said: "I feared that it would be made obligatory upon you, and you would be unable to maintain it" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2012) and Muslim (761/178), from the hadith of 'A'ishah]. Is this reason, which led the Prophet (ﷺ) to delay establishing it in congregation, still present in the time of 'Umar? The answer is no. The ruling revolves around its cause, and this cause could not exist in the time of 'Umar. Thus the clinging of the people of innovation to such a statement from Amir al-Mu'minin 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) is invalidated.

If someone says: Things were innovated that the Muslims approved, such as the compilation of the Qur'an into one codex, the arrangement of the hadiths into chapters, the building of schools, and many other things. What do you say about this?

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 6, verse 50 (part 2 of 2):

I say: This is not intended for its own sake, but for something else. The gathering of the people upon one mushaf (a single codified copy of the Qur'an) was so that the Ummah would not split apart. Had people been reading from the mushafs that existed after the Prophet (ﷺ), the Ummah would have been torn into great fragments, and the Christians would have said: "If we have four or five Gospels, you have dozens." Therefore, the unification of the mushaf was intended for something else, namely the unity of the Muslims' word and the avoidance of their disputes.

Likewise, the arrangement of hadiths by subject (tabwib) or their collection according to narrators (musnad collections) is also intended for something else, so that the fundamentals of the Sunnah (al-sunnah) may be easily accessible to the Muslims. Consider: if they had not been arranged by chapters or by musnads, a person who wished to know a ruling would have to read every hadith that came from the Prophet (ﷺ). The great hardship in this is not hidden, and in it is also the paralysis of the Shariah. So this was intended for something else.

Some people came and said: "The miḥrabs (prayer niches), these miḥrabs of the mosques, are an innovation (bid'ah) that you must demolish. If a person bequeathed that a mosque be built for him containing a miḥrab, the bequest would be void." Why? They said: "Because the Messenger (ﷺ) forbade them, warning: «Beware of the altars of the Christians» [[Narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf (4732), from the hadith of Musa al-Juhani.]], or words similar to it." So what is the answer?

The answer: First, the Prophet (ﷺ) restricted it when he said: "like the altars of the Christians." So if the miḥrab is not in the Christian form, there is no harm in it, if the hadith is authentic, although the hadith has been subject to criticism.

Second, we say: If it is established that these miḥrabs are not like the miḥrabs of the Christians, then the question remains: Is there a benefit in them or not?

The answer: There is a benefit in them. They serve in place of an entire row. If the mosque is narrow and the imam enters the miḥrab, it replaces an entire row, because the place where he would have stood without the miḥrab would be a full row. This is one benefit.

Second: they indicate the direction of the qiblah. For this reason the scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, said: "The direction of the qiblah is determined by Islamic miḥrabs." This is an observable matter. If mosques were like a closed room with nothing but four corners, people would not know the qiblah. Is this not clear? So there is a benefit in them. If there is a benefit in them, how can we say that they are a forbidden innovation that must be demolished?

If someone says: "It is possible to substitute them with coloring, or by placing tiles that differ from the tiles of the mosque," we say: What necessitates this for us? We say that there is another benefit in them, namely the widening of space for worshippers when the mosque is crowded.

It remains to be said that some people write on the miḥrab: ﴿Whenever Zachariah entered upon her the miḥrab﴾ [Ali 'Imran 37]. Look! I seek refuge in Allah. ﴿They distort the words from their places﴾ [al-Nisa' 46]. Is this the miḥrab in which Zachariah entered? No. Moreover, in the older language, miḥrab means a place of worship. This miḥrab is a place of worship, whether it is a niche, a room, or anything else. These people erred in two respects:

The first respect: The miḥrab in the verse does not mean the miḥrab of the qiblah. The second: Zachariah did not enter upon her the miḥrab; he did not enter upon Mary. Rather, this is flagrant ignorance. Such things must be traced by the Ministry of Islamic Affairs, Endowments, Call and Guidance, which must search out the mosques in which this has been written and erase it. How can the words of Allah be distorted at the qiblah of the Muslims? And praise be to Allah.

Must we hold that everything that happens has to have a witness in the Qur'an? Not at all, we are not obliged to that. What matters is that the noble verse commanded the Prophet (ﷺ) to say: ﴿I only follow what is revealed to me﴾.

* The student: May Allah be good to you. Regarding your reasoning in the matter of the miḥrab, this may open a wide door for the people of innovation.
* The Shaykh: And what is that?
* The student: It is the matter of benefits (maslahah). Most of the people of innovation now perform some innovations, saying: "There are benefits in them." For example, the Qur'an: they gather in a group to recite the Qur'an, and say to you: "I cannot recite alone." Likewise, dhikr: they say: "I cannot remember Allah alone." So the matter of benefits may open a wide door.
* The Shaykh: It depends. If the benefit is real, then it should be followed. But your performing an act of worship that the Messenger did not introduce and drawing near to Allah through it! We, for example, place miḥrabs not for the sake of drawing near through them as such, but because they are a sign of an intended legal matter.
* The student: O Shaykh, may Allah protect you, many mosques, especially in our lands, have nothing but a miḥrab above which is written, on the right (Allah) and on the left (Muhammad ﷺ). A question comes up about this. I heard that it is shirk, I heard it from you, O Shaykh, and the brothers there said: "We want a written fatwa so that we may rely on it."
* The Shaykh: The fatwa is now written with the brother.
* Another student: It has not reached us, O Shaykh.
* The Shaykh: It will reach you, God willing.
* The student: Very well, O Shaykh, regarding...
* The Shaykh: Suppose a person does not know Allah or Muhammad, but knows "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah," and in front of him is written on a level line: "Allah Muhammad." What does he understand? That they are equal. This is an error. And this is despite the fact that the original ruling is that it is an innovation. The early generations (al-salaf) did not do this. It is an innovation in itself.
* The student: We gave it to the Ministry, but they did not take up this task. They neglected this matter. Should we change it ourselves?
* The Shaykh: No, do not change it. These matters are the responsibility of officials. I myself do not issue a fatwa about them. For example, if a soldier came to me complaining about something enacted in a general way, I could not issue a fatwa to him, because that would open a door of evil and strife. I would say: Bring me an official letter from an official who is able to change it. And if it comes to us, it becomes obligatory upon the person to issue a fatwa according to what he sees.

This is a matter I hope you will pay attention to. You are students of knowledge, and God willing we hope for you a future full of benefits. If something comes to you from an individual under the umbrella of an administration, a ministry, or the like, do not issue a fatwa about it, because if you issue a fatwa about it, what happens? Strife. He himself may abandon this thing, and a question mark will be placed upon him, or he may gather people around him, and then they create strife. But say, praise be to Allah: "Ask the official above you to write to me an official letter, and then it will be obligatory upon me to act."

* Student: May Allah bless you. The one who claims knowledge of the relative unseen (al-ghayb al-nisbi): should we declare him a disbeliever? And the one who seeks help from the jinn, is he to be declared a disbeliever in major disbelief (kufr akbar)?
* The Shaykh: No, he is not declared a disbeliever in major disbelief. For example, if he has jinn who inform him of something distant, he is not declared a disbeliever. And how would he be declared one? What has he done that would make him a disbeliever?
* The student: But there is a fogged star-like thing, and he mutters.
* The Shaykh: Excellent. This is an incidental matter. We may prohibit it because it is incidental, but we do not say that it is shirk. If you review the words of Shaykh al-Islam (Ibn Taymiyyah), may Allah have mercy on him, in the fatawa, in Idah al-Dalalah 'ala 'Umum al-Risalah, and in Kitab al-Nubuwwat, and also a specific fatwa, you will understand the matter. The jinn may sometimes be benefited from in a permissible way in permissible matters.

* * *

I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Say: I do not tell you that with me are the treasuries of Allah, nor do I know the unseen, nor do I tell you that I am an angel. I only follow what is revealed to me﴾. What is meant by the treasuries of Allah?

* Student: Provision.
* The Shaykh: The treasuries of provision. His saying: ﴿nor do I know the unseen﴾ is conjoined with what?
* Student: "Say."
* The Shaykh: (...) The meaning is: nor do I say that I know the unseen. What is meant by the unseen here?
* Student: The true unseen.
* The Shaykh: And what is the meaning of "true"?
* The student: It is the future, and likewise what is absent from us.
* The Shaykh: Perhaps you have forgotten.
* Student: That which no one knows except Allah.
* The Shaykh: Precisely, that which no one knows. What is the relative unseen?
* Student: Some of it.
* The Shaykh: It is known to some and not to others. Excellent, correct. Is the negation here for both meanings or for the first?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: For both. That is, what is absent from the Prophet (ﷺ), even if it is witnessed by others, he does not know. And in this there is a refutation of a group who exaggerated regarding the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), claiming he knows the unseen.
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Excellent. And from this is the saying of al-Busiri:
......................... ∗∗∗ and of your knowledge ...............
* Student: The Preserved Tablet and the Pen.
* The Shaykh: Correct. ﴿Nor do I tell you that I am an angel﴾. The "malak" (angel) is what?
* Student: One of the angels.
* The Shaykh: And who are the angels?
* The student: An unseen creation who do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and do what they are commanded.
* The Shaykh: Allah created them for His worship. What is the meaning of His saying: ﴿I only follow what is revealed to me﴾? Is the intended meaning: of the acts of worship, or of the knowledge?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: That is, I do not know the unseen, and I do not follow except what Allah has revealed to me, and likewise I do not worship Him except by what He has revealed to me.

* From the benefits of this noble verse: the perfection of the Prophet's (ﷺ) devotion to Allah, by His saying: ﴿I only follow what is revealed to me﴾.
* And from it: the affirmation of Allah's revelation to him, by His saying: ﴿except what is revealed to me﴾. The types of revelation are mentioned in the saying of the Exalted: ﴿It is not for a human that Allah should speak to him except by revelation, or from behind a veil, or that He sends a messenger and he reveals by His permission what He wills﴾ [al-Shura 51].
* And from the benefits of this noble verse: the blind and the seeing are not equal, and they cannot be equal, by His saying: ﴿Say: Are they equal?﴾. Its basis is that the interrogative here means negation, and the interrogative in the sense of negation implies or carries the meaning of challenge.
* And from it: just as the blind and the seeing are not equal in the sensory sense, the blind and the seeing are not equal in meaning either, is that not so? The blind and the seeing are not equal in meaning: the ignorant is blind and the knowledgeable is seeing.
* And from the benefits of the noble verse: the exhortation to reflection, by His saying: ﴿Will you not then reflect?﴾.
* And from it: the reproach of the one who does not reflect, since the interrogative here is for reproach. But reflection on what? Reflection on matters as they actually are. One should not imagine things that have no connection to reality, nor reflect on things he cannot reach. So if anyone wished to reflect on the essence of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, it is not permissible; it is forbidden, because it cannot be reached. And if he wished to reflect on the manner of Allah's descent to the lowest heaven, it is not permissible, because that cannot be reached. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Vision does not perceive Him, but He perceives vision﴾ [al-An'am 103]. If sight, which perceives things by sensory perception, cannot perceive Allah, Mighty and Majestic, then reflection is all the more so.

So what should we reflect upon? We reflect on existing matters, on the cosmic and legislative signs of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. The cosmic signs are the creatures, and the great wisdoms and secrets that Allah has perfected in them. The legislative signs are the legal rulings that Allah has prescribed for the servants, and made suitable for every time and every place. That is, when the Shariah is applied, it is suitable for every time and every place; it cannot be destroyed.

Here we pause to mention those who used this phrase as a means to adapt the Shariah to reality. This is a grave error. What is obligatory is to adapt reality to the Shariah, and when reality is adapted to the Shariah, affairs become righteous. As for adapting the Shariah to reality, so that there is a Shariah for every era, or a Shariah for every place, or a Shariah for every nation, this means that the Shariah is changed, altered, and entered by whims, and this is impossible. So, then, reflection on the cosmic and legislative signs of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Likewise, reflect on His names and attributes: reflect on what the name indicates of the attribute, whether the indication is by inclusion (tadammun), by correspondence (mutabaqah), or by implication (iltizam).

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And warn thereby those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord﴾ [al-An'am 51]. "Warn thereby" means: with the Qur'an. Al-Indhar (warning) is informing someone of a matter in a manner that instills fear.

﴿Those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord﴾ means: those who believe in the Resurrection and fear the Day on which they will be raised, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said about the righteous: ﴿And they fear a Day whose evil will be widespread﴾ [al-Insan 7].

﴿They will have no protector or intercessor besides Him﴾ [al-An'am 51]: that is, none will take charge of them besides Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and none will intercede for them besides Allah. A wali (protector) is one who takes charge of their affairs, meaning he removes harm from them or brings benefit to them. A shafa'ah (intercession) is to mediate on someone's behalf before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, because intercession is mediating for another in order to bring about a benefit or repel a harm; this is what intercession is. So the intercession of the Prophet ﷺ for the people of the Standing (on the Day of Judgment), that judgment be passed between them, which of the two types is it? Is it the repelling of harm or the attainment of benefit? It is the repelling of harm, because people will suffer from distress and anguish beyond what they can bear. And his intercession for the people of Paradise, that they enter Paradise, which of the two types is it? It is the attainment of benefit.

In practice, for example, if a person interceded with a manager on behalf of someone to have him employed in his workplace, what is this? This is the attainment of benefit. And if he interceded on behalf of someone with a manager so that a discretionary punishment be lifted from him, whether by money or by imprisonment, this is the repelling of harm. Those whom Allah commanded the Prophet ﷺ to warn with the Qur'an, we say: they have no protector or intercessor besides Him.

﴿And warn thereby those who﴾ ﴿have no protector or intercessor besides Him, that they may perhaps fear Allah﴾ [al-An'am 51]. "La'alla" (perhaps/that they may) indicates a reason: that is, in order that they may be God-fearing. And whom do they fear? They fear Allah, Mighty and Majestic, or they fear the Day on which they will be gathered to Allah, and these two are interrelated.

Taqwa (God-consciousness) is derived from waqayah (protection), and it recurs frequently in the Noble Qur'an. Its meaning is to take a protection from the punishment of Allah by carrying out His commands, avoiding His prohibitions, and affirming His reports with knowledge and insight.

Some have said: taqwa is that you act in obedience to Allah, upon a light from Allah, hoping for the reward of Allah, and that you abandon what Allah has forbidden, upon a light from Allah, fearing the punishment of Allah.

Some of them expressed taqwa in verses:

Leave sins, both small and great, that is taqwa.
Walk as one who treads on thorny ground, wary of what he sees.
Do not belittle any small sin, for mountains are made of pebbles.

﴿That they may perhaps fear Allah﴾

In this noble verse there are benefits:

* The obligation of warning with the Qur'an.

* From this follows that the best thing with which to warn is the Qur'an, for it is the most eloquent of admonitions in warning, but, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿For whoever has a heart, or gives ear while he is a witness﴾ [Qaf 37].

* Among the benefits: only those who believe in the Last Day benefit from warning with the Qur'an, based on His saying: ﴿Warn thereby those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord﴾.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of the gathering to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, which will be on the Day of Resurrection, when creation is gathered to its Lord, Mighty and Majestic, to judge between them with a judgment that revolves between justice and grace: justice for whom? For the disbelievers, and grace for the believers.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: no one can prevent [anything] from Allah, based on His saying: ﴿They will have no protector or intercessor besides Him﴾.

* Among its benefits: the affirmation of intercession, for if it did not exist, its negation would not be valid. Intercession is of several kinds:

The Great Intercession (al-shafa'ah al-'uzma) for judgment to be passed among people; this is specific to the Messenger ﷺ. The Possessors of Resolve (ulu al-'azm) will excuse themselves from it, and it will be established for the Messenger ﷺ, and none of the sects of the community (millah) deny it; they all affirm it.

The second type: intercession for the people of major sins among the believers that they be brought out of the Fire. This is disputed by two sects of the community according to their affiliation: the Khawarij and the Mu'tazilah, because these two sects hold that the perpetrator of a major sin is abiding forever in the Fire, -we seek refuge with Allah- and if Allah has decreed that he be abiding in the Fire, then intercession will not benefit him.

There are other kinds of intercession, but this is not the place to mention them.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of causes and means, based on His saying: ﴿that they may perhaps fear Allah﴾. We have explained this matter at length, so there is no need to repeat it, and every person knows that affairs have causes and reasons.

Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening, seeking His Face. Nothing of their account falls upon you, and nothing of your account falls upon them, that you should drive them away and thereby be among the wrongdoers.﴾ [al-An'am 52]. This verse requires grammatical analysis.

As for His saying ﴿لَا تَطْرُدِ الَّذِينَ﴾ (do not drive away those who): ﴿لَا﴾ is a prohibitive particle, and the verb after it is jussive (majzum) by it, but it was given a kasra vowel because of the meeting of two sukun (iltiqa' al-sakinayn).

The second: His saying ﴿مَا عَلَيْكَ مِنْ حِسَابِهِمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ وَمَا مِنْ حِسَابِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ﴾. In it, ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ is the subject (mubtada'), but the superfluous preposition (harf al-jarr al-za'id) has entered upon it, so it is governed in form (lafzan) but not in position (mahallan).

For this reason, we parse ﴿مِنْ﴾ as a superfluous preposition, and ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ as the subject.

﴿فَتَطْرُدَهُمْ﴾: the fa' is of causation (li'l-sababiyyah), and the verb after it is in the subjunctive by it (according to the view of the Kufans), and by an implied (an) after it (according to the view of the Basrans). But is it a response (jawab) to a prohibition or to a negation? Because a negation and a prohibition have now preceded: ﴿لَا تَطْرُدِ﴾ is a prohibition, and ﴿مَا عَلَيْكَ﴾ is a negation. Is it a response to the negation or to the prohibition? To the negation: meaning, "Nothing of their account falls upon you, nor of your account upon them, [so] that you should drive them away." Why would you drive them away?

﴿فَتَكُونَ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾: the fa' is of causation, and ﴿تَكُونَ﴾ is a present-tense verb in the subjunctive by (an) after the fa' of causation, according to whom? The Basrans; or by it (the fa' itself), according to the Kufans. But it is a response to what? To His saying ﴿لَا تَطْرُدِ﴾, meaning: do not drive them away, lest you be among the wrongdoers.

Returning to the meanings: ﴿لَا تَطْرُدِ﴾. Al-tard (driving away) means distancing, i.e., do not distance them.

﴿الَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهُمْ بِالْغَدَاةِ وَالْعَشِيِّ﴾: ﴿يَدْعُونَ﴾ may be supplication of request (du'a' al-mas'alah) or supplication of worship (du'a' al-'ibadah). Supplication of request is that they say, "O our Lord, forgive us." Supplication of worship is that they perform the worship of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, such as prayer and other acts.

If someone asks: what is the basis for considering the worshipper to be one who makes supplication?

The answer: it rests on textual (athari) and rational (nazari) evidence. As for the textual evidence, it is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَقَالَ رَبُّكُمُ ادْعُونِي أَسْتَجِبْ لَكُمْ إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ عَنْ عِبَادَتِي سَيَدْخُلُونَ جَهَنَّمَ دَاخِرِينَ﴾ [Ghafir 60]. So Allah made supplication to be worship. As for worship being supplication, it is because if the worshipper were asked, "Why do you worship Allah?", he would say, "I hope for Allah's reward and fear His punishment." Thus it is supplication by the tongue of state (lisan al-hal), not by the tongue of speech (lisan al-maqal). Moreover, many acts of worship are not free of explicit supplication.

As for His saying ﴿بِالْغَدَاةِ وَالْعَشِيِّ﴾: the ba' here means "in" (fi), and the ba' often comes to mean "in," as in His saying: ﴿وَإِنَّكُمْ لَتَمُرُّونَ عَلَيْهِمْ مُصْبِحِينَ (137) وَبِاللَّيْلِ﴾ [al-Saffat 137-138], meaning "in" (fi).

Is there any wisdom in the ba' coming to mean "in"?

Know that the Noble Qur'an does not depart from what is linguistically familiar except for a reason. The reason here is that the ba' of place has been imbued with the meaning of comprehensiveness (istiy'ab), because the ba' also comes to express comprehensiveness, as in His saying: ﴿امْسَحُوا بِرُءُوسِكُمْ﴾ [al-Ma'idah 6], and as in His saying: ﴿وَلْيَطَّوَّفُوا بِالْبَيْتِ الْعَتِيقِ﴾ [al-Hajj 29]. The ba' is for comprehensiveness, meaning that they have fully occupied the morning and the evening with supplication. The ghadah is the beginning of the day, and the 'ashiyy is the end of the day.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿يُرِيدُونَ وَجْهَهُ﴾ is a circumstantial clause (hal) from the subject in ﴿يَدْعُونَ﴾, meaning that they are sincere to Allah, not intending by it showing off (riya') or reputation (sum'ah).

﴿مَا عَلَيْكَ مِنْ حِسَابِهِمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ وَمَا مِنْ حِسَابِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ﴾: meaning that your account is not upon them, and their account is not upon you. Since that is so, why would you drive them away? Let them attend gatherings from which they benefit and by which they benefit others. Nothing of their account falls upon you, nor of your account upon them, that you should drive them away. This is built upon His saying: ﴿مَا عَلَيْكَ مِنْ حِسَابِهِمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ وَمَا مِنْ حِسَابِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ﴾.

﴿فَتَكُونَ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾: in this expression there is gentleness in addressing the Prophet ﷺ, since He did not say "then you would be a wrongdoer," but said "among the wrongdoers." This carries a measure of consolation: that there are others who are wrongdoers, and the wrongdoers are many. It is well known that a person being with a group who share his description is easier than being alone in it.

﴿فَتَكُونَ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾

* In this noble verse there are benefits, among them: the prohibition of driving away righteous believers.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: praise of those people who attend the sessions of the Prophet ﷺ, by what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, mentioned: that they call upon Allah in the morning and the evening with sincerity to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

* Among its benefits: the affirmation of the Face of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; ﴿يُرِيدُونَ وَجْهَهُ﴾. The Face is an attribute of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, a real attribute, and we must believe in it, but in accordance with His saying: ﴿لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْبَصِيرُ﴾ [al-Shura 11]. As for whoever interprets it to mean the reward, he has erred, because that contradicts the apparent wording and contradicts the consensus of the early generations (salaf). Moreover, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said in the Qur'an: ﴿كُلُّ مَنْ عَلَيْهَا فَانٍ (26) وَيَبْقَى وَجْهُ رَبِّكَ ذُو الْجَلَالِ﴾ [al-Rahman 26-27]; He made it an attribute of the Face.

Could someone say that the reward is described as "Possessor of Majesty and Honour"?

The answer: No. Reflect on this together with His saying: ﴿تَبَارَكَ اسْمُ رَبِّكَ ذِي الْجَلَالِ وَالْإِكْرَامِ﴾ [al-Rahman 78], where He made it in the genitive as an attribute of "Lord" (rabb), not in the nominative as an attribute of the name, even though the names of Allah carry such majesty and exaltation as they do. But we ask Allah for well-being: ﴿وَمَنْ لَمْ يَجْعَلِ اللَّهُ لَهُ نُورًا فَمَا لَهُ مِنْ نُورٍ﴾ [al-Nur 40].

Glory be to Allah! I do not know what a person will encounter from his Lord on the Day of Resurrection if Allah, Exalted, has said: ﴿وَيَبْقَى وَجْهُ رَبِّكَ﴾ and said: ﴿يُرِيدُونَ وَجْهَهُ﴾, and similar verses, and then he says, "You have no face, O Lord; rather, what is meant by Your face is the reward." I do not know how a person can answer Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

The matter is not worldly disputation and worldly contention. It is a matter of creed that a person must prepare to answer for on the Day of Resurrection.
