A person may escape in this world through argument and contention, but it does not benefit him before Allah, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿هَاأَنْتُمْ هَؤُلاءِ جَادَلْتُمْ عَنْهُمْ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا فَمَنْ يُجَادِلُ اللَّهَ عَنْهُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ﴾ [al-Nisa' 109].

To these we say: if you prevail in argument in this world, will you prevail over Allah, Mighty and Majestic, on the Day of Resurrection? No, by Allah, they will not prevail over Him. The matter is grave. In my opinion, those who distort such verses, when they recite and distort them, forget that they will meet Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Otherwise, if they were mindful, they would not go about distorting words from their places in the greatest matters. If the verses and hadiths of legal rulings are taken according to their apparent meaning, and these are rulings where reason has some scope, then how are these great reports not taken according to their apparent meaning, when they concern whom? Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

* Among the benefits of this verse: that no one is held to account for another; ﴿مَا عَلَيْكَ مِنْ حِسَابِهِمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ وَمَا مِنْ حِسَابِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ﴾. This generality is restricted to the case where a person has not neglected his brother's right. If he neglects it, he is requited for that. For this reason the scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, said: it is obligatory upon a person who sees a sleeper when the time for prayer is running out to inform him, to wake him. Although the sleeper is excused and bears no sin, you, O wakeful one, must inform him, wake him and inform him. If you do not do so, his account will fall upon you. Strictly speaking, the one who is asleep is accountable for himself, but in reality it is your account, because you abandoned an obligation.

Likewise the scholars said: whoever sees a person about to perform ablution with impure water must, what? Inform him. And whoever sees an impure stain on his brother's garment must alert him to it, because of Allah's saying: ﴿وَتَعَاوَنُوا عَلَى الْبِرِّ وَالتَّقْوَى﴾ [al-Ma'idah 2].

* Among the benefits of this verse: the perfect justice of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for He addressed His Prophet with this strong address on account of some of his companions. He, peace and blessings be upon him, is greater in standing with Allah and higher in rank, yet Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is the Just Judge who decides with truth, Glorified and Exalted is He.

* Among the benefits of this verse: that withholding a person's right is an injustice, even if it is not aggression, such as by striking or taking property. But if he withholds his right, he is a wrongdoer, because of His saying: ﴿فَتَطْرُدَهُمْ فَتَكُونَ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾, and this is true. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ said: "The procrastination of the wealthy is injustice" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2288), and Muslim (1564/33), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah]. Although this person did not consume the poor man's property, for example, his procrastination, that is, withholding his right, makes him an wrongdoer toward him. So whoever withholds from the one who has a right his right is a wrongdoer toward him, just as if he had transgressed by taking something of his property.

Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And thus We tested some of them by means of others, that they might say: "Is it these whom Allah has favored among us?" Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾ [al-An'am 53]

"Thus We tested some of them by means of others": i.e., We misguided some of them by means of others. "That they might say: 'Is it these whom Allah has favored among us?'": meaning that the wealthy do not believe, and this is a trial. Why do they not believe? They say: "How can these people precede us to faith! We will not believe."

This is a trial that may befall a person: he says, "Something that so-and-so initiated, I will not take part in," for example, or "Something so-and-so did, I will not do." For this reason He said: ﴿That they might say: "Is it these whom Allah has favored among us?"﴾ The lam here (li) indicates consequence (al-'aqibah), not purpose (al-ta'lil). The meaning is: We tested some of them by means of others, so they said: ﴿Is it these whom Allah has favored among us?﴾ The interrogative here is for belittling, like His saying: ﴿And when they see you, they take you only in mockery, saying: "Is this the one whom Allah has sent as a messenger?"﴾ [al-Furqan 41].

So the meaning of His saying ﴿Is it these whom Allah has favored among us?﴾: the interrogative here is what? It is for belittling. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, responded to them: ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾, meaning: He knows that these people give thanks to Allah when Allah bestows favor upon them, whereas you do not. So this is a rebuttal to them.

* Among the benefits of this verse: Allah, glorified and exalted, tests some people by means of others, so that one misguides another because of the other. This is a reality. You find, for example, that a door of contribution to good is opened, and so-and-so and so-and-so and so-and-so precede, and others say: "Something that so-and-so has entered into, we do not agree with it nor desire it, and they cannot outdo us." Understood? This is a reality. The connection of this verse to the one before it is very clear, because those who came to the Messenger ﷺ and sat with him were poor, while the chieftains would not sit, because they despised these people and said: ﴿Is it these whom Allah has favored among us?﴾

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the disbelievers' acknowledgment that faith and Islam are a favor (minnah) from Allah, Exalted, by their saying: ﴿Is it these whom Allah has favored among us?﴾

* And among its benefits: that the enemies of the believers employ every method to repel people from the believers, by their saying ﴿Is it these whom Allah has favored among us?﴾ This is witnessed in everything. Did the enemies of the messengers, peace be upon them, mention descriptions that would repel people from them? Yes. Read the comprehensive, all-encompassing verse: ﴿Likewise, no messenger came to those before them except that they said: "A sorcerer or a madman." (52) Did they enjoin it upon one another? Rather, they are a transgressing people﴾ [al-Dhariyat 52, 53].

Likewise, the enemies of the advocates of ta'til (denial of divine attributes) from the people of the Sunnah and the Jama'ah are described by the advocates of ta'til with descriptions that repel people from them. They say: "This one is a mujassim (anthropomorphist), because he affirms the attributes," so they say: "This is tajsim," in order to repel people from him. And the people of kalam say: "These are hashwiyyah, they have no understanding, no meaning, and no intellect." Hashwiyyah means there is no good in them, and they call them nawabit, the plural of nabitah, which is the kind of growth that sprouts among crops, with leaves that bear no good.

In any case, nicknames of evil applied by people of evil to the people of good still exist. But does the person of good stand firm before these labels, or is he defeated? It is obligatory that he stand firm and not be defeated, for if he is defeated, it is not a defeat of his person, but a defeat of the truth he brought or that he adhered to.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of Allah's knowledge in His saying: ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾, that Allah knows who is grateful. And does the meaning refer to those who are grateful now, or those who will be grateful, or to all? To all. ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾ ("a'lam" is in the genitive, marked by a fatha. Why is it in the genitive marked by a fatha? Because it is descriptive of the pattern "af'al," but we say it follows the form of the verb, which is more general.) We will stop here.

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: Like that which occurred from those chieftains, and their contempt for those who attend the Prophet's ﷺ gatherings, a trial of that kind We inflicted.

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: No, it is not so in every case, but each place according to its context.

* Student: They say: (...) 'alim.

* Shaykh: This is from their ignorance. Which is more complete: "a'lam" or "'alim"? "A'lam" is a comparative (ism al-tafdil), and "'alim" is not a comparative; nothing prevents equality. ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾ [al-A'la 1]. Would one say: "Glorify the name of your Lord, the Lofty"?!

* Student: They do not say it.

* Shaykh: Even if they said it, they would be mistaken. ﴿Allah knows best where to place His message﴾ [al-An'am 124]. Would you say: "Allah is knowing"? Glory be to Allah! Allah describes Himself with the most complete description, and you bring Him down? If they say: when you say "a'lam," you are comparing Him with other knowers and preferring Him over them, I say: yes. And when you say "'alim," you describe Him with what others are described with, without preference. Observe how their distortion became a proof against them.

* Student: (...) a rule (dabit).

* Shaykh: Like His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who put the believing men and believing women to trial﴾ [al-Buruj 10].

* Student: The rule is the context?

* Shaykh: Yes, the context is what determines the meaning, and for this reason we said: there is no majaz (metaphor) in the language or in the Qur'an.

* Student: (...) in what is used?

* Shaykh: No. The intent is to establish what those people hold, that we say: the believer sees, and the disbeliever is blind. Are these two equal? They are not equal.

* Student: The blind is tested and..

* Shaykh: We said: it encompasses both matters, sensory and meaningful.

* Student: Seeking the connection (munasabah) between verses?

* Shaykh: There is no harm in it, but I have seen some authors in this field who labor enormously, and moreover it is not achievable in some cases. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Guard strictly the prayers, and the middle prayer, and stand before Allah in devotion. (238) And if you fear, then on foot or riding; but when you are safe, remember Allah as He taught you what you did not know﴾ [al-Baqarah 238, 239], followed by ﴿And those of you who die and leave wives﴾ [al-Baqarah 240]. What is the connection?

The point is that there is no doubt some verses have a clear connection, and some verses the connection is not known, which leads a person to submit completely to the arrangement of the verses, that it is tawqifi (divinely fixed), not rational. Some verses are close but not clearly connected.

* Student: The saying of Allah, Exalted: ﴿Indeed your Lord is most knowing of who strays from His way﴾ [al-An'am 117], what is the meaning?

* Shaykh: ﴿A'lam man yadillu﴾: here "a'lam" functions as a verb, meaning "knows who strays from His way." The comparative has acted in "man" now, so it is a direct object. Generally, as is known, it takes the preposition "bi" or "min."

* Student: May Allah reward you, O Shaykh (...).

* Shaykh: No, the address here is to the Prophet ﷺ, but if the Prophet ﷺ is addressed with such, then others are more deserving of it.

* Student: (...) and if it is not so, O Shaykh, what is the wisdom, O Shaykh, in mentioning the face always when expressing...?

* Shaykh: This is a good question. He says: in this verse there is an indication of the seeing of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, by His saying: ﴿Seeking His Face﴾. This is correct; it is fitting to make it among the evidences for affirming the vision of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, because the best and most delightful thing for the people of Paradise is to look upon the Face of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. O Allah, make us among those who look upon You.

For this reason, one must be wary of some clever authors. Al-Zamakhshari, author of al-Kashshaf, who was excellent in language and eloquence, and excellent in rhetoric and language, and everyone after him are dependents upon him, taking his statements. He said regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted: ﴿Whoever is spared from the Fire and admitted to Paradise has indeed succeeded﴾ [Al 'Imran 185]: "What success is greater than this?!" When you read it, you find nothing in it. But he intends to deny the vision of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, since the vision of Allah is greater than this success. But he was a clever man. He said: "What success is greater than this?" We say: greater than this is that a person sees his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, with a true vision.

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: Ta'zir (discretionary punishment)? If he interceded for you?

* Student: Yes.

* Shaykh: Yes.

* Student: What is the ruling on intercession?

* Shaykh: It is fine, but one does not intercede for you before the judge; one intercedes before the one who holds the right, saying: "O so-and-so, now you have obtained your right; pardon him." But in the case of the hudud (fixed punishments), intercession is not possible, because the Prophet ﷺ rebuked Usamah for it, saying: «Do you intercede concerning one of the hudud of Allah?»[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3475), and Muslim (1688/8), from the hadith of 'A'ishah.]]
